crawlability.noindex.title: Page is set to noindex
crawlability.noindex.why: A noindex directive removes the page from Google and Bing results, and AI search engines that rely on those indexes will not cite it. Fine on purpose, costly by accident.
crawlability.noindex.fix: Confirm the page should stay out of search. If it should be found, remove "noindex" from the robots meta tag (or the X-Robots-Tag header).

crawlability.noindex-header.title: Noindex sent in the X-Robots-Tag header
crawlability.noindex-header.why: A noindex in an HTTP header is invisible in the page source, so it often survives from staging or a CDN rule without anyone noticing.
crawlability.noindex-header.fix: Find the server, CDN or framework rule that adds "X-Robots-Tag: noindex" and limit it to the URLs that really should be hidden.

crawlability.robots-conflict.title: Conflicting robots directives
crawlability.robots-conflict.why: When the meta tag, the googlebot tag and the header disagree, Google applies the most restrictive rule, which is rarely what the person who added "index" intended.
crawlability.robots-conflict.fix: Set one clear directive per page. Remove the contradicting value from the meta robots tag, the googlebot meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header.

crawlability.noindex-canonical.title: Noindex combined with a canonical to another URL
crawlability.noindex-canonical.why: A canonical says "index that other URL instead" while noindex says "drop this". Google warns that mixing them sends conflicting signals and the noindex can be passed to the target.
crawlability.noindex-canonical.fix: Pick one: keep the canonical and remove noindex when the page is a duplicate, or keep noindex and make the canonical self-referencing (or remove it).

crawlability.nofollow-page.title: Indexable page tells crawlers not to follow its links
crawlability.nofollow-page.why: A page-level nofollow stops crawlers discovering and passing value through every link on the page, which starves the pages it links to.
crawlability.nofollow-page.fix: Remove "nofollow" from the robots meta tag. If only some links should not be followed, use rel="nofollow" on those links instead.

crawlability.snippet-restricted.title: Snippets restricted by nosnippet or max-snippet
crawlability.snippet-restricted.why: nosnippet and a small max-snippet limit what Google can show in results and stop the text being used in AI Overviews and AI Mode, which cuts the chance of being quoted.
crawlability.snippet-restricted.fix: Remove nosnippet, or raise max-snippet (use -1 for no limit) unless there is a legal reason to restrict snippets. Use data-nosnippet on specific passages instead.

crawlability.image-preview-restricted.title: Large image previews not allowed
crawlability.image-preview-restricted.why: Without max-image-preview:large, Google may show only a small thumbnail, which reduces visibility in Discover and image-rich results.
crawlability.image-preview-restricted.fix: Add "max-image-preview:large" to the robots meta tag on pages you want shown with a large image.

crawlability.unavailable-after-past.title: unavailable_after date has passed
crawlability.unavailable-after-past.why: After the unavailable_after date Google drops the page from results, which is easy to forget once the date is set.
crawlability.unavailable-after-past.fix: Remove the unavailable_after directive, or update the date if the page is meant to expire later.

crawlability.head-broken.title: Invalid element in <head> hides later SEO tags
crawlability.head-broken.why:
When a body element such as ,
or
crawlability.head-broken.fix: Move the stray element into <body> (often an injected tracking pixel or noscript fallback), or move the SEO tags above it.

crawlability.robots-meta-in-body.title: Robots meta tag placed in <body>
crawlability.robots-meta-in-body.why: Robots meta tags belong in <head>. Some crawlers ignore them in the body, so the directive may not be applied consistently.
crawlability.robots-meta-in-body.fix: Move the <meta name="robots"> tag into the <head> of the page template.

crawlability.blocked-but-linked.title: Internally linked URL is blocked by robots.txt
crawlability.blocked-but-linked.why: Blocked URLs cannot be crawled, yet internal links keep sending crawlers and link value to them. Google may still index the bare URL without its content.
crawlability.blocked-but-linked.fix: Either allow the URL in robots.txt (and use noindex if it should stay out of results) or stop linking to it internally.

crawlability.deep-page.title: Page is many clicks from the home page
crawlability.deep-page.why: Pages buried deep in the click path are crawled less often and look less important to search engines and AI crawlers.
crawlability.deep-page.fix: Link to the page from a hub, category or the main navigation so it is within three or four clicks of the home page.

crawlability.homepage-noindex.title: Home page is set to noindex
crawlability.homepage-noindex.why: A noindex home page usually means a staging setting reached production. The whole brand loses its main entry point in search and AI answers.
crawlability.homepage-noindex.fix: Remove noindex from the home page (meta robots and X-Robots-Tag). Check the CMS "discourage search engines" setting.

crawlability.noindex-linked.title: Noindex pages receive many internal links
crawlability.noindex-linked.why: Linking heavily to pages you keep out of search spends crawl effort and link value on them instead of on pages that can rank.
crawlability.noindex-linked.fix: Point navigation and in-content links at indexable pages. Keep links to noindex pages (login, cart, filters) to where users need them.

crawlability.crawl-incomplete.title: Crawl stopped at the page limit
crawlability.crawl-incomplete.why: The audit only covers the pages it reached. Site-wide findings such as orphans, duplicates and sitemap gaps may be incomplete.
crawlability.crawl-incomplete.fix: Raise the page limit (--max-pages) or crawl sections separately with include patterns.

crawlability.single-page-found.title: Crawler could not find links beyond the start page
crawlability.single-page-found.why: If a crawler following plain HTML links reaches only one page, search and AI crawlers that do not run JavaScript cannot discover the rest of the site either.
crawlability.single-page-found.fix: Render navigation as real <a href="…"> links in the server HTML. Avoid links that only exist after JavaScript runs or use onclick handlers.

crawlability.parameter-waste.title: Many indexable URLs with query parameters
crawlability.parameter-waste.why: Filters, sorts and session parameters can multiply one page into hundreds of crawlable URLs. Crawlers waste their visits on them and the duplicates dilute signals.
crawlability.parameter-waste.fix: Canonicalise parameter URLs to the clean URL, stop linking to sort/filter variants with plain links, and block pure-filter parameters in robots.txt where appropriate.

crawlability.low-indexable-share.title: Most crawled pages are not indexable
crawlability.low-indexable-share.why: When most internal links lead to redirects, errors, noindex or canonicalised pages, crawlers spend their time on URLs that can never rank.
crawlability.low-indexable-share.fix: Review the non-indexable URLs in the report and update internal links so they point straight at indexable, canonical pages.

crawlability.staging-indexable.title: Staging or development host is indexable
crawlability.staging-indexable.why: An indexable staging copy competes with the live site as a duplicate and can leak unfinished pages into search and AI answers.
crawlability.staging-indexable.fix: Protect staging with a password (best) or send "X-Robots-Tag: noindex" on every staging response.

crawlability.robots-txt-missing.title: No robots.txt file
crawlability.robots-txt-missing.why: Without robots.txt everything may be crawled, which is fine, but you lose the place to declare sitemaps and to steer crawlers away from low-value URLs.
crawlability.robots-txt-missing.fix: Add /robots.txt with at least "User-agent: *", an empty "Disallow:" (or the paths you want kept out) and a "Sitemap:" line.

crawlability.robots-txt-server-error.title: robots.txt returns a server error
crawlability.robots-txt-server-error.why: Google treats a 5xx robots.txt as "do not crawl anything" for a while and may then reduce crawling of the whole site.
crawlability.robots-txt-server-error.fix: Make /robots.txt return 200 (or 404 if you do not need one). Check the server, CDN and firewall rules for that path.

crawlability.robots-txt-unreachable.title: robots.txt could not be fetched
crawlability.robots-txt-unreachable.why: A timeout or connection error on robots.txt is treated like a server error: crawlers may pause crawling the site.
crawlability.robots-txt-unreachable.fix: Check DNS, TLS and firewall rules for /robots.txt and make sure it responds quickly to all user agents.

crawlability.robots-blocks-all.title: robots.txt blocks the whole site
crawlability.robots-blocks-all.why: "Disallow: /" for all crawlers or for Googlebot stops the site being crawled. Pages drop out of search and AI engines over time.
crawlability.robots-blocks-all.fix: Remove "Disallow: /" from the group that applies to "*" or Googlebot, unless the site is meant to be private.

crawlability.robots-blocks-home.title: Home page blocked by robots.txt
crawlability.robots-blocks-home.why: If Googlebot cannot fetch the home page, the most linked page on the site cannot be crawled and its content cannot be shown or cited.
crawlability.robots-blocks-home.fix: Adjust the robots.txt rule shown so it no longer matches "/". Use the "$" anchor for exact-path rules.

crawlability.robots-blocks-resources.title: robots.txt blocks CSS or JavaScript
crawlability.robots-blocks-resources.why: Google renders pages like a browser. If it cannot load the CSS and scripts, it may misjudge layout, mobile-friendliness and content added by JavaScript.
crawlability.robots-blocks-resources.fix: Allow the blocked asset paths (for example "Allow: /*.css$" and "Allow: /*.js$", or remove the Disallow for the asset folder).

crawlability.robots-blocks-linked-pages.title: robots.txt blocks pages linked from the home page
crawlability.robots-blocks-linked-pages.why: Pages linked from the home page are usually the ones you most want found. A broad Disallow rule often catches them by accident.
crawlability.robots-blocks-linked-pages.fix: Narrow the Disallow rules so they do not match these URLs, or remove the links if the pages are meant to be private.

crawlability.robots-no-sitemap.title: robots.txt does not list a sitemap
crawlability.robots-no-sitemap.why: The Sitemap line in robots.txt is how Bing, Google and many AI crawlers find your sitemap without a webmaster account.
crawlability.robots-no-sitemap.fix: Add a line such as "Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml" (absolute URL) to robots.txt.

crawlability.robots-sitemap-invalid.title: Sitemap line in robots.txt is not an absolute URL
crawlability.robots-sitemap-invalid.why: The Sitemap directive must be a full URL. Relative paths are ignored by Google and Bing.
crawlability.robots-sitemap-invalid.fix: Write the full URL, including https:// and the host, after "Sitemap:".

crawlability.robots-crawl-delay.title: High Crawl-delay in robots.txt
crawlability.robots-crawl-delay.why: Google ignores Crawl-delay, but Bing and several AI crawlers honour it. A long delay means new and updated pages are picked up slowly.
crawlability.robots-crawl-delay.fix: Lower or remove Crawl-delay. If the server struggles, fix capacity or caching rather than throttling crawlers (keep it under 10 seconds if you must keep it).

crawlability.robots-unsupported-rules.title: robots.txt uses rules Google does not support
crawlability.robots-unsupported-rules.why: Noindex, Nofollow and Host lines in robots.txt are ignored by Google (noindex support ended in 2019), so pages you think are hidden may still be indexed.
crawlability.robots-unsupported-rules.fix: Remove these lines and use a robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header for noindex, and redirects or canonicals instead of Host.

crawlability.robots-syntax.title: robots.txt has lines crawlers cannot parse
crawlability.robots-syntax.why: Typos such as "Dissallow" or a rule without a colon are skipped silently, so the rule you meant to apply does nothing.
crawlability.robots-syntax.fix: Correct the lines shown. Each rule must be "Field: value" using User-agent, Allow, Disallow, Sitemap or Crawl-delay.

crawlability.robots-too-large.title: robots.txt is larger than 500 KiB
crawlability.robots-too-large.why: Google stops reading robots.txt after 500 KiB. Rules after that point are ignored.
crawlability.robots-too-large.fix: Consolidate rules with wildcards and remove unused ones to bring the file well under 500 KiB.

crawlability.robots-is-html.title: robots.txt returns an HTML page
crawlability.robots-is-html.why: When /robots.txt serves an HTML page (often a 404 template with status 200), crawlers cannot read any rules or sitemap lines from it.
crawlability.robots-is-html.fix: Serve a plain-text robots.txt file, or return a real 404 status when there is none.

crawlability.gsc-impressions-not-crawled.title: Pages earning impressions were not found by the crawl
crawlability.gsc-impressions-not-crawled.why: Google shows these URLs in search, yet a crawl following your links did not reach them. They are probably orphaned, so they receive no internal link value and are easy to lose.
crawlability.gsc-impressions-not-crawled.fix: Link to these pages from relevant hubs or navigation, or redirect them if they are outdated.
crawlability.gsc-impressions-not-crawled.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-not-indexed.title: Google reports the page is not indexed
crawlability.gsc-not-indexed.why: URL Inspection says Google has not indexed this page, so it cannot appear in Search, AI Overviews or AI Mode.
crawlability.gsc-not-indexed.fix: Open the page in Search Console URL Inspection to see the reason. Fix blocking issues, improve the content, link to it internally and request indexing.
crawlability.gsc-not-indexed.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-crawled-not-indexed.title: Crawled but not indexed by Google
crawlability.gsc-crawled-not-indexed.why: Google fetched the page and chose not to index it. This is usually a quality or duplication judgement, not a technical block.
crawlability.gsc-crawled-not-indexed.fix: Make the page clearly useful and distinct: add original detail, merge it with a similar page, or link to it from stronger pages. Then request indexing.
crawlability.gsc-crawled-not-indexed.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-discovered-not-indexed.title: Discovered but not yet crawled by Google
crawlability.gsc-discovered-not-indexed.why: Google knows the URL but has not fetched it, often because the site has many low-value URLs or the page has weak internal links.
crawlability.gsc-discovered-not-indexed.fix: Add internal links to the page from well-linked pages, keep it in the sitemap with an accurate lastmod and reduce crawl waste elsewhere.
crawlability.gsc-discovered-not-indexed.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-canonical-mismatch.title: Google chose a different canonical
crawlability.gsc-canonical-mismatch.why: Google ignored the canonical you declared and indexes another URL instead, so the version you want may never be shown or cited.
crawlability.gsc-canonical-mismatch.fix: Make the signals agree: internal links, sitemap entries, redirects and the canonical tag should all point at the same URL. Remove near-duplicates.
crawlability.gsc-canonical-mismatch.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-noindex-with-impression.title: Noindex page still earning search impressions
crawlability.gsc-noindex-with-impression.why: The page is getting traffic from Google today but carries noindex, so it will drop out once Google recrawls it. Usually a recent accidental change.
crawlability.gsc-noindex-with-impression.fix: Check whether noindex was intended. If not, remove it before the page drops out of results.
crawlability.gsc-noindex-with-impression.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-low-ctr.title: High impressions, low click-through rate
crawlability.gsc-low-ctr.why: The page ranks well enough to be seen but few people click. The title or description probably does not match what searchers want.
crawlability.gsc-low-ctr.fix: Rewrite the title and meta description around the main queries for this page, state the answer or benefit plainly, and check for rich-result eligibility.
crawlability.gsc-low-ctr.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-striking-distance.title: Pages ranking just off page one
crawlability.gsc-striking-distance.why: Pages averaging positions 8 to 20 with real demand are the quickest wins: small improvements can move them onto page one, where most clicks and AI citations come from.
crawlability.gsc-striking-distance.fix: Strengthen these pages: answer the main query in the first paragraph, add missing subtopics, improve internal links from related pages and refresh dates.
crawlability.gsc-striking-distance.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-stale-crawl.title: Google has not crawled the page recently
crawlability.gsc-stale-crawl.why: A last crawl more than 90 days ago means updates to the page are not reflected in search or in AI answers built on the index.
crawlability.gsc-stale-crawl.fix: Link to the page from frequently updated pages, keep its sitemap lastmod accurate and make sure it returns 200 quickly.
crawlability.gsc-stale-crawl.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.gsc-no-impressions.title: Indexable pages with no search impressions
crawlability.gsc-no-impressions.why: Indexable pages that never appear in Search Console data are either not indexed or not relevant to any query. They add crawl load without return.
crawlability.gsc-no-impressions.fix: Review these pages: improve, merge or retire them. Check URL Inspection for the ones that should be indexed.
crawlability.gsc-no-impressions.skippedReason: Needs Google Search Console. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

crawlability.noindex-nofollow.title: Noindex page also blocks link following
crawlability.noindex-nofollow.why: A page kept out of the index can still help crawlers reach the pages it links to. "noindex, nofollow" (or "none") cuts those paths too, so pages linked mainly from it, such as filtered lists, tag pages or archives, are found later or not at all.
crawlability.noindex-nofollow.fix: Use "noindex, follow" unless you really want crawlers to ignore every link on the page. Remove nofollow from the robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag.

response.client-error.title: Internal URL returns a 4xx error
response.client-error.why: Links to missing pages waste crawl visits, lose the value of the links pointing at them and send visitors and AI agents to a dead end.
response.client-error.fix: Restore the page, 301-redirect the URL to its closest replacement, or update the links that point to it.

response.server-error.title: Internal URL returns a 5xx error
response.server-error.why: Server errors stop crawling. If they persist Google slows down crawling of the whole site and drops the failing pages.
response.server-error.fix: Check the server and application logs for this URL and fix the error. Return 503 with Retry-After only for planned maintenance.

response.forbidden.title: Crawler received 401 or 403
response.forbidden.why: A 401/403 on a public page usually means a firewall, bot protection or login rule blocks crawlers. Search and AI bots get the same answer.
response.forbidden.fix: If the page is public, allow verified search and AI crawlers through the WAF or bot rules. If it is private, stop linking to it from public pages.

response.rate-limited.title: Crawler was rate limited (429)
response.rate-limited.why: A 429 tells crawlers to slow down. Frequent 429s mean Googlebot and AI crawlers fetch fewer pages and pick up changes more slowly.
response.rate-limited.fix: Raise rate limits for verified crawlers, add caching, or send Retry-After so crawlers back off politely.

response.network-error.title: Request failed or timed out
response.network-error.why: Timeouts, DNS failures and dropped connections look like an unavailable site to every crawler.
response.network-error.fix: Check the server for slow or failing routes, TLS problems or a firewall dropping requests, then re-run the audit.

response.soft-404.title: Error page returned with status 200 (soft 404)
response.soft-404.why: A "not found" page that returns 200 gets crawled and possibly indexed as a real page. Google reports these as soft 404s and wastes crawl on them.
response.soft-404.fix: Return a real 404 (or 410) status for missing content, or redirect the URL to a relevant live page.

response.empty-body.title: HTML page with an empty body
response.empty-body.why: A 200 response with no content gives crawlers nothing to index and is often a sign of a failing template or cache.
response.empty-body.fix: Find why the server returns an empty response for this URL (application error swallowed, cache serving an empty object) and fix it.

response.content-type-missing.title: HTML served without a text/html content type
response.content-type-missing.why: Crawlers decide how to process a file from its Content-Type. HTML sent as text/plain or with no type may not be parsed as a web page.
response.content-type-missing.fix: Send "Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8" for HTML pages.

response.charset-missing.title: Character encoding not declared
response.charset-missing.why: Without a charset, browsers and crawlers may guess the wrong encoding and show garbled characters, especially for non-English text.
response.charset-missing.fix: Add <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first element in <head>, or send charset=utf-8 in the Content-Type header.

response.charset-late.title: Charset declared too late in the document
response.charset-late.why: The meta charset must appear within the first 1024 bytes. Later declarations can make the browser re-parse the page or decode it wrongly.
response.charset-late.fix: Move <meta charset="utf-8"> to be the first child of <head>.

response.homepage-error.title: Start URL does not return 200
response.homepage-error.why: If the home page fails, crawlers cannot reach anything else and AI agents treat the site as down.
response.homepage-error.fix: Make the home page return 200 for all user agents. Check firewall rules, redirects and server errors.

response.error-rate.title: High share of crawled URLs return errors
response.error-rate.why: When many internal URLs fail, crawlers lose trust in the site and reduce how often they visit.
response.error-rate.fix: Work through the 4xx and 5xx URLs in this report: fix, redirect or unlink them.

response.missing-page-returns-200.title: Non-existent URLs return 200
response.missing-page-returns-200.why: If any made-up URL returns 200, every broken link becomes an indexable duplicate (a site-wide soft 404) and crawlers cannot tell real pages from errors.
response.missing-page-returns-200.fix: Configure the server or framework to return a 404 status for unknown routes. Single-page apps need a server-side catch-all that sets the status.

response.missing-page-redirects.title: Non-existent URLs redirect to another page
response.missing-page-redirects.why: Redirecting every unknown URL (often to the home page) is treated as a soft 404 by Google and hides real broken links from you.
response.missing-page-redirects.fix: Let unknown URLs return 404 with a helpful error page. Redirect only URLs that have a genuine replacement.

response.404-page-unhelpful.title: 404 page offers no way forward
response.404-page-unhelpful.why: A bare 404 page with no links loses the visitor. A helpful one keeps people and agents on the site.
response.404-page-unhelpful.fix: Add a short message, a search box and links to the main sections on the 404 template. Keep the 404 status.

response.homepage-duplicates.title: Home page reachable at several URLs
response.homepage-duplicates.why: When /index.html, /index.php or /home also return 200 without a redirect or canonical, the home page is split across duplicate URLs.
response.homepage-duplicates.fix: Redirect these variants to the root URL with a 301, or at least add a canonical pointing to it.

redirects.chain.title: Redirect chain
redirects.chain.why: Each extra hop slows users and crawlers down. Googlebot follows up to 10 hops but other crawlers give up sooner, and link value can be lost along the way.
redirects.chain.fix: Point the first URL straight at the final destination and update internal links to the final URL.

redirects.loop.title: Redirect loop
redirects.loop.why: A loop never reaches a page. Browsers show an error and crawlers drop the URL.
redirects.loop.fix: Find the conflicting rules (often http/https or trailing-slash rules fighting each other) and make one of them stop redirecting.

redirects.temporary.title: Temporary redirect used
redirects.temporary.why: A 302 or 307 says the move is temporary, so search engines may keep the old URL indexed. Permanent moves should use 301 or 308.
redirects.temporary.fix: If the move is permanent, change the redirect to 301 (or 308).

redirects.to-error.title: Redirect ends at an error
redirects.to-error.why: A redirect to a missing or failing page is a broken link with an extra step. Users and crawlers end up nowhere.
redirects.to-error.fix: Point the redirect at a live, relevant page, or let the old URL return 404/410 if there is no replacement.

redirects.meta-refresh.title: Meta refresh or Refresh header redirect
redirects.meta-refresh.why: Refresh redirects are slow, confusing for screen-reader users and only treated as a weak signal by search engines. Many AI crawlers do not follow them.
redirects.meta-refresh.fix: Replace the meta refresh with a server-side 301 redirect.

redirects.javascript.title: Page appears to redirect with JavaScript
redirects.javascript.why: JavaScript redirects only work for crawlers that render pages. Most AI crawlers do not, and Google recommends server-side redirects.
redirects.javascript.fix: Use a server-side 301 redirect instead of changing window.location in a script.

redirects.https-to-http.title: Redirect downgrades from HTTPS to HTTP
redirects.https-to-http.why: A hop through HTTP exposes the request, triggers browser warnings and conflicts with HSTS. It also mixes protocol signals for search engines.
redirects.https-to-http.fix: Make every redirect target an https:// URL.

redirects.off-site.title: Internal URL redirects to another domain
redirects.off-site.why: An internal link that leaves the site is often a forgotten migration or a hijacked redirect. Link value leaves with it.
redirects.off-site.fix: Check the destination is intended. Link directly to the external URL, or update the link to an internal page.

redirects.linked-internally.title: Redirecting URL is still linked internally
redirects.linked-internally.why: Internal links to redirects add a hop to every visit and crawl. Linking straight to the final URL is faster and a clearer signal.
redirects.linked-internally.fix: Update the internal links to point at the final URL.

redirects.many-to-homepage.title: Many URLs redirect to the home page
redirects.many-to-homepage.why: Mass redirects to the home page are treated as soft 404s by Google, so the old URLs pass on nothing.
redirects.many-to-homepage.fix: Redirect each old URL to its closest matching page, or let it return 404/410.

redirects.http-not-redirected.title: HTTP version of the site does not redirect to HTTPS
redirects.http-not-redirected.why: If http:// pages return 200, there are two copies of the site, visitors can land on the insecure one and signals are split.
redirects.http-not-redirected.fix: Add a site-wide 301 redirect from http:// to https:// and enable HSTS.

redirects.http-temporary.title: HTTP to HTTPS redirect is temporary
redirects.http-temporary.why: A 302 from http to https tells search engines the http URL may come back, so they may keep it as the canonical.
redirects.http-temporary.fix: Use a 301 or 308 for the http to https redirect.

redirects.host-variants.title: Both www and non-www hosts serve the site
redirects.host-variants.why: If example.com and www.example.com both return pages, the site exists twice and search engines have to guess which one to use.
redirects.host-variants.fix: Choose one host and 301-redirect the other to it, keeping the path.

redirects.trailing-slash-duplicates.title: URLs work with and without a trailing slash
redirects.trailing-slash-duplicates.why: When /page and /page/ both return 200 without one pointing to the other, each page has a duplicate.
redirects.trailing-slash-duplicates.fix: Pick one style and 301-redirect the other, or make sure both carry the same canonical.

redirects.case-duplicates.title: Upper-case URL variants return 200
redirects.case-duplicates.why: URLs are case-sensitive. If /Page and /page both serve the same content without a redirect or canonical, each page can be duplicated many times.
redirects.case-duplicates.fix: Redirect mixed-case requests to the lower-case URL, or add a self-referencing canonical on every page.

response.doctype-missing.title: Missing or misplaced <!DOCTYPE html>
response.doctype-missing.why: Without <!DOCTYPE html> as the first thing in the document, browsers fall back to quirks mode: layout, box sizes and font sizes can differ from what you designed, which affects mobile usability and layout shift. Some parsers also misread the head.
response.doctype-missing.fix: Make <!DOCTYPE html> the very first line of every HTML response, before any whitespace-sensitive output, comments from plugins or <html>.

redirects.mixed-status.title: Same section redirects with both permanent and temporary codes
redirects.mixed-status.why: After a migration or URL change, redirects in one section are usually made by one rule. When some old URLs answer 301 and others 302, part of the mapping was set up differently (a plugin, a server rule, an old leftover), and the temporary ones may keep the old URLs in the index.
redirects.mixed-status.fix: Find the rule behind the temporary redirects in the listed sections and make every permanent move a 301 or 308, from one place.

onpage.title-missing.title: Missing or empty title
onpage.title-missing.why: The title is the main label for the page in search results, browser tabs and AI citations. Without one, engines invent a title from other text.
onpage.title-missing.fix: Add a unique, descriptive <title> in <head> that names the page topic first and the brand last.

onpage.title-multiple.title: More than one title element
onpage.title-multiple.why: Several <title> tags (often one from the theme and one from a plugin) make it unclear which one search engines should use.
onpage.title-multiple.fix: Remove the extra <title> so the page has exactly one, in <head>.

onpage.title-too-long.title: Title is likely to be cut off
onpage.title-too-long.why: Google shows roughly the first 60 characters (about 600 pixels). Longer titles are truncated or rewritten, so the end of the title is lost.
onpage.title-too-long.fix: Keep the title under about 60 characters with the most important words first.

onpage.title-too-short.title: Title is very short
onpage.title-too-short.why: A very short title rarely describes the page well enough to win the click or to tell an AI engine what the page covers.
onpage.title-too-short.fix: Expand the title to describe the page specifically, for example "Service in City | Brand".

onpage.title-generic.title: Generic or placeholder title
onpage.title-generic.why: Titles such as "Home", "Untitled" or "Just another WordPress site" say nothing about the page and are often rewritten by Google.
onpage.title-generic.fix: Replace it with a title that names what the page offers and who it is for.

onpage.title-repeated-words.title: Title repeats the same word
onpage.title-repeated-words.why: Repeating a keyword in the title reads as spammy, and Google rewrites keyword-stuffed titles.
onpage.title-repeated-words.fix: Use the main term once and describe the page in natural language.

onpage.title-all-caps.title: Title written in capitals
onpage.title-all-caps.why: All-caps titles are harder to read and look like shouting in results. Google may rewrite them.
onpage.title-all-caps.fix: Use sentence case or title case.

onpage.title-h1-mismatch.title: Title and H1 share no words
onpage.title-h1-mismatch.why: When the title and main heading describe different things, Google is more likely to rewrite the title and readers are less sure they landed in the right place.
onpage.title-h1-mismatch.fix: Make the title and H1 describe the same topic, even if worded differently.

onpage.title-duplicate.title: Duplicate titles
onpage.title-duplicate.why: Pages with the same title look like duplicates. Search engines struggle to pick which one to show and the pages compete with each other.
onpage.title-duplicate.fix: Give every indexable page a unique title that reflects its own content (include the page number or variant where relevant).

onpage.description-missing.title: Missing meta description
onpage.description-missing.why: Without a description, search engines pick a snippet from the page that may not sell the click. Many AI tools also read it as the page summary.
onpage.description-missing.fix: Write a unique meta description of about 120 to 160 characters that summarises the page and its main benefit.

onpage.description-multiple.title: More than one meta description
onpage.description-multiple.why: Duplicate description tags (often theme plus plugin) mean the one you edit may not be the one shown.
onpage.description-multiple.fix: Remove the extra tag so there is one meta description in <head>.

onpage.description-too-long.title: Meta description likely to be cut off
onpage.description-too-long.why: Snippets are trimmed to around 160 characters on desktop and less on mobile, so the end of a long description is lost.
onpage.description-too-long.fix: Keep the description under about 160 characters and put the key message first.

onpage.description-too-short.title: Meta description is very short
onpage.description-too-short.why: A very short description gives searchers and AI summaries little reason to choose the page and is often replaced by page text.
onpage.description-too-short.fix: Expand it to at least 70 characters: what the page offers, for whom, and why it is worth a click.

onpage.description-same-as-title.title: Meta description repeats the title
onpage.description-same-as-title.why: A description that only repeats the title wastes the snippet space that could explain the page.
onpage.description-same-as-title.fix: Write a description that adds detail beyond the title.

onpage.description-placeholder.title: Placeholder meta description
onpage.description-placeholder.why: Default descriptions left by a theme or CMS appear in search results and AI summaries and make the site look unfinished.
onpage.description-placeholder.fix: Replace the placeholder with a description written for this page.

onpage.description-duplicate.title: Duplicate meta descriptions
onpage.description-duplicate.why: Repeated descriptions make pages look interchangeable in results and are usually ignored in favour of page text.
onpage.description-duplicate.fix: Write a unique description for each indexable page, or leave it out on pages where a template would only repeat itself.

onpage.meta-keywords.title: Meta keywords tag present
onpage.meta-keywords.why: Google and Bing ignore meta keywords for ranking. The tag only shows competitors which terms you target.

onpage.og-missing.title: Open Graph tags missing
onpage.og-missing.why: og:title, og:description and og:image control how the page looks when shared on LinkedIn, Slack, WhatsApp and in some AI chat link previews.
onpage.og-missing.fix: Add og:title, og:description, og:image (absolute URL, at least 1200×630) and og:url to the page template.

onpage.og-image-invalid.title: og:image is not an absolute URL
onpage.og-image-invalid.why: Social platforms do not resolve relative paths in og:image, so no preview image is shown.
onpage.og-image-invalid.fix: Use a full https:// URL for og:image.

onpage.og-url-mismatch.title: og:url differs from the canonical
onpage.og-url-mismatch.why: Shares are counted against og:url. When it disagrees with the canonical, signals are split and the wrong URL may be shared.
onpage.og-url-mismatch.fix: Set og:url to the same URL as the canonical tag.

onpage.twitter-card-missing.title: No Twitter/X card type
onpage.twitter-card-missing.why: Without twitter:card, X shows a plain link (it falls back to Open Graph for text but needs the card type for a large image).

onpage.favicon-missing.title: No favicon declared
onpage.favicon-missing.why: Google shows the favicon next to your result on mobile and desktop, and AI tools show it next to citations. Without one, a generic icon appears.
onpage.favicon-missing.fix: Add <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.png"> (a square image, at least 48×48) to the home page.

headings.h1-missing.title: No H1 heading
headings.h1-missing.why: The H1 tells readers, assistive technology and AI extractors what the page is about. Pages without one are harder to summarise correctly.
headings.h1-missing.fix: Add one visible <h1> that states the page topic.

headings.h1-empty.title: Empty H1
headings.h1-empty.why: An empty H1 (often a logo wrapper with no text) gives the page no main heading at all.
headings.h1-empty.fix: Put real text in the H1, or use a different element for the logo.

headings.h1-multiple.title: Several H1 headings
headings.h1-multiple.why: Several H1s blur which topic is the main one. It is allowed, but one clear H1 makes the outline easier for people and parsers.
headings.h1-multiple.fix: Keep one H1 for the page topic and turn the others into H2s.

headings.h1-too-long.title: H1 is very long
headings.h1-too-long.why: A long H1 is usually a paragraph styled as a heading, which weakens the page outline.
headings.h1-too-long.fix: Shorten the H1 to under about 70 characters and move the rest into a paragraph.

headings.h1-image-only.title: H1 contains only an image
headings.h1-image-only.why: An H1 that is just an image relies on alt text for its meaning. Many crawlers and AI extractors read it as empty.
headings.h1-image-only.fix: Use real text in the H1. Keep the logo outside it, or add visually styled text.

headings.not-first.title: Content headings appear before the H1
headings.not-first.why: When H2s or H3s come before the H1 (often in sidebars or promos), the outline that screen readers and AI parsers see starts in the wrong place.
headings.not-first.fix: Put the H1 first in the main content; use non-heading elements for promos and widgets above it.

headings.skipped-level.title: Heading levels are skipped
headings.skipped-level.why: Jumping from H2 to H4 breaks the outline used by screen readers and by tools that split pages into sections for AI answers.
headings.skipped-level.fix: Use heading levels in order (H1, then H2, then H3) and style them with CSS rather than picking a level for its size.

headings.empty.title: Empty headings
headings.empty.why: Empty heading tags are announced by screen readers as blank headings and add noise to the outline.
headings.empty.fix: Remove empty heading tags or give them text.

headings.no-subheadings.title: Long page without subheadings
headings.no-subheadings.why: Long text without H2s is hard to scan. Search and AI engines use subheadings to find the passage that answers a question.
headings.no-subheadings.fix: Break the content into sections with descriptive H2s, ideally phrased the way people ask about the topic.

headings.duplicate-in-page.title: Same subheading repeated on a page
headings.duplicate-in-page.why: Identical subheadings make sections indistinguishable in the outline and in jump links.
headings.duplicate-in-page.fix: Make each subheading describe its own section.

headings.overused.title: Headings used for styling
headings.overused.why: When nearly every line is a heading, the outline stops meaning anything to screen readers and content parsers.
headings.overused.fix: Use headings only for section titles. Style other text with CSS classes.

headings.h1-duplicate.title: Duplicate H1 across pages
headings.h1-duplicate.why: Pages with the same H1 look like they cover the same topic and can compete for the same searches.
headings.h1-duplicate.fix: Give each page an H1 that names its specific topic.

onpage.description-thin-for-ai.title: Meta description is too thin to give AI context
onpage.description-thin-for-ai.why: AI assistants and answer engines often read the meta description first to decide what a page is about. A description that fits the snippet but says little (under about 120 characters) gives them too little to understand or quote.
onpage.description-thin-for-ai.fix: Rewrite it as a 120–160 character summary that names what the page offers, who it is for and one concrete detail (place, price, result).

onpage.title-same-as-h1.title: Title and H1 are identical on almost every page
onpage.title-same-as-h1.why: The title and the H1 do different jobs: the title wins the click in results, the H1 orients the reader. When a template copies one into the other everywhere, you lose the chance to add the brand, place or benefit to the title.
onpage.title-same-as-h1.fix: Keep the H1 as the on-page heading and write titles that add what searchers compare on (brand, location, offer). Most SEO plugins have a separate title field for this.

onpage.favicon-broken.title: Favicon does not load
onpage.favicon-broken.why: Google and AI tools fetch the declared favicon to show next to your result. A favicon that returns an error, or is not an image, is replaced with a generic globe.
onpage.favicon-broken.fix: Point <link rel="icon"> at an image that returns 200 (a square PNG, SVG or ICO of at least 48×48), and make sure robots.txt does not block it.

content.thin.title: Thin content
content.thin.why: Pages with very little text rarely answer a question fully, so search engines rank them poorly and AI engines have nothing worth quoting.
content.thin.fix: Add useful, original detail (what, who for, how, price, proof, FAQs), merge the page with a related one, or noindex it if it only exists for navigation.

content.low-text-ratio.title: Very little text for a heavy page
content.low-text-ratio.why: A large HTML document with little readable text is mostly code. It is slower to crawl and gives parsers more noise to wade through to find the content.
content.low-text-ratio.fix: Move inline scripts, styles and data into cached files, trim unused markup and make sure the main content is in the HTML.

content.lorem-ipsum.title: Lorem ipsum text on the page
content.lorem-ipsum.why: Dummy text in production makes the page look unfinished to visitors and low quality to search engines, and it can end up quoted in AI answers.
content.lorem-ipsum.fix: Replace the dummy text with real content or remove the section.

content.placeholder.title: Placeholder or unfinished text
content.placeholder.why: Phrases such as "coming soon", "[insert text]" or "TODO" signal an unfinished page to readers and quality systems.
content.placeholder.fix: Finish the content or remove the placeholder. Keep unfinished pages noindex until they are ready.

content.template-leak.title: Template code or broken values shown as text
content.template-leak.why: Visible "{{ variable }}", "[object Object]", "undefined" or raw page-builder shortcodes mean a template failed. Crawlers index the broken text as content.
content.template-leak.fix: Fix the template or data that produces the raw code, and make sure server-side rendering fills every value.

content.broken-encoding.title: Garbled characters (encoding errors)
content.broken-encoding.why: Sequences like "Ã©" or "â€™" come from text saved in one encoding and served as another. They look broken and corrupt quotes in search snippets and AI answers.
content.broken-encoding.fix: Store and serve everything as UTF-8 (database, files and the Content-Type header), then correct the affected text.

content.double-escaped.title: Double-escaped HTML entities in text
content.double-escaped.why: Text such as "&amp;" or "&#8217;" shows raw entity code to readers and in snippets.
content.double-escaped.fix: Escape text once. Look for a template or plugin that encodes already-encoded values.

content.keyword-stuffing.title: One word is repeated unnaturally often
content.keyword-stuffing.why: Repeating a term far more than natural writing would is a spam signal for search engines and makes the text worse for readers and AI summaries.
content.keyword-stuffing.fix: Rewrite the text naturally. Use the term where it fits and cover related subtopics instead of repeating it.

content.hard-to-read.title: Text is hard to read
content.hard-to-read.why: Dense text with long words and sentences is harder to follow. Clear, plain writing is easier to quote accurately in AI answers.
content.hard-to-read.fix: Use shorter sentences, everyday words and one idea per paragraph. Define technical terms once.

content.long-sentences.title: Sentences are long on average
content.long-sentences.why: Long sentences are harder to scan and harder to lift out as a self-contained answer.
content.long-sentences.fix: Aim for an average under 25 words per sentence. Split sentences joined with "and", "which" or semicolons.

content.long-paragraphs.title: Very long paragraphs
content.long-paragraphs.why: Walls of text are skipped on screens, especially on mobile, and are harder for AI engines to split into answerable passages.
content.long-paragraphs.fix: Break paragraphs longer than 150 words into shorter ones, or use lists for steps and options.

content.repeated-paragraph.title: Same paragraph repeated on the page
content.repeated-paragraph.why: Repeated blocks inflate the word count without adding information and look like low-effort content.
content.repeated-paragraph.fix: Remove the repeated paragraph or rewrite it for its context.

content.boilerplate-heavy.title: Navigation and footer outweigh the main content
content.boilerplate-heavy.why: When most of the text on a page is shared navigation, footer and sidebar copy, pages look alike and the unique content is hard to find.
content.boilerplate-heavy.fix: Add more page-specific content, or trim repeated menus, footers and widgets.

content.copyright-outdated.title: Copyright year is out of date
content.copyright-outdated.why: An old copyright year makes the site look abandoned to visitors and is a weak freshness signal.
content.copyright-outdated.fix: Generate the current year automatically in the footer template.

content.outdated-year-in-title.title: Title or H1 names a past year
content.outdated-year-in-title.why: A heading like "Best tools for 2022" tells searchers and AI engines the page is out of date, which lowers clicks and citations.
content.outdated-year-in-title.fix: Update the content and the year, or remove the year if the page is evergreen.

content.article-date-missing.title: Article has no published or updated date
content.article-date-missing.why: Readers and AI engines use dates to judge freshness. Undated articles are less likely to be chosen for time-sensitive answers.
content.article-date-missing.fix: Show the published and last-updated dates on the page and add datePublished and dateModified to the Article markup.

content.article-author-missing.title: Article has no author
content.article-author-missing.why: Named, credible authors are part of how Google and AI engines judge expertise and trust. Anonymous articles are weaker sources to cite.
content.article-author-missing.fix: Show the author name with a link to an author page, and add author (Person with name and url) to the Article markup.

content.date-in-future.title: Article date is in the future
content.date-in-future.why: A published or modified date ahead of today is a sign of a wrong timezone or a faked freshness date, and can be ignored or distrusted.
content.date-in-future.fix: Correct the date and include a timezone offset (for example 2025-05-01T09:00:00+01:00).

content.modified-before-published.title: Modified date is earlier than published date
content.modified-before-published.why: An updated date before the published date is contradictory, so engines may ignore both.
content.modified-before-published.fix: Make sure dateModified is the same as or later than datePublished.

content.stale-article.title: Article not updated in a long time
content.stale-article.why: Articles last touched more than 2 years ago may contain outdated facts, and engines favour current sources for many queries.
content.stale-article.fix: Review the article: update facts, examples and screenshots, then change the modified date. Retire or redirect it if it is no longer useful.

duplicates.exact.title: Exact duplicate pages
duplicates.exact.why: Identical content on several indexable URLs splits ranking signals and lets search engines pick the version to show, which may not be yours.
duplicates.exact.fix: Keep one URL. 301-redirect the others to it, or add a canonical pointing to it if both must stay reachable.

duplicates.near.title: Near-duplicate pages
duplicates.near.why: Pages that differ by only a few words (location or product variants built from one template) look like duplicates and may be filtered out of results.
duplicates.near.fix: Make each page genuinely different (local details, specific examples, pricing, FAQs), or merge them into one stronger page.

duplicates.url-variants.title: Same page indexable at several URL variants
duplicates.url-variants.why: When the same content is indexable at URLs that differ only by parameters, case or a trailing slash, link signals are split across copies.
duplicates.url-variants.fix: Pick one form, redirect the others to it, and make the canonical tag on every variant point to that form.

duplicates.shared-intro.title: Many pages open with the same text
duplicates.shared-intro.why: The first lines after the H1 are what snippets and AI answers quote most. When many pages share the same opening, none of them stands out.
duplicates.shared-intro.fix: Rewrite the opening paragraph of each page so it answers that page’s own topic directly.

duplicates.title-and-description.title: Pages share both title and description
duplicates.title-and-description.why: When two pages have the same title and the same description, search engines see them as the same result and usually show only one.
duplicates.title-and-description.fix: Differentiate the title and description of each page, or merge the pages if they really cover the same thing.

content.cannibalisation.title: Several pages target the same topic
content.cannibalisation.why: When two or more pages use the same key words in their title and H1, they compete for the same searches. Search engines and AI assistants pick one, often not the one you want, and the signals (links, engagement) are split between them.
content.cannibalisation.fix: Decide which page should rank for the topic. Merge the others into it (with a 301), or give each page a distinct focus and rewrite its title and H1 to match.

content.repeated-words.title: Doubled words in the text
content.repeated-words.why: Typos such as "the the" look careless to readers and lower trust. AI answer engines quote sentences verbatim, so a slip can travel with your brand name on it.
content.repeated-words.fix: Remove the repeated word in each quoted sentence. A spelling and grammar check (for example `avc connect spelling`) catches more.

content.spelling.title: Spelling and grammar mistakes
content.spelling.why: Mistakes make a page look less trustworthy to readers and quality raters, and AI answers that quote the page repeat them. Checked with LanguageTool on the main content only, so menus and footers do not add noise.
content.spelling.fix: Correct the listed mistakes in your CMS. Add brand and product names to your LanguageTool dictionary so they are not flagged again.
content.spelling.skippedReason: Needs a LanguageTool server. Run one locally, or opt in to the public API with `avc connect spelling`.

content.pdf-title-missing.title: PDF has no meaningful title
content.pdf-title-missing.why: Search engines index PDFs and use the document Title property as the result title. Without one, results show the file name or a generated title such as "Microsoft Word - final_v3.docx".
content.pdf-title-missing.fix: Set the Title (File → Properties → Description in Acrobat or Word) to a descriptive title, enable "show document title" in the PDF's initial view, and re-upload it at the same URL.

duplicates.semantic.title: Pages that say the same thing in different words
duplicates.semantic.why: Search engines and AI systems compare meaning, not only wording. Pages whose content is nearly the same in meaning compete with each other and dilute the one you want cited, even when no sentence is copied.
duplicates.semantic.fix: Merge pages that answer the same need (301 the weaker one), or make each page clearly different: its own audience, question or offer.
duplicates.semantic.skippedReason: Needs an embeddings model. Add an OpenAI or AI Gateway key and turn on embeddings (`avc connect embeddings`), or use --mock.

content.off-topic.title: Pages far from the site's main topics
content.off-topic.why: AI systems build a picture of what a site is an authority on. Indexable pages that have little to do with the rest of the site blur that picture and rarely earn citations themselves.
content.off-topic.fix: Check each page: connect it to your core topics (context, internal links), move it to a better home, or noindex it if it serves no search purpose.
content.off-topic.skippedReason: Needs an embeddings model. Add an OpenAI or AI Gateway key and turn on embeddings (`avc connect embeddings`), or use --mock.

canonical.missing.title: No canonical URL declared
canonical.missing.why: A self-referencing canonical tells search engines which URL to index when the page is reachable with parameters, tracking codes or other variants.
canonical.missing.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="…"> with the absolute, preferred URL of the page.

canonical.multiple.title: Several canonical tags
canonical.multiple.why: When a page declares more than one canonical, Google may ignore all of them.
canonical.multiple.fix: Keep exactly one canonical tag. Often a theme and an SEO plugin both add one; turn one off.

canonical.empty.title: Canonical tag has an empty or invalid href
canonical.empty.why: An empty or unparseable canonical is ignored, so the page has no canonical even though one was intended.
canonical.empty.fix: Fill in the full preferred URL in the canonical href.

canonical.relative.title: Canonical uses a relative URL
canonical.relative.why: Relative canonicals work but break easily: on staging, alternate hosts or http copies they point at the wrong place. Google recommends absolute URLs.
canonical.relative.fix: Use the full URL, including https:// and the host, in the canonical tag.

canonical.has-fragment.title: Canonical contains a # fragment
canonical.has-fragment.why: Search engines ignore the part after #, so a canonical with a fragment is a sign of a templating mistake.
canonical.has-fragment.fix: Remove the # fragment from the canonical URL.

canonical.outside-head.title: Canonical tag placed in <body>
canonical.outside-head.why: Google ignores rel=canonical in the body, so the canonical has no effect.

canonical.header-mismatch.title: Canonical tag and Link header disagree
canonical.header-mismatch.why: When the HTML canonical and the HTTP Link canonical point to different URLs, Google may ignore both.
canonical.header-mismatch.fix: Remove one of them, or make both point to the same URL.

canonical.points-elsewhere.title: Page canonicalises to another URL
canonical.points-elsewhere.why: This page asks search engines to index a different URL instead. That is right for duplicates, but a mistake on unique pages, which then never appear in results.
canonical.points-elsewhere.fix: Check the target. If this page is unique, make the canonical self-referencing.

canonical.to-error.title: Canonical points to an error page
canonical.to-error.why: A canonical to a 4xx or 5xx URL asks search engines to index something that does not exist. They usually ignore it and pick their own canonical.
canonical.to-error.fix: Point the canonical at a live 200 URL, normally the page itself.

canonical.to-redirect.title: Canonical points to a redirect
canonical.to-redirect.why: A canonical should name the final URL. Pointing it at a redirect sends mixed signals and is often ignored.
canonical.to-redirect.fix: Update the canonical to the URL the redirect ends at.

canonical.to-noindex.title: Canonical points to a noindex page
canonical.to-noindex.why: Saying "index that URL instead" while that URL says "do not index me" can leave neither page in search.
canonical.to-noindex.fix: Point the canonical at an indexable page, or remove noindex from the target.

canonical.to-blocked.title: Canonical points to a URL blocked by robots.txt
canonical.to-blocked.why: Search engines cannot crawl the canonical target to confirm it, so the canonical is unlikely to be honoured.
canonical.to-blocked.fix: Allow the target in robots.txt or choose a crawlable canonical.

canonical.chain.title: Canonical chain or loop
canonical.chain.why: If page A canonicalises to B and B canonicalises to C (or back to A), search engines may give up and choose a canonical themselves.
canonical.chain.fix: Point every page in the chain directly at the final preferred URL, which should canonicalise to itself.

canonical.cross-domain.title: Canonical points to another domain
canonical.cross-domain.why: A cross-domain canonical hands this page’s ranking to another site. Correct for syndicated copies, harmful when it is a leftover from a migration or a copied template.
canonical.cross-domain.fix: Confirm the other domain should rank instead of this page. If not, make the canonical self-referencing.

canonical.host-or-protocol-variant.title: Canonical uses the wrong host or protocol
canonical.host-or-protocol-variant.why: A canonical to http:// on an https site, or to www when the site runs on the bare domain, points search engines at a URL that only redirects.
canonical.host-or-protocol-variant.fix: Use the same protocol and host as the live site in every canonical.

canonical.keeps-parameters.title: Canonical keeps tracking or session parameters
canonical.keeps-parameters.why: A canonical that includes utm_, gclid or session parameters makes every tracked visit look like its own page.
canonical.keeps-parameters.fix: Strip tracking and session parameters from the canonical URL.

canonical.parameter-self.title: Parameter URL canonicalises to itself
canonical.parameter-self.why: Sorted, filtered or tracked URLs that declare themselves canonical compete with the clean URL in the index.
canonical.parameter-self.fix: Point the canonical of parameter variants at the clean URL, unless the parameter genuinely changes the main content (pagination, language).

canonical.all-to-homepage.title: Many pages canonicalise to the home page
canonical.all-to-homepage.why: A template that sets every canonical to the home page tells search engines to drop all those pages. It is a common and costly bug.
canonical.all-to-homepage.fix: Make the canonical on each page point to that page’s own URL. Check the template or SEO plugin setting that outputs it.

links-internal.broken.title: Links to broken internal pages
links-internal.broken.why: Broken internal links send visitors, crawlers and AI agents to dead ends and waste the link value they carry.
links-internal.broken.fix: Update each link to a working URL or remove it. If the target moved, add a 301 redirect too.

links-internal.to-redirect.title: Links to internal redirects
links-internal.to-redirect.why: Each link to a redirect adds a hop for users and crawlers and is a weaker signal than linking to the final URL.
links-internal.to-redirect.fix: Change these links to point directly at the final URL.

links-internal.to-canonicalised.title: Links to non-canonical URLs
links-internal.to-canonicalised.why: Linking to a URL that canonicalises elsewhere contradicts the canonical. Consistent internal links help search engines respect your preferred URL.
links-internal.to-canonicalised.fix: Link to the canonical version of each page.

links-internal.nofollow.title: Internal links marked nofollow
links-internal.nofollow.why: rel="nofollow" on your own links stops crawlers following them and does not save link value for other pages. It usually hides pages you want found.
links-internal.nofollow.fix: Remove rel="nofollow" from internal links. Use noindex on the target if it should stay out of search.

links-internal.to-blocked.title: Links to URLs blocked by robots.txt
links-internal.to-blocked.why: Links to disallowed URLs lead crawlers to pages they may not fetch, and the URLs can still be indexed without content.
links-internal.to-blocked.fix: Remove links to blocked URLs where users do not need them, or allow crawling and use noindex instead.

links-internal.insecure.title: Internal links use http://
links-internal.insecure.why: Linking to the http version of your own HTTPS site forces a redirect on every click and mixes protocol signals.
links-internal.insecure.fix: Change internal links to https:// or to root-relative paths (/page).

links-internal.tracking-parameters.title: Internal links carry tracking parameters
links-internal.tracking-parameters.why: utm_ and similar parameters on internal links create duplicate URLs for crawlers and overwrite the real traffic source in analytics.
links-internal.tracking-parameters.fix: Remove tracking parameters from internal links. Use event tracking for internal campaigns instead.

links-internal.missing-protocol.title: Link missing http(s):// is treated as a relative path
links-internal.missing-protocol.why: An href like "www.example.com" without https:// resolves as a path on your own site, creating a broken link.
links-internal.missing-protocol.fix: Add https:// to the start of the link.

links-internal.uncrawlable.title: Links that crawlers cannot follow
links-internal.uncrawlable.why: Google, Bing and AI crawlers only follow <a> elements with a real href. javascript: links, empty hrefs and onclick-only navigation are invisible to them.
links-internal.uncrawlable.fix: Use <a href="/real-url"> for navigation. Use <button> for actions that are not navigation.

links-internal.generic-anchors.title: Generic anchor text
links-internal.generic-anchors.why: Anchors such as "click here" or "read more" tell search engines, AI crawlers and screen-reader users nothing about the target page.
links-internal.generic-anchors.fix: Rewrite the links so the anchor says what the target is, for example "pricing for small teams" rather than "click here".

links-internal.long-anchor.title: Very long anchor text
links-internal.long-anchor.why: Anchors that wrap whole paragraphs or cards dilute what the link is about and are tiring for screen-reader users.
links-internal.long-anchor.fix: Keep anchor text short and specific (under about 120 characters).

links-internal.too-many.title: Very many links on one page
links-internal.too-many.why: Hundreds of links on one page divide its link value thinly and make it hard for crawlers and people to tell which links matter.
links-internal.too-many.fix: Trim mega-menus and footers, group links on hub pages and keep the most important links in the main content.

links-internal.dead-end.title: Page has no internal links
links-internal.dead-end.why: A page with no links to the rest of the site is a dead end: crawlers and visitors cannot continue, and it passes no value on.
links-internal.dead-end.fix: Add navigation and contextual links to related pages.

links-internal.single-inlink.title: Page has only one internal link pointing to it
links-internal.single-inlink.why: A page reachable through a single link is fragile and looks unimportant to crawlers.
links-internal.single-inlink.fix: Link to the page from other relevant pages, hubs or the navigation.

links-internal.low-link-score.title: Weak internal link score
links-internal.low-link-score.why: Internal links pass authority. Pages in the bottom tenth of the site’s internal link graph get little of it, so they rank and get crawled less.
links-internal.low-link-score.fix: Add contextual links to this page from strong pages (home, hubs, popular articles).

links-internal.orphan.title: Orphan pages (in the sitemap, not linked)
links-internal.orphan.why: Pages that only appear in the sitemap get no internal link value and look unimportant. Crawlers following links never reach them.
links-internal.orphan.fix: Link to each orphan from a relevant page or hub, or remove it from the sitemap if it is obsolete.

links-internal.navigation-only.title: Pages linked only from menus and footers
links-internal.navigation-only.why: Links inside the main content carry more context than site-wide menus. Pages with no contextual links are harder for search and AI engines to place in a topic.
links-internal.navigation-only.fix: Link to these pages from relevant paragraphs on related pages, with descriptive anchor text.

links-internal.concentration.title: Internal links concentrated on a few pages
links-internal.concentration.why: When a small set of pages collects nearly all internal link value, the rest of the site is under-supported in crawling and ranking.
links-internal.concentration.fix: Add contextual links between related deep pages, and from hubs to the pages they summarise.

links-internal.hashbang.title: Navigation uses #! or # routes
links-internal.hashbang.why: Crawlers ignore everything after #, so "#!/page" or "#/page" routes all look like one URL. Each view needs its own real path.
links-internal.hashbang.fix: Switch the router to history mode (real paths such as /page) and render each route on the server.

links-external.broken.title: Broken outbound links
links-external.broken.why: Links to dead pages frustrate readers and suggest the content is not maintained, which weakens it as a source for search and AI engines.
links-external.broken.fix: Update each link to a working source, link to an archived copy, or remove it.

links-external.redirecting.title: Outbound links that redirect
links-external.redirecting.why: Outbound links that redirect are often moved or retired pages; some end at a different page than the one you meant to cite.
links-external.redirecting.fix: Update the links to the current URLs.

links-external.insecure.title: Outbound links use http://
links-external.insecure.why: Linking to http:// pages sends readers to unencrypted sites and browsers may warn them. Many such sites now support https.
links-external.insecure.fix: Switch links to https:// where the destination supports it.

links-external.dev-host.title: Links to localhost or private network addresses
links-external.dev-host.why: Links to localhost, private IPs or .local hosts are leftovers from development. They are broken for everyone else.
links-external.dev-host.fix: Replace these links with the live URLs (often a find-and-replace in the database or content files).

links-external.sponsored-unqualified.title: Affiliate links without rel="sponsored"
links-external.sponsored-unqualified.why: Google asks for paid and affiliate links to be marked rel="sponsored" (or nofollow). Unmarked ones can be treated as link schemes.
links-external.sponsored-unqualified.fix: Add rel="sponsored" to affiliate and paid links.

links-external.noopener.title: target="_blank" links without rel="noopener"
links-external.noopener.why: Older browsers let a page opened with target="_blank" control the original tab (tabnabbing). Modern browsers default to noopener, but explicit rel protects every visitor.
links-external.noopener.fix: Add rel="noopener" (or "noopener noreferrer") to external links that open in a new tab.

links-external.too-many.title: Very many outbound links
links-external.too-many.why: A page with hundreds of outbound links looks like a link directory and gives each link little weight.
links-external.too-many.fix: Keep outbound links to sources that support the content.

links-external.unsafe.title: Links to sites flagged for malware or phishing
links-external.unsafe.why: Linking to a site Google Safe Browsing lists for malware, phishing or unwanted software puts visitors at risk and can make browsers warn about your pages. It is often a sign of a hacked page, an expired domain someone bought, or spam in comments.
links-external.unsafe.fix: Remove or replace each flagged link. If you did not add it, check the page for injected content and change your CMS passwords.
links-external.unsafe.skippedReason: Needs a Google Safe Browsing API key (AVC_SAFE_BROWSING_KEY) and --external-links.

images.alt-missing.title: Images without an alt attribute
images.alt-missing.why: Alt text is how screen readers, image search and AI crawlers understand an image. Without the attribute, screen readers may read the file name instead.
images.alt-missing.fix: Add alt text describing what the image shows and why it is there. Use alt="" for purely decorative images.

images.alt-unhelpful.title: Alt text is a file name or a generic word
images.alt-unhelpful.why: Alt text like "IMG_2041.jpg" or "image" gives no information to screen-reader users or to search and AI engines.
images.alt-unhelpful.fix: Replace it with a short description of the image content.

images.alt-too-long.title: Alt text is very long
images.alt-too-long.why: Very long alt text is tiring for screen-reader users and often stuffed with keywords.
images.alt-too-long.fix: Keep alt text under about 125 characters. Put longer explanations in a caption or the body text.

images.alt-stuffed.title: Alt text looks keyword-stuffed
images.alt-stuffed.why: Comma-separated keyword lists in alt text are a spam pattern and useless to screen-reader users.
images.alt-stuffed.fix: Write alt text as a natural sentence fragment describing the image.

images.dimensions-missing.title: Images without width and height
images.dimensions-missing.why: Without width and height the browser cannot reserve space, so the layout jumps when images load (Cumulative Layout Shift).
images.dimensions-missing.fix: Add width and height attributes matching the image’s aspect ratio. CSS can still make it responsive.

images.large.title: Heavy image files
images.large.why: Large images are the most common cause of slow Largest Contentful Paint, especially on mobile data.
images.large.fix: Resize to the displayed size, compress, and serve WebP or AVIF. Most CMSs and image CDNs can do this automatically.

images.legacy-format.title: Large images in JPEG, PNG or GIF
images.legacy-format.why: WebP and AVIF are typically 25–50% smaller than JPEG or PNG at the same quality, and every current browser supports WebP.
images.legacy-format.fix: Serve WebP or AVIF, using <picture> with a fallback if you need one, or turn on format conversion in your image CDN.

images.no-srcset.title: Large images without responsive sizes
images.no-srcset.why: Without srcset, phones download the same large file as desktops.
images.no-srcset.fix: Provide srcset and sizes (or use your framework’s image component) so each device gets a suitably sized file.

images.lazy-above-fold.title: First images are lazy-loaded
images.lazy-above-fold.why: Lazy-loading the hero image delays the Largest Contentful Paint, because the browser waits for layout before fetching it.
images.lazy-above-fold.fix: Remove loading="lazy" from the first one or two images and add fetchpriority="high" to the main one.

images.no-lazy-loading.title: Many images and none lazy-loaded
images.no-lazy-loading.why: Loading every image up front competes with the content people see first and wastes data on images they may never scroll to.
images.no-lazy-loading.fix: Add loading="lazy" to images below the first screen.

images.lcp-priority.title: Hero image is not prioritised
images.lcp-priority.why: fetchpriority="high" (or a preload) on the main above-the-fold image lets the browser fetch it first, which often improves LCP noticeably.
images.lcp-priority.fix: Add fetchpriority="high" to the hero image, or preload it with <link rel="preload" as="image">.

images.broken.title: Broken images
images.broken.why: Missing images show as empty boxes, look neglected and are dropped from image search.
images.broken.fix: Fix the image path, restore the file, or remove the reference.

images.wrong-content-type.title: Image URL does not return an image
images.wrong-content-type.why: An whose URL returns HTML or text (often an error page) will not display and cannot be indexed.
images.wrong-content-type.fix: Point the image at a real image file and make the server send an image/* Content-Type.

images.empty-src.title: Images with an empty src
images.empty-src.why: An empty src makes some browsers request the page itself again, and the image never shows for crawlers that do not run JavaScript.
images.empty-src.fix: Set a real src in the HTML. If a lazy-load script swaps data-src, include a <noscript> fallback or use native loading="lazy".

images.inline-data-heavy.title: Large images embedded as data URIs
images.inline-data-heavy.why: Base64 images inside the HTML cannot be cached separately and inflate every page download.
images.inline-data-heavy.fix: Serve large images as separate files. Keep data URIs for tiny icons or placeholders only.

images.too-many.title: Very many images on one page
images.too-many.why: Hundreds of images mean hundreds of requests and a heavy page, even with lazy loading.
images.too-many.fix: Paginate galleries, use thumbnails, and remove decorative images that add little.

images.oversized-rendered.title: Images far larger than they are displayed
images.oversized-rendered.why: An image shown 300 pixels wide but delivered 2,000 pixels wide downloads several times more data than needed, which slows Largest Contentful Paint on phones. Measured in a real browser render.
images.oversized-rendered.fix: Serve images close to their displayed size: add srcset and sizes so phones get smaller files, or use your CMS or image CDN resizing.

schema.invalid-json.title: JSON-LD block cannot be parsed
schema.invalid-json.why: A syntax error (trailing comma, unescaped quote, HTML inside the script) makes the whole block unreadable, so search and AI engines ignore all of it.
schema.invalid-json.fix: Fix the JSON syntax. Validate with the Schema Markup Validator or Google’s Rich Results Test.

schema.missing-context.title: JSON-LD without a schema.org @context
schema.missing-context.why: Without "@context": "https://schema.org", the types and properties have no defined meaning and parsers may skip the block.
schema.missing-context.fix: Add "@context": "https://schema.org" at the top level of each JSON-LD block.

schema.missing-type.title: JSON-LD block without @type
schema.missing-type.why: A node without @type does not say what it describes, so it cannot be used for rich results or entity understanding.
schema.missing-type.fix: Add the correct @type (for example Organization, Article, Product) to the node.

schema.type-misspelled.title: Schema type misspelled or wrong case
schema.type-misspelled.why: schema.org types are case-sensitive and use American spelling. "Organisation" or "localbusiness" are not recognised, so the markup does nothing.
schema.type-misspelled.fix: Use the exact type name from schema.org, for example "Organization", "LocalBusiness", "BreadcrumbList".

schema.date-format.title: Dates not in ISO 8601 format
schema.date-format.why: Dates like "12/03/2024" are ambiguous and are rejected for rich results. ISO 8601 (2024-03-12T09:00:00+00:00) is required.
schema.date-format.fix: Output dates in ISO 8601, ideally with time and timezone offset.

schema.relative-urls.title: Relative URLs in structured data
schema.relative-urls.why: Structured data is often read out of context. Relative paths for url, image or logo may be resolved wrongly or dropped.
schema.relative-urls.fix: Use absolute https:// URLs for url, image, logo, sameAs and item properties.

schema.empty-values.title: Empty values in structured data
schema.empty-values.why: Empty strings for name, description or image usually come from a template field left blank. They are invalid and can block rich results.
schema.empty-values.fix: Fill the fields or omit them from the markup when there is no value.

schema.conflicting-ids.title: Same @id used for different things
schema.conflicting-ids.why: @id joins nodes into one entity. Reusing an @id for nodes with different types merges unrelated things in the knowledge graph parsers build.
schema.conflicting-ids.fix: Give each distinct entity its own @id (for example https://example.com/#organization, …/#website).

schema.sameas-invalid.title: sameAs values are not profile URLs
schema.sameas-invalid.why: sameAs links your entity to its profiles (LinkedIn, Wikipedia, Wikidata, Crunchbase). Values that are not URLs, or point back at your own site, add nothing.
schema.sameas-invalid.fix: List full URLs of official profiles on other sites in sameAs.

schema.microdata-only.title: Structured data only in Microdata or RDFa
schema.microdata-only.why: Google supports Microdata, but JSON-LD is its recommended format and is far easier to keep correct. Many AI tools only read JSON-LD.
schema.microdata-only.fix: Move the markup to a JSON-LD script in <head> and remove the inline attributes once it is validated.

schema.organization-incomplete.title: Organization markup is missing properties
schema.organization-incomplete.why: Organization markup with name, url, logo and sameAs helps Google and AI engines recognise your brand as one entity and show the right logo.
schema.organization-incomplete.fix: Include name, url, logo (absolute image URL, at least 112×112) and sameAs links to official profiles.

schema.localbusiness-incomplete.title: LocalBusiness markup is missing properties
schema.localbusiness-incomplete.why: Local business markup with a full address, phone and opening hours supports local results and lets AI assistants answer "is it open" and "where is it" correctly.
schema.localbusiness-incomplete.fix: Add name, a PostalAddress (streetAddress, addressLocality, postalCode, addressCountry), telephone, openingHoursSpecification, geo and image.

schema.article-incomplete.title: Article markup is missing properties
schema.article-incomplete.why: Article markup with headline, image, dates and author makes the piece eligible for article features and gives AI engines clear authorship and freshness signals.
schema.article-incomplete.fix: Include headline, image, datePublished, dateModified and author (a Person or Organization with name and url).

schema.headline-too-long.title: Article headline is very long
