schema.headline-too-long.why: Very long headlines are truncated in article features; Google historically limited headline to 110 characters.
schema.headline-too-long.fix: Use the page’s concise title as the headline.

schema.headline-mismatch.title: Article headline does not match the page
schema.headline-mismatch.why: Structured data must describe the visible page. A headline that matches neither the title nor the H1 suggests copied or stale markup.
schema.headline-mismatch.fix: Generate the headline from the same field as the page title or H1.

schema.product-incomplete.title: Product markup is missing properties
schema.product-incomplete.why: Product markup needs a name and at least one of offers, review or aggregateRating to be eligible for product results. Identifiers and brand help shopping surfaces and AI shopping agents match the product.
schema.product-incomplete.fix: Add name, image, description, brand, an identifier (sku or gtin) and an Offer with price, priceCurrency and availability.

schema.offer-incomplete.title: Offer markup is missing properties
schema.offer-incomplete.why: Offers without price, currency and availability cannot show price in results and give shopping agents nothing reliable to act on.
schema.offer-incomplete.fix: Add price (a plain number such as 1299.00), priceCurrency (ISO code such as GBP) and availability (https://schema.org/InStock).

schema.faq-incomplete.title: FAQPage markup is missing properties
schema.faq-incomplete.why: FAQ markup needs Question items with an acceptedAnswer. Incomplete markup is ignored, and AI engines lose a clean question-and-answer source.
schema.faq-incomplete.fix: Give mainEntity a list of Question nodes, each with name and acceptedAnswer.text.

schema.faq-not-visible.title: FAQ markup questions are not on the page
schema.faq-not-visible.why: Google requires FAQ content to be visible to users. Questions that appear only in markup break the guidelines and can be treated as spammy structured data.
schema.faq-not-visible.fix: Show every marked-up question and answer on the page, or remove the ones that are not shown.

schema.howto-incomplete.title: HowTo markup is missing properties
schema.howto-incomplete.why: Google no longer shows HowTo rich results, but complete step markup still gives AI engines an unambiguous sequence to quote.
schema.howto-incomplete.fix: Give the HowTo a name and a list of HowToStep items, each with text (and name or url where useful).

schema.breadcrumb-incomplete.title: BreadcrumbList markup is missing properties
schema.breadcrumb-incomplete.why: Breadcrumb markup replaces the URL in results with a readable path. Items without position, name or item are ignored.
schema.breadcrumb-incomplete.fix: Each ListItem needs position (1, 2, 3…), name and item (the URL; optional for the last item).

schema.website-incomplete.title: WebSite markup is missing properties
schema.website-incomplete.why: WebSite markup with name and url is how Google picks the site name shown in results. alternateName covers acronyms or shorter names.
schema.website-incomplete.fix: Add WebSite markup on the home page with name, url and optionally alternateName.

schema.event-incomplete.title: Event markup is missing properties
schema.event-incomplete.why: Events need a name, start date and location to appear in event results and to be answered correctly by assistants.
schema.event-incomplete.fix: Add name, startDate (ISO 8601 with timezone), location (Place with address, or VirtualLocation), and recommended endDate, eventStatus, image and offers.

schema.review-incomplete.title: Review markup is missing properties
schema.review-incomplete.why: Reviews need an author and a rating to be valid. Incomplete reviews are ignored for review snippets.
schema.review-incomplete.fix: Add author (Person or Organization with name), reviewRating with ratingValue, and itemReviewed when the review stands alone.

schema.rating-invalid.title: AggregateRating markup is missing properties
schema.rating-invalid.why: An aggregate rating needs a value and a count, and the value must sit inside the rating scale. Invalid ratings are dropped and can look manipulated.
schema.rating-invalid.fix: Provide ratingValue within bestRating/worstRating (default 1–5) and a ratingCount or reviewCount above zero, taken from real reviews.

schema.video-incomplete.title: VideoObject markup is missing properties
schema.video-incomplete.why: Videos need name, thumbnail and upload date to appear in video results. contentUrl or embedUrl lets Google fetch the file for key moments.
schema.video-incomplete.fix: Add name, thumbnailUrl, uploadDate (ISO 8601), description, duration (ISO 8601, e.g. PT2M30S) and contentUrl or embedUrl.

schema.person-incomplete.title: Person markup is missing properties
schema.person-incomplete.why: A Person with a name, profile URL and role lets search and AI engines connect authors and team members to their wider reputation.
schema.person-incomplete.fix: Give each Person a name, url (their author or team page), sameAs (LinkedIn and other profiles) and jobTitle.

schema.jobposting-incomplete.title: JobPosting markup is missing properties
schema.jobposting-incomplete.why: Job postings missing required fields are not shown in Google’s job experience.
schema.jobposting-incomplete.fix: Add title, description, datePosted, hiringOrganization and jobLocation (or applicantLocationRequirements with jobLocationType TELECOMMUTE for remote roles).

schema.self-serving-reviews.title: Business rates itself in its own markup
schema.self-serving-reviews.why: Google ignores review stars that an Organization or LocalBusiness adds about itself on its own site, and repeated misuse can lead to a manual action.
schema.self-serving-reviews.fix: Remove aggregateRating and review from Organization/LocalBusiness markup. Keep ratings on Product or Service pages where they reflect real third-party reviews.

schema.price-not-visible.title: Marked-up price not shown on the page
schema.price-not-visible.why: Prices in markup must match what shoppers see. A mismatch can remove the product from rich results and misleads shopping agents.
schema.price-not-visible.fix: Make sure the Offer price in the markup is the price shown on the page.

schema.article-missing.title: Article page without Article markup
schema.article-missing.why: Article markup states the headline, author and dates explicitly, which helps Google’s article features and gives AI engines reliable authorship and freshness.
schema.article-missing.fix: Add Article or BlogPosting JSON-LD with headline, image, datePublished, dateModified and author.

schema.organization-missing.title: No Organization or LocalBusiness markup
schema.organization-missing.why: Organization markup on the home page is the clearest statement of who runs the site: name, logo, contact details and official profiles. Search and AI engines use it to build an entity for your brand.
schema.organization-missing.fix: Add Organization (or the most specific LocalBusiness type) JSON-LD to the home page with name, url, logo, contactPoint and sameAs.

schema.website-missing.title: No WebSite markup on the home page
schema.website-missing.why: WebSite markup is how Google chooses the site name shown above your results.
schema.website-missing.fix: Add WebSite JSON-LD to the home page with name and url.

schema.breadcrumbs-missing.title: Deeper pages without breadcrumb markup
schema.breadcrumbs-missing.why: Breadcrumb markup shows the site hierarchy in results and helps engines understand where a page sits.
schema.breadcrumbs-missing.fix: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD (and a visible breadcrumb trail) to pages below the top level.

schema.organization-inconsistent.title: Organization details differ between pages
schema.organization-inconsistent.why: If pages describe the organisation with different names, logos or phone numbers, search and AI engines cannot tell which is right and may merge or split the entity.
schema.organization-inconsistent.fix: Output the Organization markup from one shared source so every page carries identical name, logo and contact details.

hreflang.invalid-code.title: Invalid hreflang language or region code
hreflang.invalid-code.why: hreflang values must be an ISO 639-1 language, optionally with an ISO 3166-1 region (en-GB). Invalid codes such as "en-UK" or "jp" are ignored.
hreflang.invalid-code.fix: Correct the codes. Use language-REGION with a hyphen, for example en-GB, pt-BR, es-419.

hreflang.missing-self.title: hreflang set has no self-reference
hreflang.missing-self.why: Each page in an hreflang set should list itself as well as its alternates. Without it, Google may not treat the set as complete.
hreflang.missing-self.fix: Add an hreflang entry pointing to the page itself, with its own language code.

hreflang.missing-x-default.title: No x-default hreflang
hreflang.missing-x-default.why: x-default tells search engines which version to show users whose language or region you do not target.
hreflang.missing-x-default.fix: Add hreflang="x-default" pointing at the language selector or the main version.

hreflang.duplicate-code.title: Same hreflang code points to different URLs
hreflang.duplicate-code.why: If one language-region code lists two different URLs, search engines cannot tell which to show and may ignore both.
hreflang.duplicate-code.fix: Keep one URL per hreflang code.

hreflang.single-entry.title: hreflang lists only the page itself
hreflang.single-entry.why: A lone self-referencing hreflang does nothing. It usually means alternates failed to output from the CMS.
hreflang.single-entry.fix: List every language version in the set, or remove hreflang if the site has only one language.

hreflang.relative-url.title: hreflang uses relative URLs
hreflang.relative-url.why: Google requires fully qualified URLs in hreflang annotations. Relative ones are ignored.
hreflang.relative-url.fix: Use absolute URLs including https:// and the host.

hreflang.lang-mismatch.title: Self hreflang language differs from the page language
hreflang.lang-mismatch.why: When a page says hreflang="fr" for itself but its html lang is "en", one of the two is wrong and the language version may be served to the wrong audience.
hreflang.lang-mismatch.fix: Make the self-referencing hreflang code and the <html lang> attribute agree.

hreflang.canonical-conflict.title: Canonical points to another language version
hreflang.canonical-conflict.why: If a translated page canonicalises to a different language version, search engines drop the translation and the hreflang set breaks.
hreflang.canonical-conflict.fix: Make each language version canonicalise to itself.

hreflang.target-problem.title: hreflang points to a URL that is not indexable
hreflang.target-problem.why: Alternates must be live, indexable, canonical URLs. Links to errors, redirects, noindex or canonicalised pages are ignored.
hreflang.target-problem.fix: Point each hreflang entry at the final, indexable, self-canonical URL of that language version.

hreflang.on-non-indexable.title: hreflang on a page that is not indexable
hreflang.on-non-indexable.why: hreflang on a noindex or canonicalised page cannot take effect, and the alternates pointing back to it are wasted.
hreflang.on-non-indexable.fix: Remove hreflang from non-indexable pages, or make the page indexable if it is a real language version.

hreflang.missing-return.title: hreflang return links missing
hreflang.missing-return.why: hreflang only counts when both pages point to each other. If page A lists B but B does not list A, Google ignores the pair.
hreflang.missing-return.fix: Make every language version list every other version (and itself). Generate the set from one source so they stay in sync.

hreflang.source-conflict.title: HTML and sitemap hreflang disagree
hreflang.source-conflict.why: When hreflang is declared in both the HTML and the sitemap with different values, search engines get two conflicting sets.
hreflang.source-conflict.fix: Declare hreflang in one place, or generate both from the same data.

mobile.viewport-missing.title: No viewport meta tag
mobile.viewport-missing.why: Without a viewport tag, phones render the page at desktop width and shrink it. Google indexes the mobile version, so this affects every page’s rankings.

mobile.viewport-not-responsive.title: Viewport is not set to the device width
mobile.viewport-not-responsive.why: A fixed viewport width (width=1024) or missing width=device-width forces a desktop layout on phones.
mobile.viewport-not-responsive.fix: Use content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" and make the layout responsive with CSS.

mobile.zoom-disabled.title: Pinch-zoom is disabled
mobile.zoom-disabled.why: user-scalable=no or a low maximum-scale stops people with low vision from zooming. It fails WCAG 1.4.4.
mobile.zoom-disabled.fix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag.

mobile.viewport-multiple.title: More than one viewport tag
mobile.viewport-multiple.why: Several viewport tags conflict and browsers use the last one, which may not be the one you meant.

mobile.plugins.title: Content needs a browser plugin
mobile.plugins.why: Flash, Java applets and similar plugin content does not run on phones or modern browsers, and crawlers cannot read it.
mobile.plugins.fix: Replace plugin content with HTML5 video, images or plain HTML.

mobile.fixed-width.title: Elements with fixed widths wider than a phone
mobile.fixed-width.why: Inline widths above 640px force sideways scrolling on phones.
mobile.fixed-width.fix: Use max-width: 100% or relative units instead of fixed pixel widths on tables, iframes and containers.

mobile.small-text.title: Text set below 12px
mobile.small-text.why: Text smaller than 12px is hard to read on phones without zooming.
mobile.small-text.fix: Use a base font size of at least 16px for body text and avoid sizes under 12px.

mobile.input-types.title: Email or phone fields use a plain text input
mobile.input-types.why: type="email" and type="tel" bring up the right keyboard on phones and help browsers and AI agents fill the form correctly.
mobile.input-types.fix: Set type="email" on email fields and type="tel" on phone fields, with matching autocomplete values.

mobile.separate-mobile-urls.title: Separate mobile URLs (m-dot) in use
mobile.separate-mobile-urls.why: Separate mobile URLs need rel=alternate and rel=canonical annotations in both directions and full content parity. Google indexes the mobile version, so any gap costs rankings.
mobile.separate-mobile-urls.fix: Prefer a responsive site. If you keep m-dot URLs, check alternate/canonical pairs and that mobile pages have the same content and structured data.

mobile.touch-icon-missing.title: No apple-touch-icon
mobile.touch-icon-missing.why: The touch icon is used when people save the site to a phone home screen and by some apps for link previews.

mobile.horizontal-scroll.title: Page is wider than a phone screen
mobile.horizontal-scroll.why: When content is wider than the viewport, visitors have to scroll sideways and text runs off the screen. Google indexes the mobile version of a page, so mobile usability problems affect everyone.
mobile.horizontal-scroll.fix: Find the wide element (fixed widths, wide tables, long unbroken strings, images without max-width) and make it fit: max-width: 100%, overflow-x: auto for tables, overflow-wrap: anywhere for long strings.

mobile.tap-targets.title: Buttons and links too small to tap
mobile.tap-targets.why: Targets smaller than 24×24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8) are hard to hit with a finger, so visitors tap the wrong thing. Links inside sentences are exempt.
mobile.tap-targets.fix: Give icon buttons and small links at least 24×24px of tappable area (padding counts), and leave space between neighbouring targets.

mobile.content-parity.title: Phones get less content than desktops
mobile.content-parity.why: Google indexes the mobile version of each page. Text or links that only appear on desktop are, for search, not on the page at all, and AI crawlers that fetch as a phone miss them too.
mobile.content-parity.fix: Serve the same main content and links to phones and desktops. Collapse sections on small screens instead of removing them, and avoid separate mobile templates that drop content.

mobile.interstitial.title: Pop-up covers the content on phones
mobile.interstitial.why: A pop-up or overlay that covers much of the screen right after load makes content hard to reach. Google treats intrusive interstitials on mobile as a page experience problem; cookie notices and age gates required by law are fine when they are small.
mobile.interstitial.fix: Show newsletter and offer pop-ups later (after scrolling or on exit), as a small banner on phones, and make them easy to close. Keep legally required notices compact.

mobile.blocked-resources.title: Resources fail to load only on phones
mobile.blocked-resources.why: Google renders the mobile version. Scripts, styles or API calls that fail only for a phone user agent (device-specific rules, mobile CDNs, bot rules) can leave the indexed version broken.
mobile.blocked-resources.fix: Check the listed URLs with a mobile user agent and remove the rule that blocks or breaks them (CDN device rules, separate mobile asset paths, firewall rules).

mobile.rendered-small-text.title: Text renders smaller than 12px on phones
mobile.rendered-small-text.why: Body text under 12 CSS pixels on a phone is hard to read without zooming. Measured from computed styles in a phone render, so it includes stylesheet rules, not only inline styles.
mobile.rendered-small-text.fix: Set body text to at least 16px on small screens (and never below 12px for secondary text) in your stylesheet.

performance.html-heavy.title: HTML document is very large
performance.html-heavy.why: A heavy HTML file is slow on mobile, and crawlers have size limits: Googlebot stops reading HTML after a fixed number of megabytes and many AI crawlers cut off far sooner.
performance.html-heavy.fix: Move inline data, SVG sprites and scripts into cached files, paginate long lists and remove unused markup.

performance.ttfb-slow.title: Slow server response (TTFB)
performance.ttfb-slow.why: Time to first byte delays everything else on the page. Slow responses also reduce how many pages crawlers fetch per visit, and AI fetchers time out.
performance.ttfb-slow.fix: Cache pages at the CDN or server, speed up database queries and keep TTFB under 800 ms.

performance.slow-download.title: HTML takes a long time to download
performance.slow-download.why: A slow complete response delays rendering and wastes crawler time, especially on heavy pages.
performance.slow-download.fix: Reduce HTML size, enable compression and stream or cache the response.

performance.no-compression.title: HTML is not compressed
performance.no-compression.why: Gzip or Brotli shrinks HTML by around 70–80%, so uncompressed pages are much slower to download for people and crawlers.
performance.no-compression.fix: Enable Brotli or gzip on the server or CDN for text/html, CSS, JavaScript, JSON and XML.

performance.render-blocking-scripts.title: Render-blocking scripts in <head>
performance.render-blocking-scripts.why: Synchronous scripts in <head> stop the browser drawing anything until they download and run, which delays First and Largest Contentful Paint.
performance.render-blocking-scripts.fix: Add defer (or async for independent scripts) to scripts in <head>, or move them to the end of <body>.

performance.render-blocking-css.title: Many stylesheets block rendering
performance.render-blocking-css.why: Every stylesheet in <head> must load before the page paints. More than 5 separate files adds round trips.
performance.render-blocking-css.fix: Combine stylesheets, inline the critical CSS and load the rest without blocking (media="print" swap or preload).

performance.too-many-scripts.title: Many external scripts
performance.too-many-scripts.why: Each script costs a request plus parse and run time on the main thread, which hurts responsiveness (INP).
performance.too-many-scripts.fix: Remove unused scripts and tags, bundle your own scripts and load third-party ones only where needed.

performance.too-many-requests.title: Page makes many requests
performance.too-many-requests.why: Lots of separate files (scripts, styles, images) slow loading on mobile networks.
performance.too-many-requests.fix: Bundle assets, lazy-load images below the fold and drop unused third-party resources.

performance.third-party-heavy.title: Scripts from many third-party hosts
performance.third-party-heavy.why: Each third-party host needs its own connection and runs code you do not control. Chat widgets, tag managers and ad scripts are the usual cause of poor INP.
performance.third-party-heavy.fix: Audit third-party tags, remove ones nobody uses and load the rest after the page is interactive.

performance.duplicate-scripts.title: Same script loaded twice
performance.duplicate-scripts.why: Loading a script twice doubles its cost and can make it run twice (double tracking, double event handlers).
performance.duplicate-scripts.fix: Remove the duplicate include. It often comes from a theme and a plugin both adding the same library.

performance.image-weight.title: Images on the page are very heavy in total
performance.image-weight.why: Total image weight drives how long a page takes on mobile data, and the biggest image is often the LCP element.
performance.image-weight.fix: Compress and resize images, serve WebP/AVIF and lazy-load below-the-fold images.

performance.script-weight.title: Large amount of JavaScript
performance.script-weight.why: JavaScript is the most expensive byte on the web: it must download, parse and run, which blocks interaction on mid-range phones.
performance.script-weight.fix: Split bundles by route, remove unused libraries and defer non-essential scripts.

performance.page-weight.title: Total page weight is high
performance.page-weight.why: Pages over a few megabytes load slowly on mobile and cost visitors data.
performance.page-weight.fix: Reduce the biggest contributors first: images, then JavaScript, then fonts and HTML.

performance.inline-script-heavy.title: Large inline scripts
performance.inline-script-heavy.why: Inline scripts are re-downloaded with every page and cannot be cached. Large hydration payloads also bloat the HTML that crawlers fetch.
performance.inline-script-heavy.fix: Move large inline scripts into external cached files and trim serialised page data.

performance.inline-style-heavy.title: Large inline styles
performance.inline-style-heavy.why: Inlining a little critical CSS helps; inlining the whole stylesheet makes every page heavier and uncacheable.
performance.inline-style-heavy.fix: Inline only above-the-fold CSS and load the rest from a cached stylesheet.

performance.unminified-inline.title: Inline code is not minified
performance.unminified-inline.why: Comments, indentation and long names in inline code add weight to every page view.
performance.unminified-inline.fix: Minify inline scripts and styles in the build step or with your CMS’s optimisation plugin.

performance.dom-size.title: Very large DOM
performance.dom-size.why: More than about 1500 elements slows style calculation and interaction, and gives AI agents reading the page a much larger tree to work through.
performance.dom-size.fix: Simplify nested wrappers, paginate long lists and render hidden menus or tabs only when opened.

performance.no-preconnect.title: Critical third-party origins without preconnect
performance.no-preconnect.why: Fonts and CSS from another origin need a new connection. preconnect starts it early and can save hundreds of milliseconds.
performance.no-preconnect.fix: Add <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin> (and for other render-critical origins).

performance.font-display.title: Web fonts may hide text while loading
performance.font-display.why: Without font-display: swap (or display=swap for Google Fonts), text stays invisible until the font arrives, which delays when people can read the page.
performance.font-display.fix: Add font-display: swap to @font-face rules, or &display=swap to the Google Fonts URL.

performance.html-no-validators.title: HTML has no caching or revalidation headers
performance.html-no-validators.why: Without Cache-Control, ETag or Last-Modified, every crawl and repeat visit downloads the full page again, and crawlers cannot ask "has this changed?".
performance.html-no-validators.fix: Send ETag or Last-Modified on HTML, and a Cache-Control policy that suits how often pages change.

performance.asset-cache-short.title: Static assets have short or no cache lifetime
performance.asset-cache-short.why: CSS, JavaScript, fonts and images that are re-downloaded on every visit slow repeat views.
performance.asset-cache-short.fix: Serve fingerprinted assets with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

performance.slow-pages-share.title: Server is slow across much of the site
performance.slow-pages-share.why: When a large share of pages respond slowly, the cause is usually server capacity or missing caching, and crawlers reduce how much of the site they fetch.
performance.slow-pages-share.fix: Add full-page caching or a CDN, and profile the slowest templates.

performance.lcp.title: Largest Contentful Paint is slow
performance.lcp.why: LCP measures when the main content appears. Google’s Core Web Vitals threshold is 2.5 s; over 4 s is poor.
performance.lcp.fix: Speed up the server response, preload and prioritise the hero image, remove render-blocking resources and serve smaller images.
performance.lcp.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.cls.title: Layout shifts while loading (CLS)
performance.cls.why: CLS measures how much content jumps around. Over 0.1 fails Core Web Vitals and causes mis-taps.
performance.cls.fix: Set width and height on images and embeds, reserve space for ads and banners, and avoid inserting content above what is already shown.
performance.cls.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.inp.title: Slow response to interactions (INP)
performance.inp.why: INP measures how quickly the page reacts to taps and clicks. Over 200 ms fails Core Web Vitals.
performance.inp.fix: Break up long JavaScript tasks, defer third-party scripts and reduce work in event handlers.
performance.inp.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.tbt.title: Main thread blocked for long periods (TBT)
performance.tbt.why: Total Blocking Time in the lab test is the best predictor of poor INP: the page cannot respond while long scripts run.
performance.tbt.fix: Reduce and split JavaScript, remove unused tags and delay non-essential scripts until after load.
performance.tbt.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.fcp.title: First Contentful Paint is slow
performance.fcp.why: FCP is when anything first appears. A slow FCP makes the page feel broken and usually points to a slow server or blocking resources.
performance.fcp.fix: Improve TTFB, inline critical CSS and defer blocking scripts.
performance.fcp.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.psi-score.title: Low Lighthouse performance score
performance.psi-score.why: The Lighthouse score summarises lab performance. Under 50 means several serious problems; it is a useful trend line rather than a ranking factor.
performance.psi-score.fix: Work through the PageSpeed Insights opportunities for this URL, starting with the biggest savings.
performance.psi-score.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.psi-opportunities.title: Large savings available according to PageSpeed Insights
performance.psi-opportunities.why: Lighthouse estimates how much time each fix would save. These are the most valuable changes for this page.
performance.psi-opportunities.fix: Start with the opportunities listed with the largest savings.
performance.psi-opportunities.skippedReason: Needs PageSpeed Insights data. Add a PSI API key with `avc connect psi`.

performance.rendered-lcp.title: Slow LCP in a local browser test
performance.rendered-lcp.why: In a real browser run, the main content took longer than 2.5 s to appear. This is a lab measurement from your machine, so treat it as a pointer rather than field data.
performance.rendered-lcp.fix: Check the page in PageSpeed Insights, then optimise the largest element (usually the hero image or heading font).

performance.rendered-cls.title: Layout shift in a local browser test
performance.rendered-cls.why: Content moved after it first appeared during the render. Shifts after load also confuse AI agents that click on elements.
performance.rendered-cls.fix: Reserve space for images, embeds, banners and late-loading fonts.

performance.rendered-tbt.title: Long main-thread blocking in a local browser test
performance.rendered-tbt.why: Long tasks during load mean taps and clicks are ignored for a while.
performance.rendered-tbt.fix: Reduce JavaScript run on load; split and defer bundles.

performance.rendered-load-slow.title: Page takes a long time to finish loading
performance.rendered-load-slow.why: A slow load event means the page keeps fetching resources for a long time, which keeps spinners going and delays analytics and agent interaction.
performance.rendered-load-slow.fix: Lazy-load below-the-fold media and delay third-party embeds until they are needed.

performance.unminified-assets.title: CSS or JavaScript files are not minified
performance.unminified-assets.why: Indentation, comments and long names in CSS and JavaScript files add bytes every visitor downloads before the page can render. Minified files are typically 20–40% smaller before compression.
performance.unminified-assets.fix: Minify CSS and JavaScript in your build (most bundlers do this in production mode) or turn on minification in your CMS, cache plugin or CDN.

security.not-https.title: Page served over plain HTTP
security.not-https.why: HTTPS is a Google ranking signal and browsers mark HTTP pages "Not secure". Many AI agents and browsers refuse to submit forms over HTTP.
security.not-https.fix: Serve the site over HTTPS with a valid certificate and 301-redirect every HTTP URL to its HTTPS version.

security.mixed-content.title: HTTPS page loads HTTP resources
security.mixed-content.why: Browsers block insecure scripts and styles on HTTPS pages (breaking the page) and warn about insecure images.
security.mixed-content.fix: Change resource URLs to https:// (or protocol-relative to root paths). Add "Content-Security-Policy: upgrade-insecure-requests" as a safety net.

security.insecure-form.title: Form submits over HTTP
security.insecure-form.why: A form that posts to http:// sends what people type in clear text. Browsers warn users and agents should refuse to submit it.
security.insecure-form.fix: Point the form action at an https:// URL (or a relative path on an HTTPS page).

security.protocol-relative.title: Protocol-relative resource URLs
security.protocol-relative.why: "//host/file.js" URLs inherit the page protocol. On an HTTPS site that is harmless but outdated; if a copy of the page is ever served over HTTP, the resources load insecurely too.

security.cookie-not-secure.title: Cookies set without the Secure flag
security.cookie-not-secure.why: On an HTTPS site, cookies without Secure can be sent over an HTTP request and intercepted. SameSite=None cookies without Secure are rejected by browsers.
security.cookie-not-secure.fix: Add Secure to every cookie the site sets (and HttpOnly to session cookies).

security.cookie-not-httponly.title: Session cookie readable by JavaScript
security.cookie-not-httponly.why: Session cookies without HttpOnly can be stolen by any injected script.
security.cookie-not-httponly.fix: Add HttpOnly to session and authentication cookies.

security.debug-output.title: Server errors or debug output shown on the page
security.debug-output.why: PHP warnings, stack traces and debug dumps leak file paths and versions to attackers, and crawlers index them as page content.
security.debug-output.fix: Turn off display of errors in production (for example WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY false, display_errors Off) and log them instead. Fix the underlying error.

security.directory-listing.title: Directory listing enabled
security.directory-listing.why: An "Index of /" page exposes every file in a folder, including backups and files you never linked.
security.directory-listing.fix: Disable directory listing (Options -Indexes in Apache, autoindex off in nginx) and add an index file.

security.sri-missing.title: CDN scripts loaded without integrity checks
security.sri-missing.why: If a public CDN file is tampered with, every site loading it runs the attacker’s code. Subresource Integrity makes the browser refuse a changed file.
security.sri-missing.fix: Add integrity="sha384-…" and crossorigin="anonymous" to scripts loaded from public CDNs at fixed versions.

security.hsts-missing.title: No HSTS header
security.hsts-missing.why: Strict-Transport-Security tells browsers to always use HTTPS, closing the window where a first HTTP request can be intercepted.
security.hsts-missing.fix: Send "Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" on HTTPS responses once every subdomain supports HTTPS.

security.hsts-short.title: HSTS max-age is short
security.hsts-short.why: A max-age under about six months gives little protection between visits and does not qualify for browser preload lists.
security.hsts-short.fix: Raise max-age to at least 31536000 (one year).

security.csp-missing.title: No Content-Security-Policy
security.csp-missing.why: A CSP limits where scripts can load from, which blunts cross-site scripting and injected malware that could otherwise hijack pages and their rankings.
security.csp-missing.fix: Start with a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header, review reports, then enforce it.

security.csp-unsafe.title: CSP allows unsafe inline scripts or eval
security.csp-unsafe.why: 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in script-src remove most of the protection a CSP gives against injected scripts.
security.csp-unsafe.fix: Use nonces or hashes for inline scripts and remove 'unsafe-eval'. Keep 'unsafe-inline' only as a fallback alongside a nonce or 'strict-dynamic'.

security.nosniff-missing.title: No X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
security.nosniff-missing.why: Without nosniff, browsers may guess a file’s type and run an uploaded file as a script.

security.frame-protection-missing.title: Pages can be framed by any site
security.frame-protection-missing.why: Without X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, other sites can embed your pages invisibly and trick people into clicking (clickjacking).

security.referrer-policy-missing.title: No Referrer-Policy
security.referrer-policy-missing.why: Browsers now default to a safe referrer policy, but an explicit one guarantees full URLs (which can contain tokens or search terms) are not leaked to other sites.

security.version-disclosure.title: Server software versions exposed in headers
security.version-disclosure.why: Headers such as "Server: Apache/2.4.29" or "X-Powered-By: PHP/7.2" tell attackers exactly which known vulnerabilities to try.
security.version-disclosure.fix: Hide version numbers (ServerTokens Prod, server_tokens off, expose_php Off) and remove X-Powered-By.

security.exposed-files.title: Sensitive files are publicly readable
security.exposed-files.why: An exposed .git folder or .env file can reveal source code, passwords and API keys. Automated scanners look for these constantly.
security.exposed-files.fix: Block access to dotfiles at the server or CDN (deny /\.(git|env)), remove the files from the web root and rotate any secrets they contained.

security.http-pages.title: Some pages still served over HTTP
security.http-pages.why: On an HTTPS site, internal pages that load over http:// are duplicates and show browser warnings.
security.http-pages.fix: Redirect all http:// URLs to https:// and update internal links.

security.tls-expired.title: TLS certificate has expired
security.tls-expired.why: Browsers show a full-page security warning for an expired certificate, most visitors leave, and crawlers may stop fetching the site. AI agents and search bots treat it as an error.
security.tls-expired.fix: Renew the certificate now (or fix the automatic renewal of your Let’s Encrypt / host certificate) and reload the web server.

security.tls-expiring.title: TLS certificate expires soon
security.tls-expiring.why: When the certificate runs out, the whole site shows a security warning. Automatic renewal usually happens about 30 days before expiry, so a certificate this close to the end suggests renewal is failing.
security.tls-expiring.fix: Check the automatic renewal (certbot, your host or CDN dashboard) and renew now. Add a monitor for certificate expiry.

security.tls-invalid.title: Browsers do not trust the TLS certificate
security.tls-invalid.why: A certificate for the wrong host name, a self-signed certificate or a missing intermediate certificate makes browsers, crawlers and AI agents refuse the connection or warn visitors.
security.tls-invalid.fix: Install a certificate that covers this host name, with the full chain (leaf plus intermediates). SSL Labs’ server test shows exactly what is wrong.

urls.uppercase.title: URL contains upper-case letters
urls.uppercase.why: URLs are case-sensitive. Mixed case invites people and other sites to link to the wrong variant, creating duplicates or 404s.
urls.uppercase.fix: Use lower-case URLs and 301-redirect upper-case variants to them.

urls.underscores.title: Underscores used to separate words
urls.underscores.why: Google recommends hyphens between words in URLs. Underscores can be read as joining words together.
urls.underscores.fix: Use hyphens in new URLs. Change existing ones only with 301 redirects, and only when it is worth the effort.

urls.too-long.title: Very long URL
urls.too-long.why: Long URLs are hard to share, are truncated in results and often contain repeated or stuffed words.
urls.too-long.fix: Keep URLs short and readable (under about 115 characters) for new pages.

urls.unsafe-characters.title: Spaces or unsafe characters in the URL
urls.unsafe-characters.why: Spaces (%20) and characters like commas, quotes or brackets break when URLs are copied, shared or parsed by other tools.
urls.unsafe-characters.fix: Use only lower-case letters, numbers and hyphens in paths.

urls.double-slash.title: Double slash in the path
urls.double-slash.why: "//" in a path is usually a templating mistake and creates a duplicate of the single-slash URL.
urls.double-slash.fix: Fix the link template and redirect // URLs to the single-slash version.

urls.repeated-segment.title: Repeated folder in the URL
urls.repeated-segment.why: Paths like /blog/blog/ usually come from relative links resolving wrongly and can create endless crawl loops.
urls.repeated-segment.fix: Use root-relative (/blog/post) or absolute links in templates and fix the link that produced this URL.

urls.session-id.title: Session ID in the URL
urls.session-id.why: Session IDs give every visit a new URL, so crawlers see endless duplicates and links shared by users can leak sessions.
urls.session-id.fix: Keep sessions in cookies, not URLs, and strip session parameters from links.

urls.tracking-parameters.title: Indexable URL with tracking parameters
urls.tracking-parameters.why: URLs with utm_, gclid or fbclid parameters that are indexable and self-canonical become duplicates of the clean page.
urls.tracking-parameters.fix: Make parameter URLs canonicalise to the clean URL, and stop linking to tracked URLs internally.

urls.many-parameters.title: Indexable URL with many parameters
urls.many-parameters.why: URLs with more than 3 parameters are usually filter combinations. They multiply into huge numbers of near-duplicate pages.
urls.many-parameters.fix: Canonicalise filter combinations to the main category page, or noindex them, and avoid plain links to deep filter states.

urls.deep-path.title: Deeply nested URL path
urls.deep-path.why: Many folder levels make URLs long and often mirror an over-complicated site structure.
urls.deep-path.fix: Keep new URLs within about 5 folder levels.

urls.non-descriptive.title: URL has no readable words
urls.non-descriptive.why: IDs like ?p=123 or /node/456 tell people and AI engines nothing about the page; readable slugs are clearer when shared and cited.
urls.non-descriptive.fix: Enable readable permalinks (for example /services/seo-audit/) and redirect the ID URLs to them.

urls.internal-search-indexable.title: Internal search results are indexable
urls.internal-search-indexable.why: Search result pages are endless, thin and duplicate. Google advises keeping them out of the index; they waste crawl budget and can be abused for spam.
urls.internal-search-indexable.fix: Add noindex to search result pages and stop linking to them; optionally disallow the search path in robots.txt.

urls.index-file.title: URL ends in index.html or index.php
urls.index-file.why: /folder/index.html and /folder/ are two URLs for one page. Linking to the index file splits signals.
urls.index-file.fix: Link to the folder URL and redirect the index file URL to it.

urls.case-duplicates.title: URLs that differ only by letter case
urls.case-duplicates.why: Two crawled URLs that differ only in capitals are duplicates of each other.
urls.case-duplicates.fix: Redirect the mixed-case URL to the lower-case one and correct the links.

urls.trailing-slash-mixed.title: Mixed trailing-slash style
urls.trailing-slash-mixed.why: Using both /page and /folder/ styles across the site makes it easy to link to the wrong form and create redirects or duplicates.
urls.trailing-slash-mixed.fix: Pick one convention for page URLs and enforce it with redirects and consistent links.

sitemaps.missing.title: No XML sitemap found
sitemaps.missing.why: A sitemap lists every page you want indexed with its last change date. It is how search engines and AI crawlers find new and deep pages quickly.
sitemaps.missing.fix: Generate an XML sitemap of indexable, canonical URLs (most CMSs and frameworks can), publish it at /sitemap.xml and list it in robots.txt.

sitemaps.not-in-robots.title: Sitemap not declared in robots.txt
sitemaps.not-in-robots.why: Crawlers that do not use webmaster tools (Bing without an account, AI crawlers) find sitemaps through the robots.txt Sitemap line.

sitemaps.unreachable.title: Declared sitemap cannot be fetched
sitemaps.unreachable.why: A sitemap listed in robots.txt (or a sitemap index) that returns an error gives crawlers nothing, and Search Console reports it as failed.
sitemaps.unreachable.fix: Fix the sitemap URL or the server error, or remove the stale reference.

sitemaps.parse-errors.title: Sitemap has XML or format errors
sitemaps.parse-errors.why: Malformed XML, wrong namespaces or invalid entries can make search engines reject part or all of the sitemap.
sitemaps.parse-errors.fix: Fix the errors shown. Escape &, <, > in URLs, use the sitemaps.org namespace and UTF-8 encoding.

sitemaps.empty.title: Sitemap lists no URLs
sitemaps.empty.why: An empty sitemap usually means a generator failed or is filtering out every page.
sitemaps.empty.fix: Check the sitemap generator settings and make sure published pages are included.

sitemaps.too-large.title: Sitemap exceeds the size limits
sitemaps.too-large.why: A single sitemap may hold at most 50,000 URLs and 50 MB uncompressed. Larger files are rejected.
sitemaps.too-large.fix: Split it into several sitemaps and list them in a sitemap index.

sitemaps.error-urls.title: Sitemap lists URLs that return errors
sitemaps.error-urls.why: Sitemaps should only list live pages. Error URLs waste crawl visits and make search engines trust the sitemap less.
sitemaps.error-urls.fix: Remove 4xx/5xx URLs from the sitemap (most generators do this automatically once the page is deleted or unpublished).

sitemaps.redirect-urls.title: Sitemap lists redirecting URLs
sitemaps.redirect-urls.why: Sitemaps should list final URLs. Redirects in the sitemap send mixed signals about which URL is canonical.
sitemaps.redirect-urls.fix: Replace each redirecting URL with its destination.

sitemaps.noindex-urls.title: Sitemap lists noindex pages
sitemaps.noindex-urls.why: Listing a page in the sitemap says "index this", while noindex says the opposite. Search Console flags these as errors.
sitemaps.noindex-urls.fix: Remove noindex pages from the sitemap, or remove noindex if they should be indexed.

sitemaps.canonicalised-urls.title: Sitemap lists non-canonical URLs
sitemaps.canonicalised-urls.why: Sitemaps act as a canonical hint. Listing URLs that canonicalise elsewhere contradicts your own canonical tags.
sitemaps.canonicalised-urls.fix: List only the canonical version of each page.

sitemaps.blocked-urls.title: Sitemap lists URLs blocked by robots.txt
sitemaps.blocked-urls.why: Search engines cannot crawl these URLs, so listing them only produces "submitted URL blocked" errors.
sitemaps.blocked-urls.fix: Remove blocked URLs from the sitemap, or allow them in robots.txt.

sitemaps.foreign-urls.title: Sitemap lists URLs on another host or protocol
sitemaps.foreign-urls.why: A sitemap may only list URLs on its own host and protocol (unless cross-submission is verified). Others are ignored.
sitemaps.foreign-urls.fix: Use the live protocol and host (for example https://www.) for every URL in the sitemap.

sitemaps.duplicate-urls.title: Same URL listed more than once
sitemaps.duplicate-urls.why: Duplicate entries add noise and often come from two generators writing the same sitemap.

sitemaps.indexable-missing.title: Indexable pages missing from the sitemap
sitemaps.indexable-missing.why: Pages left out of the sitemap rely only on links to be found and do not get lastmod hints, so updates are picked up more slowly.
sitemaps.indexable-missing.fix: Include every indexable, canonical page in the sitemap. Check the generator’s post-type and taxonomy settings.

sitemaps.lastmod-invalid.title: Invalid lastmod dates
sitemaps.lastmod-invalid.why: lastmod must be in W3C datetime format (2025-05-01 or 2025-05-01T09:00:00+00:00). Invalid values are ignored.
sitemaps.lastmod-invalid.fix: Output lastmod in W3C datetime format.

sitemaps.lastmod-future.title: lastmod dates in the future
sitemaps.lastmod-future.why: Future dates are clearly wrong, and Google says it ignores lastmod from sitemaps where the values are not consistently accurate.
sitemaps.lastmod-future.fix: Set lastmod to when the page content last changed meaningfully, with the correct timezone.

sitemaps.lastmod-uniform.title: Every URL has the same lastmod
sitemaps.lastmod-uniform.why: When all entries share one timestamp, the generator is stamping the build time rather than real changes. Search engines learn to ignore it.
sitemaps.lastmod-uniform.fix: Use each page’s real last-modified date (from the CMS or file history) for lastmod.

sitemaps.lastmod-missing.title: Sitemap has no lastmod dates
sitemaps.lastmod-missing.why: Google and Bing use accurate lastmod values to decide what to recrawl. Without them, updated pages wait longer to be refreshed.
sitemaps.lastmod-missing.fix: Add a lastmod to each URL with the date its content last changed.

sitemaps.stale.title: Sitemap has not changed in over a year
sitemaps.stale.why: If the newest lastmod is more than a year old while the site has been updated, the sitemap is probably not being regenerated.
sitemaps.stale.fix: Regenerate the sitemap automatically on publish, or on a schedule.

sitemaps.no-image-entries.title: Content images are not listed in the sitemap
sitemaps.no-image-entries.why: Image sitemap entries help Google find images that are loaded by JavaScript or sit on pages it rarely recrawls, so product and project photos can appear in image search and AI answers with images.
sitemaps.no-image-entries.fix: Add <image:image><image:loc>…</image:loc></image:image> entries for the main images of each page (most SEO plugins and e-commerce platforms have a setting for this).

pagination.canonical-to-first.title: Page 2+ canonicalises to page 1
pagination.canonical-to-first.why: Each page in a series lists different items. Canonicalising them all to page 1 tells search engines to ignore those items, so products or posts further down are discovered less.
pagination.canonical-to-first.fix: Give each paginated page a self-referencing canonical (or canonicalise to a view-all page if one exists).

pagination.noindex.title: Paginated pages are noindex
pagination.noindex.why: Noindex on page 2+ is allowed, but over time Google may stop following links on noindex pages, so items listed only there can become hard to reach.
pagination.noindex.fix: Let paginated pages be indexed with self-canonicals, or make sure every item is also linked from somewhere indexable.

pagination.next-broken.title: rel="next" or rel="prev" points to an error
pagination.next-broken.why: Broken pagination links stop crawlers walking the series, and Bing still uses these hints.
pagination.next-broken.fix: Point rel next/prev at live pages, and omit rel="next" on the last page.

pagination.sequence-mismatch.title: rel="next" target does not point back with rel="prev"
pagination.sequence-mismatch.why: When page 2 does not name page 1 as prev, the series is inconsistent and crawlers may not treat it as one sequence.
pagination.sequence-mismatch.fix: Make each next page declare the current page as its rel="prev".

pagination.multiple-rel.title: Several rel="next" or rel="prev" tags
pagination.multiple-rel.why: A page can only have one next and one previous page. Duplicates make the sequence ambiguous.
pagination.multiple-rel.fix: Keep one rel="next" and one rel="prev" per page.

pagination.page-one-duplicate.title: Links to "page 1" create a duplicate URL
pagination.page-one-duplicate.why: Linking to ?page=1 or /page/1/ creates a second URL for the first page of a series.
pagination.page-one-duplicate.fix: Link to the clean URL for page 1, and redirect ?page=1 and /page/1/ to it.

pagination.load-more-only.title: "Load more" or infinite scroll without page links
pagination.load-more-only.why: Crawlers do not click buttons or scroll. Items loaded only by "load more" or infinite scroll are invisible unless there are plain paginated links too.
pagination.load-more-only.fix: Back the button with real <a href="?page=2"> links (the button can enhance them with JavaScript).

pagination.fragment.title: Pagination uses # fragments
pagination.fragment.why: Search engines ignore everything after #, so "#page=2" pages are never crawled as separate pages.
pagination.fragment.fix: Use query parameters (?page=2) or paths (/page/2/) for paginated pages.

pagination.out-of-range-200.title: Out-of-range page numbers return 200
pagination.out-of-range-200.why: If ?page=9999 returns an empty page with status 200, crawlers can generate endless empty pages that look like soft 404s.
pagination.out-of-range-200.fix: Return 404 for page numbers beyond the last page.

pagination.deep-series.title: Long paginated list with no shortcut to deep pages
pagination.deep-series.why: When page 1 only links to page 2, an item on page 10 is ten or more clicks deep. Crawlers reach it late or not at all, and it gets little internal link value. Jump links, a view-all page or category splits shorten the path.
pagination.deep-series.fix: Link to more page numbers from each list page (1 2 3 … 10 … last), add sub-categories or filters with crawlable URLs, or offer a view-all page for lists that load fast enough.

accessibility.lang-missing.title: Page language not declared
accessibility.lang-missing.why: Without <html lang>, screen readers guess the pronunciation and translation tools and AI engines may misjudge the page language.
accessibility.lang-missing.fix: Add the language to the root element, for example <html lang="en-GB">.

accessibility.lang-invalid.title: Invalid page language code
accessibility.lang-invalid.why: An invalid lang value (such as "english" or "en_UK") is ignored by assistive technology and parsers.
accessibility.lang-invalid.fix: Use a valid BCP 47 code: en, en-GB, fr-CA, zh-Hant.

accessibility.form-label-missing.title: Form fields without labels
accessibility.form-label-missing.why: Fields without a label are announced as "edit text" with no purpose. AI agents filling forms rely on the same labels to know what goes where.
accessibility.form-label-missing.fix: Give every field a visible <label for="…">, or aria-label / aria-labelledby when a visible label is not possible. Placeholders do not count.

accessibility.link-name-missing.title: Links without an accessible name
accessibility.link-name-missing.why: An icon or image link with no text or alt is announced as just "link". Search engines and AI agents also get no anchor text for it.
accessibility.link-name-missing.fix: Add text, an aria-label, or alt text on the image inside the link that says where it goes.

accessibility.button-name-missing.title: Buttons without an accessible name
accessibility.button-name-missing.why: Icon-only buttons with no label are announced as "button". Agents trying to act on the page cannot tell "search" from "close".
accessibility.button-name-missing.fix: Add visible text or an aria-label to each button (and alt text to input type="image").

accessibility.clickable-div.title: Clickable elements that are not buttons or links
accessibility.clickable-div.why: A <div> or <span> with an onclick handler cannot be reached by keyboard and is invisible as a control to screen readers and AI agents.
accessibility.clickable-div.fix: Use <button> for actions and <a href> for navigation. If you must keep the element, add role, tabindex="0" and keyboard handlers.

accessibility.main-landmark-missing.title: No main landmark
accessibility.main-landmark-missing.why: A <main> element lets screen-reader users jump straight to the content, and helps parsers and agents separate content from navigation.
accessibility.main-landmark-missing.fix: Wrap the primary content in a single <main> element.

accessibility.main-landmark-multiple.title: More than one main landmark
accessibility.main-landmark-multiple.why: A page should have one visible main region. Several confuse landmark navigation and content extraction.
accessibility.main-landmark-multiple.fix: Keep one <main> and use <section> or <article> for the other regions.

accessibility.skip-link-missing.title: No skip link before a long navigation
accessibility.skip-link-missing.why: Keyboard users have to tab through every menu item on every page without a "skip to content" link.
accessibility.skip-link-missing.fix: Add a "Skip to main content" link as the first focusable element, pointing to the id of <main>.

accessibility.duplicate-ids.title: Duplicate id attributes
accessibility.duplicate-ids.why: Labels, aria-labelledby and in-page links point at ids. When an id is used twice, they may point at the wrong element.
accessibility.duplicate-ids.fix: Make every id unique on the page (components rendered more than once often repeat them).

accessibility.positive-tabindex.title: Positive tabindex values
accessibility.positive-tabindex.why: tabindex above 0 changes the keyboard order away from the visual order, which disorients keyboard and switch users.
accessibility.positive-tabindex.fix: Use tabindex="0" or "-1" only, and order elements in the HTML the way they should be reached.

accessibility.iframe-title-missing.title: Iframes without a title
accessibility.iframe-title-missing.why: Screen readers announce iframes by their title. Without one, users cannot tell a video from a map or a form.
accessibility.iframe-title-missing.fix: Add a short title to each iframe, for example title="Map of our office".

accessibility.autoplay-audio.title: Media that plays sound automatically
accessibility.autoplay-audio.why: Audio that starts on its own talks over screen readers and startles visitors. Browsers usually block it anyway.
accessibility.autoplay-audio.fix: Remove autoplay, or add muted and provide visible controls.

accessibility.video-captions-missing.title: Videos without captions
accessibility.video-captions-missing.why: Captions are needed by deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors, and give search and AI engines the spoken content as text.
accessibility.video-captions-missing.fix: Add <track kind="captions"> to self-hosted videos, and publish a transcript on the page.

accessibility.aria-hidden-focusable.title: Focusable elements hidden from assistive technology
accessibility.aria-hidden-focusable.why: Links or buttons inside aria-hidden="true" can still receive keyboard focus, but screen readers announce nothing, so users land on a silent control.
accessibility.aria-hidden-focusable.fix: Remove aria-hidden from containers with interactive content, or add tabindex="-1"/inert to the controls inside.

accessibility.invalid-role.title: Unknown ARIA role values
accessibility.invalid-role.why: An invalid role is ignored, so the element is exposed as something else and assistive technology and agents misread it.
accessibility.invalid-role.fix: Use a valid WAI-ARIA role, or better, the native HTML element.

accessibility.invalid-aria-attribute.title: Misspelled or unknown aria-* attributes
accessibility.invalid-aria-attribute.why: An aria attribute that does not exist (aria-labeledby, aria-role) does nothing, so the label or state you intended is never exposed.
accessibility.invalid-aria-attribute.fix: Correct the attribute name (for example aria-labelledby, with two Ls).

accessibility.broken-aria-reference.title: Labels or ARIA references point at missing ids
accessibility.broken-aria-reference.why: label for, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby must reference an existing id. Broken references leave the control unnamed.
accessibility.broken-aria-reference.fix: Make the referenced ids exist, or point the attribute at the right element.

accessibility.svg-no-name.title: Meaningful SVG images without a name
accessibility.svg-no-name.why: An SVG marked role="img" needs a <title> or aria-label, or it is announced as an unnamed image.
accessibility.svg-no-name.fix: Add aria-label or a <title> child to SVGs with role="img"; add aria-hidden="true" to decorative ones.

accessibility.table-headers-missing.title: Data tables without header cells
accessibility.table-headers-missing.why: Without <th>, screen readers cannot say which column or row a value belongs to, and AI engines lose the structure of the data.
accessibility.table-headers-missing.fix: Mark header cells with <th> (and scope="col"/"row" where needed). Use CSS, not tables, for layout.

accessibility.list-structure.title: List items outside a list
accessibility.list-structure.why: <li> elements must sit inside <ul>, <ol> or <menu>. Stray items break the list semantics screen readers announce.
accessibility.list-structure.fix: Wrap list items in a <ul> or <ol>.

accessibility.obsolete-motion.title: Blinking or scrolling text elements
accessibility.obsolete-motion.why: <marquee> and <blink> move content that users cannot pause, which fails WCAG and distracts people with attention or vestibular conditions.
accessibility.obsolete-motion.fix: Replace them with static text, or CSS animation that respects prefers-reduced-motion and can be paused.

accessibility.low-contrast-inline.title: Low colour contrast in inline styles
accessibility.low-contrast-inline.why: Text below a 4.5:1 contrast ratio with its background is hard to read for many people. This check only sees colours set inline in the HTML.
accessibility.low-contrast-inline.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio is at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

accessibility.role-nesting.title: ARIA roles used outside their required parent
accessibility.role-nesting.why: Roles such as tab, option, menuitem and row only work inside their container role (tablist, listbox, menu, table). Out of place, screen readers and AI agents that read the accessibility tree cannot tell what the control belongs to.
accessibility.role-nesting.fix: Wrap the elements in the container role (for example role="tablist" around role="tab"), or remove the role if the element is not that kind of control.

accessibility.low-contrast-rendered.title: Low colour contrast in the rendered page
accessibility.low-contrast-rendered.why: Text below 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for large text) is hard to read for many people and in bright light. Measured from the computed colours in a browser render, including stylesheets, not only inline styles.
accessibility.low-contrast-rendered.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background in your stylesheet until each listed sample reaches 4.5:1 (3:1 for text of 24px, or 18.66px bold, and larger).

js-rendering.client-only.title: Content only appears after JavaScript runs
js-rendering.client-only.why: The raw HTML is almost empty and the content is built in the browser. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and most other AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they see a blank page.
js-rendering.client-only.fix: Render the page on the server or pre-render it at build time (SSR/SSG), so the HTML response already contains the text, links and headings.

js-rendering.content-gap.title: Much of the content depends on JavaScript
js-rendering.content-gap.why: A large share of the text is added by JavaScript. Crawlers that read only the HTML response, including most AI crawlers, miss it.
js-rendering.content-gap.fix: Server-render the main content (descriptions, FAQs, reviews, specs). Keep JavaScript for interactivity.

js-rendering.content-removed.title: JavaScript removes content after load
js-rendering.content-removed.why: The rendered page has far less text than the HTML. Google indexes the rendered version, so content may vanish from search, often because of a client-side error or a consent wall.
js-rendering.content-removed.fix: Check the console errors for this page and make sure hydration does not replace server content with an empty or error state.

js-rendering.links-only-rendered.title: Links added only by JavaScript
js-rendering.links-only-rendered.why: Crawlers that do not render cannot follow links that are inserted by JavaScript, so the pages they lead to may never be discovered.
js-rendering.links-only-rendered.fix: Output navigation and content links as <a href> in the server HTML.

js-rendering.title-changed.title: JavaScript changes or adds the title
js-rendering.title-changed.why: Non-rendering crawlers see the raw title, Google may see the rendered one. Different titles send mixed signals, and a missing raw title leaves AI crawlers with none.
js-rendering.title-changed.fix: Output the final title in the server HTML (for example with your framework’s metadata API).

js-rendering.h1-only-rendered.title: H1 appears only after JavaScript
js-rendering.h1-only-rendered.why: Crawlers reading the HTML response see a page with no main heading.
js-rendering.h1-only-rendered.fix: Render the H1 on the server.

js-rendering.schema-only-rendered.title: Structured data added only by JavaScript
js-rendering.schema-only-rendered.why: Google can read JSON-LD injected by JavaScript, but most other consumers, including AI crawlers and many SEO tools, cannot.
js-rendering.schema-only-rendered.fix: Output JSON-LD in the server HTML (Google Tag Manager–injected schema is the usual culprit).

js-rendering.canonical-changed.title: JavaScript changes the canonical
js-rendering.canonical-changed.why: Google warns against changing the canonical with JavaScript: it may use either value, and non-rendering crawlers only see the original.
js-rendering.canonical-changed.fix: Set the correct canonical in the server HTML and do not modify it client-side.

js-rendering.robots-changed.title: JavaScript changes the robots meta tag
js-rendering.robots-changed.why: If the raw HTML says noindex, Google may not render the page at all, so removing it with JavaScript does not work. Adding noindex with JavaScript hides the page from Google but not from other crawlers.
js-rendering.robots-changed.fix: Set the robots directive in the server response only.

js-rendering.description-changed.title: JavaScript changes the meta description
js-rendering.description-changed.why: Different raw and rendered descriptions mean different crawlers show different snippets.
js-rendering.description-changed.fix: Output the final meta description in the server HTML.

js-rendering.console-errors.title: JavaScript errors while rendering
js-rendering.console-errors.why: Script errors can stop content, links or structured data from appearing in the rendered page that Google indexes, and break the page for visitors and AI agents.
js-rendering.console-errors.fix: Open the page with the browser console and fix the errors listed.

js-rendering.failed-requests.title: Resources failed to load during rendering
js-rendering.failed-requests.why: Failed scripts, styles or API calls can leave the rendered page incomplete. If an API is blocked for bots, crawlers get the broken version.
js-rendering.failed-requests.fix: Fix or remove the failing requests; make sure APIs the page needs are not blocked by robots.txt or bot protection.

analytics.inventory.title: Analytics and tracking tools detected
analytics.inventory.why: Knowing which tags run on the site helps you plan how to measure traffic from AI assistants and keep third-party scripts under control.
analytics.inventory.fix: Check the list matches what you expect; remove tools nobody uses.

analytics.none.title: No analytics detected
analytics.none.why: Without analytics you cannot see visits referred by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Copilot, or tell whether SEO changes worked.
analytics.none.fix: Add an analytics tool (GA4, or a privacy-friendly one such as Plausible or Fathom) and set up a channel for AI assistant referrals.

analytics.duplicate-ga4.title: Same GA4 measurement ID loaded twice
analytics.duplicate-ga4.why: Loading the same GA4 property twice (often once directly and once through Tag Manager) double-counts page views and halves the bounce rate.
analytics.duplicate-ga4.fix: Load GA4 once: either the gtag snippet or the Tag Manager tag, not both.

analytics.duplicate-gtm.title: Same Tag Manager container loaded twice
analytics.duplicate-gtm.why: A duplicated GTM container fires every tag twice: double page views, double conversions and slower pages.
analytics.duplicate-gtm.fix: Remove the second container snippet (often one is in the theme and one in a plugin).

analytics.multiple-ga4-properties.title: Several GA4 properties on one page
analytics.multiple-ga4-properties.why: More than one GA4 ID is sometimes intended (agency plus client), but often a leftover from an old property that still receives data.
analytics.multiple-ga4-properties.fix: Confirm each GA4 property is in use and remove the ones that are not.

analytics.universal-analytics.title: Retired Universal Analytics code still on the site
analytics.universal-analytics.why: Universal Analytics stopped processing data in 2023 (2024 for 360). The script still loads and costs performance, but records nothing.
analytics.universal-analytics.fix: Remove the analytics.js / ga.js snippet and UA- IDs, and make sure GA4 (or another tool) is in place.

analytics.inconsistent.title: Analytics missing on some pages
analytics.inconsistent.why: If some templates lack the tag, visits to those pages (and the AI referrals landing on them) are not counted.
analytics.inconsistent.fix: Add the analytics tag to the shared layout so every template includes it.

analytics.consent-not-detected.title: Tracking tags without a detectable consent tool
analytics.consent-not-detected.why: In the UK, EU and several other places, non-essential tracking cookies need prior consent. No consent manager was found in the HTML.
analytics.consent-not-detected.fix: If you have visitors from regions that require consent, add a consent banner and Google Consent Mode, or switch to cookie-less analytics.

analytics.gtm-noscript-misplaced.title: Tag Manager noscript iframe placed in <head>
analytics.gtm-noscript-misplaced.why: The GTM <noscript><iframe> belongs right after <body>. In <head> it ends the head early, which can make Google ignore tags after it (canonical, hreflang, robots).
analytics.gtm-noscript-misplaced.fix: Move the GTM noscript snippet to immediately after the opening <body> tag.

analytics.verification-missing.title: No search engine verification tags on the home page
analytics.verification-missing.why: Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools show indexing problems, queries and (for Bing) Copilot data. No verification tag was found; DNS verification would not be visible here.
analytics.verification-missing.fix: Verify the site in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools (DNS verification is best; a meta tag works too).

analytics.no-ai-referrals.title: No AI assistant visits recorded in GA4
analytics.no-ai-referrals.why: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot send visitors with a referrer or utm_source. If GA4 shows none in the period, either no assistant links to you yet or the visits are lumped into Direct or Referral, so you cannot see whether AI visibility work pays off.
analytics.no-ai-referrals.fix: In GA4, create a custom channel group with an "AI assistants" channel (source matches chatgpt|perplexity|gemini|claude|copilot) placed above Referral. Then track AI visibility (`avc visibility`) to see whether assistants name you.
analytics.no-ai-referrals.skippedReason: Needs Google Analytics 4. Connect it with `avc connect google`.

cms.wp-version-exposed.title: WordPress version is published
cms.wp-version-exposed.why: The generator tag and ?ver= query strings tell anyone exactly which WordPress version you run, which makes targeting known vulnerabilities easy.
cms.wp-version-exposed.fix: Remove the generator meta tag (remove_action('wp_head', 'wp_generator') or your security plugin) and keep WordPress updated.

cms.wp-readme-exposed.title: WordPress readme.html is public
cms.wp-readme-exposed.why: The default readme.html confirms the site runs WordPress and, in older versions, its version number.
cms.wp-readme-exposed.fix: Delete readme.html and license.txt from the web root (they return after updates; block them at the server instead).

cms.wp-xmlrpc-enabled.title: XML-RPC endpoint is enabled
cms.wp-xmlrpc-enabled.why: xmlrpc.php is a common target for password-guessing and DDoS amplification. Few sites still need it.
cms.wp-xmlrpc-enabled.fix: Disable XML-RPC (security plugin or a server rule denying /xmlrpc.php) unless Jetpack or the mobile app needs it.

cms.wp-user-enumeration.title: Usernames can be listed through ?author=
cms.wp-user-enumeration.why: Requesting /?author=1 redirects to /author/<username>/, giving attackers half of a login.
cms.wp-user-enumeration.fix: Block ?author= requests for visitors who are not logged in (most security plugins have a switch), and use display names that differ from usernames.

cms.wp-rest-users-exposed.title: REST API lists user accounts
cms.wp-rest-users-exposed.why: /wp-json/wp/v2/users returns usernames (slugs) of everyone who has published, which helps attackers guess logins.
cms.wp-rest-users-exposed.fix: Restrict the users endpoint to authenticated requests (security plugin or a rest_endpoints filter).

cms.wp-attachment-page.title: Media attachment pages are indexable
cms.wp-attachment-page.why: WordPress creates a thin page for every uploaded image. Indexed, they flood the index with near-empty pages.
cms.wp-attachment-page.fix: Redirect attachment URLs to the file or parent post (Yoast and Rank Math have a setting; WordPress 6.4+ disables them on new sites).

cms.wp-thin-archive.title: Thin tag, author or date archive is indexable
cms.wp-thin-archive.why: Archives with a handful of excerpts duplicate posts and dilute the site. Tags used once or twice are the worst offenders.
cms.wp-thin-archive.fix: Noindex tag, date and single-author archives in your SEO plugin, or add a unique introduction to archives you want to rank.

cms.wp-uncategorized.title: Default "Uncategorized" category is in use
cms.wp-uncategorized.why: Posts left in "Uncategorized" show sloppy structure in URLs, breadcrumbs and archives, and the archive itself is a low-value page.
cms.wp-uncategorized.fix: Rename the default category to something meaningful, or move posts into proper categories and noindex the empty archive.

cms.wp-default-content.title: WordPress sample content still published
cms.wp-default-content.why: The default "Hello world!" post, "Sample Page" and "Just another WordPress site" tagline make the site look unfinished to people and to quality systems.
cms.wp-default-content.fix: Delete the sample post and page and set a real site tagline under Settings → General.

cms.wp-seo-plugin-conflict.title: Two SEO plugins output tags on the same page
cms.wp-seo-plugin-conflict.why: When Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress run together, pages get duplicate titles, canonicals and schema that contradict each other.
cms.wp-seo-plugin-conflict.fix: Keep one SEO plugin. Import its settings into the one you keep, then deactivate the other.

cms.wp-replytocom.title: Comment reply links create duplicate URLs
cms.wp-replytocom.why: Every ?replytocom= link is a crawlable copy of the post. Large comment threads can create thousands of duplicates.
cms.wp-replytocom.fix: Turn off threaded-comment reply links without JavaScript, or let your SEO plugin strip replytocom.

cms.wp-comment-pages.title: Paginated comment pages are indexable
cms.wp-comment-pages.why: /comment-page-2/ URLs repeat the post with a different slice of comments: duplicate content with little value.
cms.wp-comment-pages.fix: Disable comment pagination (Settings → Discussion) or make sure those URLs canonicalise to the post.

cms.wp-emoji-script.title: WordPress emoji script is loaded
cms.wp-emoji-script.why: wp-emoji-release.min.js adds an inline script and request on every page to support emoji in very old browsers.
cms.wp-emoji-script.fix: Disable it with a performance plugin or by removing the print_emoji_detection_script action.

cms.wp-many-plugins.title: Many plugins load assets on the page
cms.wp-many-plugins.why: Assets from more than 25 plugins on one page usually mean scripts and styles loading where they are not needed, slowing every page.
cms.wp-many-plugins.fix: Remove unused plugins and load plugin assets only on the pages that use them (asset manager plugins can do this).

cms.shopify-collection-product-urls.title: Product links go through /collections/…/products/
cms.shopify-collection-product-urls.why: Shopify themes often link to products inside a collection path. Every collection then creates another URL for the same product, canonicalised away, so internal links point at non-canonical URLs.
cms.shopify-collection-product-urls.fix: In the theme, link products with {{ product.url }} instead of {{ product.url | within: collection }}.

cms.shopify-tracking-params.title: Shopify recommendation tracking parameters in links
cms.shopify-tracking-params.why: Links with _pos, _sid, _ss or _psq parameters (from search and recommendations) create crawlable duplicates of product pages.
cms.shopify-tracking-params.fix: Make sure these URLs canonicalise to the clean product URL and avoid them in links you control.

cms.shopify-vendor-type-pages.title: Automatic vendor or type collection pages are indexable
cms.shopify-vendor-type-pages.why: /collections/vendors?q= and /collections/types?q= pages are generated automatically, thin and duplicate.
cms.shopify-vendor-type-pages.fix: Add a noindex rule for these templates in theme.liquid, or build proper collections instead.

cms.platform-subdomain-links.title: Links or canonicals point to the platform’s default domain
cms.platform-subdomain-links.why: References to *.myshopify.com, *.webflow.io, *.wixsite.com, *.vercel.app and similar build domains send visitors and link signals to a duplicate of your site.
cms.platform-subdomain-links.fix: Replace these URLs with your own domain, and make the platform domain redirect to it.

cms.default-title.title: Platform default title or site name
cms.default-title.why: Titles like "My WordPress Website", "My Store", "My Site" or "Squarespace" are platform defaults that were never changed.
cms.default-title.fix: Set your real site name in the platform’s general or SEO settings.

cms.search-results-crawlable.title: Internal search pages are linked and crawlable
cms.search-results-crawlable.why: Links to search result URLs let crawlers generate endless thin pages and can be abused to inject spam text into your domain.
cms.search-results-crawlable.fix: Disallow the search path in robots.txt (for example "Disallow: /?s=" or "Disallow: /search") and add noindex to the search template.

cms.thin-taxonomy-share.title: Tag and category archives make up much of the index
cms.thin-taxonomy-share.why: When indexable archives outnumber real content, the site looks thin overall and crawlers spend their time on lists instead of articles.
cms.thin-taxonomy-share.fix: Noindex tag archives, merge rarely used tags, and keep only category archives with a written introduction.

ai-crawlers.search-bots-blocked.title: AI search crawlers blocked in robots.txt
ai-crawlers.search-bots-blocked.why: You drop out of the index the assistant searches when it answers. This group decides whether you can be cited at all.
ai-crawlers.search-bots-blocked.fix: Remove the Disallow rules for these bots in robots.txt, or add an explicit group such as "User-agent: OAI-SearchBot" with "Allow: /".

ai-crawlers.user-fetchers-blocked.title: AI user-triggered fetchers blocked in robots.txt
ai-crawlers.user-fetchers-blocked.why: When someone pastes your link into an assistant, or it opens your page to answer them, the request fails and the assistant answers without you.
ai-crawlers.user-fetchers-blocked.fix: Remove the Disallow rules for these bots in robots.txt, or add an explicit group such as "User-agent: ChatGPT-User" with "Allow: /".

ai-crawlers.training-bots-blocked.title: AI training crawlers blocked in robots.txt
ai-crawlers.training-bots-blocked.why: Your pages stay out of future model training. Live answers that search the web are not affected, but models will know less about you when they answer from memory. Blocking this is a legitimate choice.
ai-crawlers.training-bots-blocked.fix: If keeping your content out of model training is a deliberate choice, no change is needed. If not, remove the Disallow rules for these tokens in robots.txt.

ai-crawlers.googlebot-blocked.title: Googlebot blocked from the site
ai-crawlers.googlebot-blocked.why: Googlebot feeds Google Search, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Blocking it removes the site from all three; there is no way to opt out of AI Overviews alone through robots.txt.
ai-crawlers.googlebot-blocked.fix: Remove the Disallow: / that applies to Googlebot. To keep content out of Gemini training only, disallow Google-Extended instead.

ai-crawlers.bingbot-blocked.title: Bingbot blocked from the site
ai-crawlers.bingbot-blocked.why: Bing’s index grounds Microsoft Copilot and is one of the indexes other AI search products draw on. Blocking Bingbot removes the site from those answers as well as from Bing.
ai-crawlers.bingbot-blocked.fix: Remove the Disallow rules that apply to Bingbot in robots.txt.
