ai-crawlers.key-pages-blocked.title: Key pages blocked for AI search or user bots
ai-crawlers.key-pages-blocked.why: The home page can be open while the pages people actually ask about (services, pricing, guides) are disallowed by a path rule. Those pages then cannot be cited.
ai-crawlers.key-pages-blocked.fix: Narrow the Disallow rules so they do not match these pages, or add Allow rules for them in the groups that apply to AI bots.

ai-crawlers.wildcard-catches-ai.title: A User-agent: * rule blocks AI bots that have no group of their own
ai-crawlers.wildcard-catches-ai.why: Rules written for all crawlers also apply to every AI bot without its own group. Sites often add a broad block for scrapers and silently remove themselves from AI search and assistants.
ai-crawlers.wildcard-catches-ai.fix: Add explicit groups for the AI bots you want (for example "User-agent: OAI-SearchBot" then "Allow: /"), or narrow the User-agent: * rules.

ai-crawlers.duplicate-groups.title: The same AI bot is named in more than one robots.txt group
ai-crawlers.duplicate-groups.why: RFC 9309 says groups for the same agent are merged, but not every crawler implements that; some apply only the first group. The outcome for that bot becomes unpredictable.
ai-crawlers.duplicate-groups.fix: Merge the rules for each bot into a single group.

ai-crawlers.misspelt-tokens.title: robots.txt names an AI bot with a misspelt token
ai-crawlers.misspelt-tokens.why: A group for "GPT-Bot" or "Claude Bot" matches nothing, so the bot falls through to User-agent: * and the rule you wrote has no effect.
ai-crawlers.misspelt-tokens.fix: Use the exact product tokens the operators publish (for example GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended).

ai-crawlers.legacy-tokens-only.title: Anthropic blocked only through retired tokens
ai-crawlers.legacy-tokens-only.why: anthropic-ai and Claude-Web are retired. A block on them alone does not stop ClaudeBot, so the policy you intended is not in force.
ai-crawlers.legacy-tokens-only.fix: If you mean to block Anthropic training, add "User-agent: ClaudeBot" with "Disallow: /". If not, remove the legacy groups to avoid confusion.

ai-crawlers.extended-optout-scope.title: Google-Extended or Applebot-Extended opt-out: know what it does not cover
ai-crawlers.extended-optout-scope.why: Google-Extended controls Gemini training and grounding only; pages still appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode through Googlebot. Applebot-Extended likewise leaves Applebot search crawling in place. Owners often expect more from these switches.
ai-crawlers.extended-optout-scope.fix: No change is needed if training opt-out is what you want. To appear less in Google’s AI features, use nosnippet or max-snippet on specific pages, accepting it also affects normal results.

ai-crawlers.backwards-policy.title: Training allowed but search blocked for the same AI company
ai-crawlers.backwards-policy.why: This combination gives the company your content to train on while stopping its assistant from citing or linking to you. Most owners want the opposite.
ai-crawlers.backwards-policy.fix: Allow the search bot (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot). If you object to training, block the training bot instead.

ai-crawlers.user-fetcher-robots-ineffect.title: robots.txt rules aimed at fetchers that do not apply them
ai-crawlers.user-fetcher-robots-ineffect.why: Some operators say their user-triggered fetchers act on a person’s behalf and generally ignore robots.txt (for example Perplexity-User and Google’s user-triggered fetchers). A Disallow for them gives a false sense of control.
ai-crawlers.user-fetcher-robots-ineffect.fix: If you really need to stop these requests, use a firewall rule on the user agent (verified by the operator’s published IP ranges). Otherwise remove the rule.

ai-crawlers.robots-server-error.title: robots.txt returns a server error
ai-crawlers.robots-server-error.why: Under RFC 9309, when robots.txt fails with a 5xx crawlers must treat the whole site as disallowed. Google and AI crawlers stop fetching until it recovers.
ai-crawlers.robots-server-error.fix: Make /robots.txt return 200 with your rules (or 404 if you have none). Check the server, CDN and any security rule that serves an error to bots.

ai-crawlers.robots-missing.title: No robots.txt
ai-crawlers.robots-missing.why: Without robots.txt every crawler is allowed, which is fine for access. But you lose the one place to point crawlers at your sitemap and state AI preferences.
ai-crawlers.robots-missing.fix: Add /robots.txt with at least a Sitemap: line, and any AI-specific groups you want.

ai-crawlers.robots-not-text.title: robots.txt is served as an HTML page
ai-crawlers.robots-not-text.why: A robots.txt URL that returns an HTML page (often a soft 404) is not a valid robots file; crawlers ignore it, along with any rules and sitemap you meant to declare.
ai-crawlers.robots-not-text.fix: Serve a plain-text robots.txt at the site root with Content-Type: text/plain.

ai-crawlers.robots-too-large.title: robots.txt is larger than crawlers read
ai-crawlers.robots-too-large.why: Google reads only the first 500 KiB of robots.txt; rules after that are ignored, and other crawlers have similar limits.
ai-crawlers.robots-too-large.fix: Shorten robots.txt: group paths with wildcards and drop rules for URLs that no longer exist.

ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-in-robots.title: robots.txt does not list a sitemap
ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-in-robots.why: Crawlers that do not know your site well, which includes most AI crawlers, find the sitemap through the Sitemap: line in robots.txt.
ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-in-robots.fix: Add a line such as "Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml" to robots.txt.

ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-found.title: No XML sitemap could be found
ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-found.why: A sitemap is how crawlers discover pages your navigation does not link prominently, and how they learn which pages changed. AI crawlers visit less often than Googlebot and lean on it more.
ai-crawlers.sitemap-not-found.fix: Publish /sitemap.xml listing your indexable pages with lastmod dates, and reference it from robots.txt.

ai-crawlers.crawl-delay-high.title: Crawl-delay slows AI crawlers to a trickle
ai-crawlers.crawl-delay-high.why: A large Crawl-delay limits how many pages a crawler that honours it can fetch per day. At 10 seconds or more, a site of a few thousand pages takes days to refresh.
ai-crawlers.crawl-delay-high.fix: Remove Crawl-delay or lower it to a few seconds; manage load with caching or rate limits instead.

ai-crawlers.firewall-challenge.title: Firewall or CDN challenges AI bots
ai-crawlers.firewall-challenge.why: A bot shown a JavaScript challenge or captcha cannot pass it, so it gets nothing however open robots.txt is. This is the most common hidden reason a site is never cited.
ai-crawlers.firewall-challenge.fix: In your CDN or firewall (Cloudflare, Vercel, Akamai…), allow verified AI search and user bots. On Cloudflare, check Security → Bots and AI Crawl Control; on Vercel, the Firewall bot rules.

ai-crawlers.live-blocked.title: AI bots refused by the server
ai-crawlers.live-blocked.why: The server answered these bots with an error or dropped the connection while a browser got the page. Something other than robots.txt — a WAF rule, hosting bot filter or plugin — is blocking them.
ai-crawlers.live-blocked.fix: Find the rule that matches these user agents (CDN firewall, hosting security, a WordPress security plugin) and allow the bots you want, verified by IP where the operator publishes ranges.

ai-crawlers.live-differs.title: AI bots receive less content than a browser
ai-crawlers.live-differs.why: When a bot is redirected elsewhere or given a much thinner page than visitors, the assistant answers from that thinner version, or not at all.
ai-crawlers.live-differs.fix: Serve bots the same HTML as browsers. Look for bot-specific rules in the CDN, a prerender service with a stale cache, or a consent wall shown to unknown user agents.

ai-crawlers.live-inconclusive.title: Live bot test inconclusive: the browser request was blocked too
ai-crawlers.live-inconclusive.why: The audit’s own browser-like request was challenged or refused, so bot access cannot be compared. Often this means the firewall blocks unfamiliar traffic generally.
ai-crawlers.live-inconclusive.fix: Run the audit from a network your firewall trusts, or allow the audit’s IP temporarily, then re-run.

ai-crawlers.slow-for-bots.title: AI bots are served much more slowly than a browser
ai-crawlers.slow-for-bots.why: Some bot-management products slow suspected bots down rather than block them. Crawlers with tight time budgets give up, and user-triggered fetchers time out while a person waits.
ai-crawlers.slow-for-bots.fix: Check for tarpit or rate-limit rules matching AI user agents, and make sure bots are served from cache.

ai-crawlers.bot-missing-schema.title: AI bots receive the page without its structured data
ai-crawlers.bot-missing-schema.why: If JSON-LD is injected only for browsers (by a tag manager or client script), crawlers that do not run JavaScript never see it.
ai-crawlers.bot-missing-schema.fix: Render JSON-LD into the server HTML rather than through a tag manager or client-side script.

ai-crawlers.bot-title-differs.title: AI bots see a different page title
ai-crawlers.bot-title-differs.why: A different title for bots usually means they are being served a block page, a stale prerender or a different language variant, so the assistant describes the wrong page.
ai-crawlers.bot-title-differs.fix: Compare the HTML your CDN serves to the bot user agent with what browsers get, and remove the bot-specific variant.

ai-crawlers.sample-pages-blocked.title: AI bots blocked on key pages
ai-crawlers.sample-pages-blocked.why: Firewall rules often apply to paths rather than the whole site, so the home page can pass while articles or product pages are blocked. These are usually the pages an assistant would cite.
ai-crawlers.sample-pages-blocked.fix: Find the path-specific rule (WAF custom rule, paywall, rate limit on /blog/*) and allow verified AI search and user bots through it.

ai-crawlers.sample-pages-differ.title: AI bots get thinner key pages than a browser
ai-crawlers.sample-pages-differ.why: A metered paywall, consent wall or bot variant can give crawlers a fraction of the page. The assistant then cites, or misquotes, that fraction.
ai-crawlers.sample-pages-differ.fix: Serve bots the full page HTML. For paywalled content, consider structured paywall markup (isAccessibleForFree) rather than serving bots a stub.

ai-crawlers.page-noai.title: Page carries noai / noimageai
ai-crawlers.page-noai.why: noai and noimageai are non-standard signals some tools honour to exclude content from AI use. If they were added by a plugin default rather than by choice, they work against being cited.
ai-crawlers.page-noai.fix: Remove noai/noimageai from the robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag unless excluding this page from AI use is intended.

ai-crawlers.page-nosnippet.title: Page forbids snippets (nosnippet or max-snippet:0)
ai-crawlers.page-nosnippet.why: Google treats nosnippet as an opt-out from AI Overviews and AI Mode as well as text snippets; other engines read it the same way. The page can rank but cannot be quoted.
ai-crawlers.page-nosnippet.fix: Remove nosnippet / max-snippet:0 unless it is deliberate. To protect one passage, wrap only that passage in data-nosnippet.

ai-crawlers.page-max-snippet-low.title: max-snippet is too short to quote an answer
ai-crawlers.page-max-snippet-low.why: A max-snippet limit under about 50 characters is shorter than a single answer sentence, so engines that honour it can barely quote the page.
ai-crawlers.page-max-snippet-low.fix: Remove max-snippet or set it to -1 (no limit), or at least 160.

ai-crawlers.bot-specific-meta.title: Robots meta tag aimed at a specific AI bot
ai-crawlers.bot-specific-meta.why: A <meta name="GPTBot" content="noindex"> style tag applies to that one crawler only. Such tags are often left over from experiments and quietly remove the page from one assistant.
ai-crawlers.bot-specific-meta.fix: Remove the bot-specific meta tag unless the exclusion is intended.

ai-crawlers.x-robots-tag-bot.title: X-Robots-Tag header restricts an AI bot
ai-crawlers.x-robots-tag-bot.why: An X-Robots-Tag header such as "GPTBot: noindex" or "noai" is invisible in the page source, so it is easy to forget it is there. It is often set site-wide by a CDN or server rule.
ai-crawlers.x-robots-tag-bot.fix: Remove the header rule in your server, CDN or hosting config unless the restriction is intended.

ai-crawlers.data-nosnippet-main.title: Most of the main content is marked data-nosnippet
ai-crawlers.data-nosnippet-main.why: Text inside data-nosnippet cannot be shown or quoted by Google, including in AI Overviews. Wrapping the main content in it removes the page from answers.
ai-crawlers.data-nosnippet-main.fix: Apply data-nosnippet only to the specific passages you need to protect, not to the article body.

ai-crawlers.empty-shell.title: Page HTML is an empty JavaScript app shell
ai-crawlers.empty-shell.why: AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and most others) do not run JavaScript. A page whose HTML is an empty root element reads to them as blank.
ai-crawlers.empty-shell.fix: Render the content on the server: server-side rendering or static generation (Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, SvelteKit), or a prerender step for single-page apps.

ai-crawlers.js-gap.title: Much of the content appears only after JavaScript runs
ai-crawlers.js-gap.why: Text that exists only in the rendered page is invisible to AI crawlers, which read the raw HTML. They see a partial page and cite it accordingly, or skip it.
ai-crawlers.js-gap.fix: Move the missing content into the server-rendered HTML (render it on the server or at build time instead of fetching it in the browser).

ai-crawlers.rendered-headings-missing.title: Headings exist only after JavaScript runs
ai-crawlers.rendered-headings-missing.why: Headings tell an engine how the page is divided. If they are added client-side, a crawler reading raw HTML sees one undivided block.
ai-crawlers.rendered-headings-missing.fix: Render the headings in the server HTML.

ai-crawlers.hidden-content.title: Much of the content is hidden in tabs or collapsed panels
ai-crawlers.hidden-content.why: Text in hidden tabs is in the HTML, so most crawlers still read it. But extractors that drop hidden elements, and pipelines that read the rendered text, can miss it, and engines may weight it less.
ai-crawlers.hidden-content.fix: Keep the answer to the page’s main question visible by default. Use <details>/<summary> rather than hidden attributes for secondary content.

ai-crawlers.iframe-content.title: Main content is loaded in an iframe
ai-crawlers.iframe-content.why: Content inside an iframe belongs to the framed URL, not this page. Crawlers attribute it elsewhere or skip it, so this page looks empty.
ai-crawlers.iframe-content.fix: Put the content directly in the page HTML; keep iframes for embeds such as maps and video.

ai-crawlers.common-crawl.title: Site not found in the latest Common Crawl
ai-crawlers.common-crawl.why: Common Crawl is the open web archive most AI training datasets start from. Absence is a strong hint models know little about you from training. Presence is not proof any model trained on you.
ai-crawlers.common-crawl.fix: Allow CCBot in robots.txt and make sure your firewall does not block it; the next monthly crawl can then include you.

ai-crawlers.bing-webmaster.title: No sign the site is verified in Bing Webmaster Tools
ai-crawlers.bing-webmaster.why: Copilot is grounded in Bing, and Bing’s index is one of the sources other AI search products draw on. Bing Webmaster Tools shows what Bing has indexed and lets you submit URLs through IndexNow.
ai-crawlers.bing-webmaster.fix: Verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools (importing from Google Search Console is quickest), submit the sitemap, and enable IndexNow if your CMS supports it. If you verified by DNS, ignore this.

llms-txt.missing.title: No /llms.txt
llms-txt.missing.why: An llms.txt gives AI tools a short, curated map of your site in markdown. llms.txt is a proposal read mainly by coding assistants and agent tools; no major answer engine has confirmed using it for citations.
llms-txt.missing.fix: Publish /llms.txt: an H1 with your name, a one-line > summary, then ## sections listing your key pages as - [Title](https://…): what it covers.

llms-txt.served-as-html.title: /llms.txt returns an HTML page
llms-txt.served-as-html.why: A 200 response with an HTML page (usually a catch-all route or soft 404) tells tools an llms.txt exists when it does not, and they ingest your page template as if it were the file.
llms-txt.served-as-html.fix: Either publish a real markdown llms.txt or make /llms.txt return 404.

llms-txt.no-h1.title: llms.txt does not start with an H1
llms-txt.no-h1.why: The format requires one H1 with the project or site name as the first line; parsers use it as the document title.
llms-txt.no-h1.fix: Make the first line "# Your Company Name".

llms-txt.multiple-h1.title: llms.txt has more than one H1
llms-txt.multiple-h1.why: The format allows exactly one H1; extra ones are usually sections that should be H2, and parsers will not see them as sections.
llms-txt.multiple-h1.fix: Keep the first H1 and change the others to "## ".

llms-txt.no-summary.title: llms.txt has no blockquote summary
llms-txt.no-summary.why: The > summary under the title is what a model reads first to understand who you are. Without it, the file is a list of links with no context.
llms-txt.no-summary.fix: Add a line under the H1 such as "> Acme builds accounting software for UK sole traders."

llms-txt.no-sections.title: llms.txt has no H2 sections
llms-txt.no-sections.why: Sections are how the format groups links (## Docs, ## Services). Tools that expand llms.txt into context rely on them.

llms-txt.no-links.title: llms.txt lists no links
llms-txt.no-links.why: The point of llms.txt is to point tools at your most useful pages. Without markdown links there is nothing to follow.
llms-txt.no-links.fix: List key pages as "- [Title](https://example.com/page): one-line description".

llms-txt.malformed-items.title: llms.txt list items are not markdown links
llms-txt.malformed-items.why: Inside sections the format expects "- [name](url): notes". Bare URLs or plain text items are skipped by parsers.

llms-txt.relative-links.title: llms.txt uses relative links
llms-txt.relative-links.why: llms.txt is often copied into a prompt or another tool, where a relative link no longer resolves.

llms-txt.duplicate-links.title: llms.txt lists the same URL more than once
llms-txt.duplicate-links.why: Duplicates waste the limited context a model gives the file and suggest it was generated without review.
llms-txt.duplicate-links.fix: Keep each URL once, in the section where it fits best.

llms-txt.empty-link-notes.title: Most llms.txt links have no description
llms-txt.empty-link-notes.why: The note after each link (": what this page covers") is how a model decides which link to open for a question. Bare titles force it to guess.
llms-txt.empty-link-notes.fix: Add a short note after each link, for example "- [Pricing](https://…): plans, what each includes, and VAT".

llms-txt.broken-links.title: llms.txt links to pages that fail
llms-txt.broken-links.why: A tool following a broken link from llms.txt gets an error instead of your content, and the file loses credibility as a map.
llms-txt.broken-links.fix: Update or remove links that return 4xx/5xx or fail to load.

llms-txt.redirecting-links.title: llms.txt links redirect
llms-txt.redirecting-links.why: Each redirect costs a request and some tools do not follow them. Linking the final URL is cleaner.
llms-txt.redirecting-links.fix: Replace each redirecting link with the URL it ends up at.

llms-txt.links-not-indexable.title: llms.txt points to noindex or non-canonical pages
llms-txt.links-not-indexable.why: Sending AI tools to a page you have asked search engines not to index, or to a duplicate whose canonical is elsewhere, sends mixed signals about which URL represents the content.
llms-txt.links-not-indexable.fix: Link the canonical, indexable URL of each page instead.

llms-txt.links-blocked-by-robots.title: llms.txt links to pages AI bots are disallowed from
llms-txt.links-blocked-by-robots.why: Listing a page in llms.txt while robots.txt disallows AI crawlers from it is contradictory; compliant tools will not fetch it.
llms-txt.links-blocked-by-robots.fix: Either allow AI bots to fetch these pages or remove them from llms.txt.

llms-txt.mostly-offsite.title: Most llms.txt links point to other sites
llms-txt.mostly-offsite.why: llms.txt should map your own content. A file that mostly links elsewhere tells tools little about you.
llms-txt.mostly-offsite.fix: Lead with your own key pages; keep external links to the few that matter (docs hosted elsewhere, a GitHub repo).

llms-txt.missing-key-pages.title: llms.txt leaves out key pages
llms-txt.missing-key-pages.why: The pages your own navigation links most are usually the ones people ask about. If llms.txt omits them, tools that rely on it never see them.
llms-txt.missing-key-pages.fix: Add the missing pages to the relevant section with a one-line description each.

llms-txt.key-pages-in-optional.title: Key pages listed under ## Optional
llms-txt.key-pages-in-optional.why: In the llms.txt format, the "Optional" section holds links a tool may skip when context is short. Core pages placed there are the first to be dropped.
llms-txt.key-pages-in-optional.fix: Move core pages out of ## Optional into a main section.

llms-txt.link-dump.title: llms.txt is too large to be useful
llms-txt.link-dump.why: An llms.txt with hundreds of links or hundreds of kilobytes will not fit beside a question in a model’s context, which defeats its purpose as a short map.
llms-txt.link-dump.fix: Keep llms.txt to your key pages (tens of links). Put exhaustive lists in the sitemap and full content in llms-full.txt.

llms-txt.too-thin.title: llms.txt lists very few pages
llms-txt.too-thin.why: One or two links say little more than the home page does. The file earns its keep by pointing at the specific pages that answer common questions.
llms-txt.too-thin.fix: List the pages people most need: services or products, pricing, about, contact, and your best guides.

llms-txt.content-type.title: llms.txt served with an unexpected content type
llms-txt.content-type.why: Served as text/plain or text/markdown in UTF-8, the file displays and parses predictably. Other types (application/octet-stream, no charset) can be downloaded instead of read, or garble non-ASCII text.
llms-txt.content-type.fix: Serve llms.txt as "text/plain; charset=utf-8" or "text/markdown; charset=utf-8".

llms-txt.quality-grade.title: llms.txt quality below good
llms-txt.quality-grade.why: A well-formed llms.txt is short, titled, summarised, sectioned and lists the right pages with notes. llms.txt is a proposal read mainly by coding assistants and agent tools; no major answer engine has confirmed using it for citations.
llms-txt.quality-grade.fix: Work through the reasons listed with this finding, highest-weight first.

llms-txt.full-missing.title: No /llms-full.txt on a content-heavy site
llms-txt.full-missing.why: llms-full.txt carries the full text of your key pages in one markdown file, which documentation tools and coding assistants load directly. It matters most for docs and knowledge sites.
llms-txt.full-missing.fix: Generate llms-full.txt from your content at build time (many docs generators and SEO plugins can).

llms-txt.full-too-large.title: llms-full.txt is very large
llms-txt.full-too-large.why: Above a few megabytes the file no longer fits any model’s context and many tools truncate or refuse it.
llms-txt.full-too-large.fix: Split by product or section (for example /docs/llms-full.txt per area) and link each from llms.txt.

llms-txt.full-stale.title: llms-full.txt is older than your content
llms-txt.full-stale.why: A full-text export that lags your site feeds tools outdated facts, which then appear in their answers.
llms-txt.full-stale.fix: Regenerate llms-full.txt on every deploy or content change.

llms-txt.full-is-html.title: /llms-full.txt returns an HTML page
llms-txt.full-is-html.why: Tools that load llms-full.txt will ingest your page template instead of content.
llms-txt.full-is-html.fix: Publish a real markdown file or make the URL return 404.

llms-txt.no-markdown-variants.title: Pages listed in llms.txt have no markdown versions
llms-txt.no-markdown-variants.why: The llms.txt proposal suggests offering each page as markdown at the same URL plus .md, so tools can fetch clean text without HTML clutter. Optional, and useful mainly for docs.
llms-txt.no-markdown-variants.fix: Serve a markdown copy at <page>.md, or answer Accept: text/markdown with markdown.

geo-content.no-answer-first.title: Page does not open with a direct answer
geo-content.no-answer-first.why: Answer engines favour passages that state the answer plainly near the top. Opening with a welcome, a rhetorical question or scene-setting pushes the answer down where it is less likely to be lifted.
geo-content.no-answer-first.fix: Rewrite the first 40–60 words after the H1 to answer the page’s main question directly: what it is, who it is for, and the key fact.

geo-content.no-question-headings.title: No subheadings phrased as questions
geo-content.no-question-headings.why: People ask assistants questions. A subheading that matches the question, followed by a direct answer, is the easiest passage for an engine to match and quote.
geo-content.no-question-headings.fix: Rephrase two or three subheadings as the questions your readers ask, and answer each in the first sentence below.

geo-content.answer-buried.title: Answers under question headings are long-winded
geo-content.answer-buried.why: When the paragraph under a question heading runs past 80 words before answering, engines struggle to extract a concise answer and may pick another source.
geo-content.answer-buried.fix: Start each answer with a one or two sentence direct answer (under about 50 words), then add detail in following paragraphs.

geo-content.faq-without-schema.title: FAQ content without FAQPage markup
geo-content.faq-without-schema.why: FAQPage JSON-LD states each question and answer explicitly, so engines do not have to infer the pairs from layout. Google limits FAQ rich results to some sites, but the markup still describes the content clearly.
geo-content.faq-without-schema.fix: Add FAQPage JSON-LD whose questions and answers match the visible FAQ text exactly.

geo-content.faq-schema-mismatch.title: FAQPage markup does not match the visible page
geo-content.faq-schema-mismatch.why: Markup for questions that are not on the page is treated as misleading by Google and gives engines facts the reader cannot see. It undermines trust in all your markup.
geo-content.faq-schema-mismatch.fix: Make the FAQPage questions and answers match the visible FAQ, or remove the markup.

geo-content.faq-answers-thin.title: FAQ answers are too short to be useful
geo-content.faq-answers-thin.why: One-line answers such as "Yes." or "Contact us." give an engine nothing to quote and read as filler.
geo-content.faq-answers-thin.fix: Give each FAQ answer two or three sentences with the specific fact (price, time, condition).

geo-content.no-lists-or-tables.title: Long page with no lists or tables
geo-content.no-lists-or-tables.why: Steps, options, specifications and comparisons are lifted whole when they are lists or tables. As running prose they must be paraphrased, and other sources win.
geo-content.no-lists-or-tables.fix: Turn steps into a numbered list, options into bullets, and comparisons or specifications into a table.

geo-content.howto-without-steps.title: “How to” page without numbered steps
geo-content.howto-without-steps.why: For how-to questions, engines prefer sources that give an ordered list of steps they can reproduce.
geo-content.howto-without-steps.fix: Present the procedure as a numbered list (<ol>), one action per step.

geo-content.no-specifics.title: No concrete figures on the page
geo-content.no-specifics.why: Answers are built from specifics: prices, timescales, quantities, dates. A page without a single figure gives an engine nothing factual to quote.
geo-content.no-specifics.fix: Add the figures you can stand behind: starting price, delivery time, years in operation, sizes, limits.

geo-content.stats-without-sources.title: Statistics without sources
geo-content.stats-without-sources.why: Percentages and market figures with no link to their source are hard for an engine to trust or attribute. Cited statistics are more likely to be repeated.
geo-content.stats-without-sources.fix: Link each statistic to the study, dataset or official source it came from, or label it as your own data.

geo-content.no-citations.title: Long article cites no outside sources
geo-content.no-citations.why: Content that links claims to authoritative sources is easier to verify, and engines that weigh trust treat it as a safer citation.
geo-content.no-citations.fix: Link key claims to primary sources: standards, official statistics, research, or vendor documentation.

geo-content.quotes-unattributed.title: Quotations without attribution
geo-content.quotes-unattributed.why: A blockquote with no named source cannot be attributed, so an engine cannot repeat it with confidence.
geo-content.quotes-unattributed.fix: Name the person and role for each quotation, in a <cite> or caption, and link the source where there is one.

geo-content.no-author.title: Article has no author
geo-content.no-author.why: A named, accountable author is one of the clearest trust signals for both Google and AI engines. Anonymous articles are weaker citation candidates, especially on advice topics.
geo-content.no-author.fix: Show a byline linking to an author page, and set "author" (a Person with name and url) in the Article schema.

geo-content.author-not-in-schema.title: Byline shown but no author in the schema
geo-content.author-not-in-schema.why: The visible byline helps readers; the schema author is how engines connect the article to a known person and their other work.

geo-content.author-no-credentials.title: Author markup has only a name
geo-content.author-no-credentials.why: A name alone is ambiguous. A url to an author page, a jobTitle and sameAs links to professional profiles let engines identify the person and judge their expertise.
geo-content.author-no-credentials.fix: Extend the author Person with url, jobTitle, and sameAs (LinkedIn and similar).

geo-content.no-visible-date.title: Article shows no date
geo-content.no-visible-date.why: Engines and readers both prefer current information. Without a visible published or updated date, an article cannot show it is current.
geo-content.no-visible-date.fix: Show the published date and, when you revise it, “Last updated” with the date.

geo-content.no-schema-dates.title: Article schema without datePublished or dateModified
geo-content.no-schema-dates.why: datePublished and dateModified in the schema are the machine-readable freshness signal engines read.
geo-content.no-schema-dates.fix: Add datePublished and dateModified (ISO 8601) to the Article JSON-LD and keep dateModified current.

geo-content.date-invalid.title: Schema dates are invalid or contradictory
geo-content.date-invalid.why: A dateModified before datePublished, a date in the future, or an unparseable date makes freshness unreliable and can be ignored altogether.
geo-content.date-invalid.fix: Use ISO 8601 dates (2026-03-14 or 2026-03-14T09:00:00+00:00) and make sure dateModified is on or after datePublished.

geo-content.stale.title: Article not updated in over 18 months
geo-content.stale.why: For topics that change (prices, tools, regulations), engines favour recent sources. An old date is a reason to choose a competitor’s page.
geo-content.stale.fix: Review the article, update facts and figures, and set a new dateModified. Do not change the date without changing the content.

geo-content.long-sections.title: Sections too long to stand alone
geo-content.long-sections.why: Engines retrieve passages, not pages. A section of 400+ words under one heading mixes several points, so no single chunk answers a question cleanly.
geo-content.long-sections.fix: Split long sections with descriptive subheadings so each covers one point in roughly 100–300 words.

geo-content.wall-of-text.title: Very long paragraphs
geo-content.wall-of-text.why: Paragraphs over 150 words hide the key sentence and make passage extraction less precise.
geo-content.wall-of-text.fix: Break long paragraphs so each makes one point, leading with that point.

geo-content.too-few-headings.title: Too few headings for the length
geo-content.too-few-headings.why: Headings are how engines segment a page into answerable passages. Under one subheading per 400 words, sections blur together.
geo-content.too-few-headings.fix: Add descriptive H2/H3 headings for each distinct topic on the page.

geo-content.heading-noise.title: More headings than content
geo-content.heading-noise.why: When headings outnumber the text beneath them (one per 40 words or fewer), passages are fragments with no answer in them.
geo-content.heading-noise.fix: Merge thin sections and give each remaining heading enough text to answer its point.

geo-content.vague-language.title: Marketing language instead of specifics
geo-content.vague-language.why: Words like “world-class” or “seamless” carry no information. Engines skip them, and pages built on them have little left to quote.
geo-content.vague-language.fix: Replace each claim with the fact behind it: what you do, for whom, how fast, at what price, with what result.

geo-content.no-summary.title: Long article with no summary up front
geo-content.no-summary.why: A short summary or key-takeaways block near the top gives engines a ready-made answer and readers a reason to stay.
geo-content.no-summary.fix: Add a three to five point “Key takeaways” or a two-sentence summary right after the introduction.

geo-content.no-definition.title: “What is” page without a definition sentence
geo-content.no-definition.why: For definitional questions engines look for a sentence of the form “X is …”. Without one they quote a source that has it.
geo-content.no-definition.fix: Open with a one-sentence definition: “[Term] is [category] that [distinguishing feature].”

geo-content.comparison-no-table.title: Comparison page without a comparison table
geo-content.comparison-no-table.why: “X vs Y”, “best” and “alternatives” questions are often answered with a table. Pages that give one are easy to lift; prose comparisons are not.
geo-content.comparison-no-table.fix: Add a table comparing the options on the criteria buyers care about (price, features, fit), with honest entries.

geo-content.low-entity-density.title: Few named things on the page
geo-content.low-entity-density.why: Engines build answers around entities: products, places, organisations, standards. Text that rarely names anything specific is hard to match to a question.
geo-content.low-entity-density.fix: Name the specific products, tools, places, standards and organisations you mean instead of “our solution” or “the platform”.

geo-content.no-first-hand-evidence.title: Long article with no first-hand evidence
geo-content.no-first-hand-evidence.why: Engines can already summarise what everyone says. Pages with your own tests, data, cases or experience offer something new to cite.
geo-content.no-first-hand-evidence.fix: Add what only you can say: results from your own work, measurements, examples or a short case study.

geo-content.missing-article-schema.title: Article without Article schema
geo-content.missing-article-schema.why: Article (or BlogPosting) JSON-LD states the headline, author, publisher and dates in a form engines read reliably.
geo-content.missing-article-schema.fix: Add Article or BlogPosting JSON-LD with headline, author, publisher, datePublished, dateModified and image.

geo-content.isolated-article.title: Article barely linked from the rest of the site
geo-content.isolated-article.why: Topical clusters, where related pages link to each other, show engines you cover a subject in depth and help crawlers find each piece.
geo-content.isolated-article.fix: Link to this article from two or more related pages and from a hub page for its topic.

geo-content.no-related-links.title: Article links to no related content
geo-content.no-related-links.why: Links from an article to related pages build the topical cluster from the other side and keep crawlers moving through your expertise.
geo-content.no-related-links.fix: Add in-text links to two or three related articles or service pages.

geo-content.boilerplate-lead.title: Same opening text on many pages
geo-content.boilerplate-lead.why: When many pages open with the same banner or intro, the first thing an engine reads on each is identical, and the page-specific answer is pushed down.
geo-content.boilerplate-lead.fix: Move shared banners out of the main content (or below it) so each page opens with its own answer.

geo-content.low-geo-score.title: Low GEO readiness score for the page
geo-content.low-geo-score.why: The GEO score sums how easily an answer engine can lift, trust and attribute this page: direct answer, structure, specifics, sources, author, freshness and chunking.
geo-content.low-geo-score.fix: Work through the tips listed with this finding; each names the specific change for this page.

geo-content.site-geo-score.title: Site-wide GEO readiness is low
geo-content.site-geo-score.why: The average GEO score across content pages shows whether answer-friendly writing is a habit or an exception. Low averages usually trace to a template (no dates, no authors) or a house style (no direct answers).
geo-content.site-geo-score.fix: Fix template-level gaps first (author, dates, schema), then rewrite the openings of your most-visited pages.

geo-content.gated-content.title: Content is behind a login or paywall
geo-content.gated-content.why: AI crawlers do not sign in or subscribe. Content behind a login or paywall cannot be read, quoted or cited, and Google needs paywall markup to tell a paywall from cloaking.
geo-content.gated-content.fix: Keep a substantial public part of each gated page (a summary, the first section, key facts). For a paywall, mark it up with isAccessibleForFree: false and a hasPart cssSelector for the hidden section.

geo-content.no-first-party-facts.title: No first-party facts for AI to cite
geo-content.no-first-party-facts.why: When people ask an assistant about prices, what is included, delivery or returns, it prefers to quote the business itself. Without pricing, FAQ or policy pages (and their markup), the answer comes from directories, resellers or competitors.
geo-content.no-first-party-facts.fix: Publish the facts customers ask about on your own site: a pricing or plans page, an FAQ with real answers, delivery, returns and warranty terms. Mark them up with FAQPage, Product/Offer or Service schema.

geo-entity.no-organization.title: No Organization or LocalBusiness schema
geo-entity.no-organization.why: Organization markup is how you tell engines, in their own vocabulary, who is behind the site: legal name, logo, contact and profiles. Without it they infer, and can confuse you with similarly named companies.
geo-entity.no-organization.fix: Add Organization (or the most specific LocalBusiness subtype) JSON-LD to the home page with name, url, logo, sameAs, contactPoint and, for local firms, address.

geo-entity.org-incomplete.title: Organization schema missing core properties
geo-entity.org-incomplete.why: name, url and logo are the minimum engines use to identify the organisation and show it. Missing any of them weakens the match between your site and your entity.
geo-entity.org-incomplete.fix: Add the missing properties to the Organization JSON-LD.

geo-entity.org-no-sameas.title: Organization has no sameAs links
geo-entity.org-no-sameas.why: sameAs ties your site to the same organisation’s profiles elsewhere (LinkedIn, Wikidata, Crunchbase). It is one of the strongest ways to disambiguate your brand for knowledge graphs and AI models.
geo-entity.org-no-sameas.fix: Add "sameAs": [ … ] listing the URLs of your official profiles.

geo-entity.sameas-thin.title: sameAs misses major profiles
geo-entity.sameas-thin.why: LinkedIn, Wikidata and (for local firms) the Google Business Profile are the sources AI models and knowledge graphs most often reconcile companies against.
geo-entity.sameas-thin.fix: Add the missing official profiles to sameAs. Only link profiles you control or that are about you.

geo-entity.no-wikidata.title: No Wikidata entry linked
geo-entity.no-wikidata.why: Wikidata is the open knowledge graph many AI systems use to identify organisations. Linking an existing entry from sameAs removes ambiguity. Not every business qualifies for one; only add an entry if you meet Wikidata’s notability rules.
geo-entity.no-wikidata.fix: If a Wikidata item for your organisation exists, add its URL (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q…) to sameAs.

geo-entity.sameas-invalid.title: sameAs contains invalid or self links
geo-entity.sameas-invalid.why: sameAs should list other pages about the same entity. Relative paths, non-URLs and links back to your own site add nothing and can be read as errors.
geo-entity.sameas-invalid.fix: Keep only absolute https URLs of external profiles in sameAs.

geo-entity.social-not-in-sameas.title: Profiles linked on the site are missing from sameAs
geo-entity.social-not-in-sameas.why: You already link these profiles in your header or footer. Listing them in sameAs as well turns a visual link into a machine-readable identity claim.
geo-entity.social-not-in-sameas.fix: Add the listed profile URLs to the Organization sameAs.

geo-entity.org-no-contact.title: Organization schema has no contact details
geo-entity.org-no-contact.why: contactPoint, telephone or email let engines answer “how do I contact X” from your own data rather than a directory that may be out of date.
geo-entity.org-no-contact.fix: Add contactPoint (contactType, telephone or email) or telephone/email to the Organization schema.

geo-entity.local-no-address.title: Local business schema without address or hours
geo-entity.local-no-address.why: For a business people visit or call, address, geo coordinates and opening hours are what “near me” and “open now” answers are built from.
geo-entity.local-no-address.fix: Add address (PostalAddress), geo, telephone and openingHoursSpecification to the LocalBusiness schema.

geo-entity.org-no-description.title: Organization schema has no description
geo-entity.org-no-description.why: A one-sentence description in your own words is a ready answer to “what does X do” that engines can attribute to you.
geo-entity.org-no-description.fix: Add "description": what you do, for whom, and where, in one plain sentence.

geo-entity.org-no-background.title: Organization schema lacks founding facts
geo-entity.org-no-background.why: foundingDate, founder and location are facts engines repeat when describing a company. Supplying them reduces the chance of wrong guesses.
geo-entity.org-no-background.fix: Add foundingDate and founder (Person) and, if relevant, foundingLocation.

geo-entity.org-no-expertise.title: Organization schema does not say what you do
geo-entity.org-no-expertise.why: knowsAbout, areaServed and makesOffer/hasOfferCatalog describe your subject areas, markets and services in a structured way, helping engines match you to category questions.
geo-entity.org-no-expertise.fix: Add knowsAbout (topics), areaServed (countries or regions) and makesOffer or hasOfferCatalog (services).

geo-entity.org-no-id.title: Organization schema has no @id
geo-entity.org-no-id.why: A stable @id (such as https://example.com/#organization) lets every page’s Article publisher, WebSite and Product markup point to one organisation node instead of creating many.
geo-entity.org-no-id.fix: Give the Organization an "@id" and reference it ({"@id": "…#organization"}) from publisher, brand and provider fields.

geo-entity.org-name-conflict.title: Different organisation names across pages
geo-entity.org-name-conflict.why: If page templates declare different organisation names, engines cannot tell whether they are one company or several.
geo-entity.org-name-conflict.fix: Use one exact organisation name in every Organization node (put trading names in alternateName).

geo-entity.brand-inconsistent.title: Brand name differs between title, og:site_name and schema
geo-entity.brand-inconsistent.why: The site name engines show and repeat is taken from WebSite schema, og:site_name and title patterns. When they disagree, engines pick one, not necessarily yours.
geo-entity.brand-inconsistent.fix: Use the same brand name in WebSite/Organization schema, og:site_name and the title suffix.

geo-entity.no-og-site-name.title: No og:site_name on the home page
geo-entity.no-og-site-name.why: og:site_name is one of the signals Google and link previews use for your site name.

geo-entity.no-website-schema.title: No WebSite schema on the home page
geo-entity.no-website-schema.why: WebSite JSON-LD with name and url is Google’s preferred way to state your site name, and links the site to its publisher organisation.
geo-entity.no-website-schema.fix: Add WebSite JSON-LD to the home page with name, url, and publisher referencing your Organization @id.

geo-entity.publisher-mismatch.title: Article publisher differs from the organisation
geo-entity.publisher-mismatch.why: When articles name a different publisher from your Organization schema, engines may credit the content to someone else.
geo-entity.publisher-mismatch.fix: Set publisher on Article/BlogPosting to your Organization (ideally by @id).

geo-entity.logo-not-image.title: Organization logo is not an image URL
geo-entity.logo-not-image.why: Engines show and match your logo from this URL. A page URL or relative path cannot be used.
geo-entity.logo-not-image.fix: Point logo at an absolute URL of a square or rectangular PNG, SVG or JPG (at least 112 × 112 px).

geo-entity.nap-inconsistent.title: Phone numbers differ across pages
geo-entity.nap-inconsistent.why: Consistent name, address and phone details across your pages and directories are how engines confirm a business is real and where it is. Several numbers in click-to-call links suggest outdated templates.
geo-entity.nap-inconsistent.fix: Use one primary phone number site-wide (and in schema); label any other numbers clearly by department or branch.

geo-entity.no-about-page.title: No About page found
geo-entity.no-about-page.why: An About page is where engines look for who you are, how long you have operated and who runs the business. It is a basic trust signal for people and for AI answers.
geo-entity.no-about-page.fix: Publish an About page (/about) with the company story, people, location and credentials, and link it from the main navigation or footer.

geo-entity.about-not-linked.title: About page not linked from the home page
geo-entity.about-not-linked.why: If the About page is not linked from the home page, crawlers reach it late or not at all, and it loses weight as the source of who you are.
geo-entity.about-not-linked.fix: Link the About page from the header or footer.

geo-entity.no-contact-page.title: No Contact page found
geo-entity.no-contact-page.why: A contact page with address, phone and email confirms you are a real, reachable business and gives engines contact facts from the source.
geo-entity.no-contact-page.fix: Publish a Contact page with your business name, address (if you have one), phone and email, and link it site-wide.

geo-entity.no-author-pages.title: Authors have no profile pages
geo-entity.no-author-pages.why: An author page that lists a person’s role, experience and other articles, linked from each byline, lets engines connect the work to a person and judge their expertise.
geo-entity.no-author-pages.fix: Create a page per author (/authors/name) with bio, credentials and sameAs profiles, and link bylines and the schema author url to it.

geo-entity.duplicate-org-nodes.title: Several conflicting Organization nodes on one page
geo-entity.duplicate-org-nodes.why: When a theme and a plugin each output an Organization, engines see two descriptions of the company that may disagree.
geo-entity.duplicate-org-nodes.fix: Keep one Organization node per page (disable the duplicate output in the theme or SEO plugin).

agentic.no-agent-discovery.title: No agent discovery documents
agentic.no-agent-discovery.why: Agents look for machine-readable descriptions of what a site offers: an MCP server card, an A2A agent card, an API catalog or OpenAPI. None is expected of a typical business site today; they matter once you offer bookings, data or an app that agents could use directly.
agentic.no-agent-discovery.fix: Nothing to do unless you have a service an agent could use. If you do, start with an OpenAPI description listed in /.well-known/api-catalog, then consider an MCP server.

agentic.mcp-card-missing.title: API or sign-in present but no MCP discovery document
agentic.mcp-card-missing.why: The site exposes an API or OAuth server, so it could serve AI agents. An MCP server card (a draft at the MCP project) lets clients find your server and its auth requirements without manual setup.
agentic.mcp-card-missing.fix: If you run or plan an MCP server, publish its card at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json with the server name, endpoint, transport and authentication.

agentic.mcp-card-invalid.title: MCP discovery document is invalid
agentic.mcp-card-invalid.why: A published MCP card that clients cannot parse, or that has no usable endpoint, is worse than none: automated clients fail with no explanation.
agentic.mcp-card-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors. At minimum: a server name, an HTTPS endpoint URL, and the transport type.

agentic.mcp-card-incomplete.title: MCP discovery document lacks useful detail
agentic.mcp-card-incomplete.why: Clients decide whether to connect from the card alone. Without a description, version or list of tools, the server is hard to choose.
agentic.mcp-card-incomplete.fix: Add the missing fields listed with this finding.

agentic.mcp-auth-no-prm.title: MCP server needs auth but no protected resource metadata
agentic.mcp-auth-no-prm.why: MCP authorisation is built on OAuth protected resource metadata (RFC 9728): clients fetch it to find your authorisation server. Without it, a compliant client cannot start sign-in.
agentic.mcp-auth-no-prm.fix: Serve /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (or the path-specific variant for your MCP endpoint) naming your authorisation server, and return a WWW-Authenticate header pointing to it on 401.

agentic.a2a-card-invalid.title: A2A agent card is invalid
agentic.a2a-card-invalid.why: A2A clients read the agent card to learn your agent’s endpoint, skills and authentication. Missing required fields mean clients reject it.
agentic.a2a-card-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors: name, description, version, an HTTPS url, capabilities, default input/output modes and at least one described skill.

agentic.a2a-card-incomplete.title: A2A agent card lacks recommended detail
agentic.a2a-card-incomplete.why: Skills without examples, no declared security schemes or no provider make it harder for other agents to pick and safely call yours.
agentic.a2a-card-incomplete.fix: Add the fields listed with this finding.

agentic.a2a-legacy-path.title: A2A card only at the old /.well-known/agent.json path
agentic.a2a-legacy-path.why: Current A2A versions look for /.well-known/agent-card.json. Clients following the current spec will not find a card that exists only at agent.json.
agentic.a2a-legacy-path.fix: Serve the card at /.well-known/agent-card.json (keep agent.json as a redirect or copy for older clients).

agentic.oauth-as-invalid.title: OAuth authorisation server metadata is invalid
agentic.oauth-as-invalid.why: Agents and MCP clients configure sign-in automatically from this document (RFC 8414). Missing required fields stop them.
agentic.oauth-as-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors so the document has issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint and response_types_supported.

agentic.oauth-issuer-mismatch.title: OAuth or OpenID issuer does not match where it is served
agentic.oauth-issuer-mismatch.why: RFC 8414 and OpenID Discovery require clients to reject metadata whose issuer differs from the URL it was fetched for. This is a common cause of “invalid issuer” sign-in failures.
agentic.oauth-issuer-mismatch.fix: Make "issuer" exactly the origin (and path, if any) the metadata is served under, or serve the metadata from the issuer’s own origin.

agentic.oauth-no-pkce.title: Authorisation server does not advertise PKCE S256
agentic.oauth-no-pkce.why: OAuth 2.1 and the MCP authorisation spec require PKCE with S256. MCP clients refuse to proceed when code_challenge_methods_supported does not list it.
agentic.oauth-no-pkce.fix: Support PKCE and add "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["S256"] to the metadata.

agentic.oauth-no-registration.title: No way for new AI clients to register
agentic.oauth-no-registration.why: MCP clients are not known to you in advance. Dynamic client registration or client ID metadata documents let them obtain a client ID; without either, each client needs manual setup.
agentic.oauth-no-registration.fix: Support client ID metadata documents (client_id_metadata_document_supported) or dynamic client registration (registration_endpoint), with whatever approval policy suits you.

agentic.prm-invalid.title: Protected resource metadata is invalid
agentic.prm-invalid.why: RFC 9728 metadata tells clients which authorisation server protects your API or MCP server. If "resource" is missing or does not match, compliant clients reject it.
agentic.prm-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors: "resource" must equal the resource URL, and "authorization_servers" should list your issuer.

agentic.prm-as-unreachable.title: The authorisation server named in resource metadata has no metadata
agentic.prm-as-unreachable.why: A client follows authorization_servers to the issuer’s RFC 8414 or OpenID metadata. If that is missing, sign-in cannot start.
agentic.prm-as-unreachable.fix: Publish /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (or openid-configuration) at the issuer named in authorization_servers.

agentic.openid-invalid.title: OpenID configuration is missing required fields
agentic.openid-invalid.why: OpenID Connect clients, including agent frameworks, rely on the required discovery fields to sign users in.
agentic.openid-invalid.fix: Add the missing fields listed with this finding.

agentic.api-catalog-missing.title: API description found but no API catalog
agentic.api-catalog-missing.why: RFC 9727 defines /.well-known/api-catalog so agents can find your APIs from the domain alone. Without it, your OpenAPI file is only found by guessing.
agentic.api-catalog-missing.fix: Serve /.well-known/api-catalog as application/linkset+json with a linkset entry whose service-desc points to your OpenAPI file.

agentic.api-catalog-invalid.title: API catalog is invalid
agentic.api-catalog-invalid.why: An api-catalog that is not a valid RFC 9264 linkset cannot be read by the clients it is meant for.

agentic.openapi-invalid.title: OpenAPI description is invalid
agentic.openapi-invalid.why: Agent frameworks turn OpenAPI operations into tools. A document without openapi, info or paths produces no tools.
agentic.openapi-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors and validate the file with an OpenAPI linter.

agentic.openapi-undescribed.title: API operations lack descriptions
agentic.openapi-undescribed.why: An agent chooses which operation to call from its summary and description. Undescribed operations are guessed at or ignored.
agentic.openapi-undescribed.fix: Add a summary and description to every operation, saying when to use it.

agentic.web-bot-auth-invalid.title: Web Bot Auth key directory has problems
agentic.web-bot-auth-invalid.why: If you operate an agent or crawler, this directory (an IETF draft) publishes the keys verifiers use to check your signed requests. An invalid or unsigned directory means your requests cannot be verified.
agentic.web-bot-auth-invalid.fix: Publish a JWKS of Ed25519 public keys as application/http-message-signatures-directory+json, and sign the response.

agentic.markdown-negotiation-missing.title: No markdown version of pages for agents
agentic.markdown-negotiation-missing.why: Some agents ask for pages with Accept: text/markdown to save tokens and avoid HTML clutter, and some CDNs now offer this conversion. It is an emerging convention; HTML still works for every engine.
agentic.markdown-negotiation-missing.fix: Optionally answer Accept: text/markdown with a markdown rendering of the page (with Vary: Accept), or enable your CDN’s markdown conversion.

agentic.markdown-no-vary.title: Markdown negotiation without Vary: Accept
agentic.markdown-no-vary.why: When the same URL returns markdown or HTML depending on Accept, caches must be told with Vary: Accept. Otherwise a CDN can serve markdown to browsers or HTML to agents.
agentic.markdown-no-vary.fix: Add "Vary: Accept" to responses from negotiated URLs.

agentic.markdown-is-html.title: Markdown response is really HTML
agentic.markdown-is-html.why: A response labelled text/markdown that contains an HTML document confuses agents that trusted the label.
agentic.markdown-is-html.fix: Convert the page to markdown before serving it as text/markdown, or stop labelling HTML as markdown.

agentic.webmcp-not-used.title: Key forms are not exposed as WebMCP tools
agentic.webmcp-not-used.why: WebMCP (a W3C community draft, in early browser trials) lets a page declare forms as tools an in-browser agent can call with toolname and tooldescription attributes, instead of guessing which fields to fill. Optional today; low effort for contact and booking forms.
agentic.webmcp-not-used.fix: Add toolname="request_quote" and tooldescription="…" to key forms, and give each input a clear name and label.

agentic.webmcp-form-incomplete.title: WebMCP form tool is incomplete
agentic.webmcp-form-incomplete.why: An agent sees only the tool name, description and field names. A tool without a description, or fields without names, cannot be used reliably.
agentic.webmcp-form-incomplete.fix: Give the form a tooldescription saying what it does, and give every field a name (and toolparamdescription where the label is unclear).

agentic.webmcp-tool-incomplete.title: Script-registered WebMCP tool lacks description or schema
agentic.webmcp-tool-incomplete.why: Tools registered with navigator.modelContext need a description and an input schema; agents rely on both to call them correctly.
agentic.webmcp-tool-incomplete.fix: Pass description and inputSchema (JSON Schema) for every tool you register.

agentic.form-unlabelled.title: Form fields an agent cannot identify
agentic.form-unlabelled.why: Browsing agents fill forms through the accessibility tree. Fields with no label, aria-label or descriptive name appear as anonymous text boxes, so the agent guesses or gives up.
agentic.form-unlabelled.fix: Give every field a visible <label for> (or aria-label) and a meaningful name attribute.

agentic.form-no-autocomplete.title: Contact fields without autocomplete hints
agentic.form-no-autocomplete.why: autocomplete="email", "tel", "name" tell browsers and agents exactly what each field wants, so they can fill it from the user’s details without guessing.
agentic.form-no-autocomplete.fix: Add autocomplete attributes (name, email, tel, organization, postal-code…) to personal-detail fields.

agentic.captcha-only-form.title: Captcha-protected form is the only way to get in touch
agentic.captcha-only-form.why: Agents acting for a person cannot solve captchas. If the form is the only contact route, the person’s agent cannot reach you; a visible email or phone gives it another way.
agentic.captcha-only-form.fix: Show an email address or phone number next to the form, or use invisible bot protection that scores rather than challenges.

agentic.icon-only-controls.title: Buttons and links without accessible names
agentic.icon-only-controls.why: Agents operate pages through the accessibility tree. Icon-only buttons and links with no text or aria-label are anonymous there, so the agent cannot tell “menu” from “add to basket”.
agentic.icon-only-controls.fix: Give icon-only controls an aria-label (or visually hidden text) describing the action.

agentic.div-buttons.title: Clickable elements that are not buttons or links
agentic.div-buttons.why: A <div onclick> is not exposed as a control in the accessibility tree, so browsing agents (and keyboard users) cannot find or activate it.
agentic.div-buttons.fix: Use <button> or <a href> for anything clickable, or add role="button", tabindex="0" and keyboard handling.

agentic.no-search-action.title: Site search not described with SearchAction
agentic.no-search-action.why: A WebSite potentialAction of type SearchAction tells agents how to query your site search directly with a URL template.
agentic.no-search-action.fix: Add to the WebSite JSON-LD: "potentialAction": {"@type": "SearchAction", "target": {"@type": "EntryPoint", "urlTemplate": "https://example.com/search?q={search_term_string}"}, "query-input": "required name=search_term_string"}.

agentic.search-action-invalid.title: SearchAction markup cannot be used
agentic.search-action-invalid.why: A SearchAction whose target has no {placeholder}, or whose query-input does not name it, gives an agent a template it cannot fill.
agentic.search-action-invalid.fix: Use a urlTemplate with {search_term_string} and "query-input": "required name=search_term_string".

agentic.business-actions-missing.title: Bookable business without action markup
agentic.business-actions-missing.why: schema.org ReserveAction, OrderAction and ScheduleAction let assistants offer “book a table” or “order” directly with your own booking URL, instead of a third-party aggregator’s.
agentic.business-actions-missing.fix: Add potentialAction (ReserveAction / OrderAction / ScheduleAction with an EntryPoint urlTemplate) to your LocalBusiness schema, pointing at your booking or ordering page.

agentic.nlweb-error.title: Natural-language /ask endpoint returns errors
agentic.nlweb-error.why: An /ask endpoint (the NLWeb convention) that errors tells agents your conversational interface is broken. NLWeb is an open project, not a standard; only relevant if you deployed it.
agentic.nlweb-error.fix: Check the NLWeb service logs, or remove the route if it is not in use.

agentic.ai-preferences-missing.title: No AI usage preferences in robots.txt
agentic.ai-preferences-missing.why: robots.txt controls crawling, not use. Content-Signal lines (published by Cloudflare) and the IETF aipref Content-Usage vocabulary (in draft) let you say separately whether content may be used for search, AI answers and training. Adoption by AI companies is still limited.
agentic.ai-preferences-missing.fix: Add a line such as "Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no" under User-agent: * to state your preference.

agentic.ai-preferences-invalid.title: AI preference lines are malformed
agentic.ai-preferences-invalid.why: A preference that does not follow the vocabulary (unknown keys, values other than yes/no) will be ignored by any parser that does read it.
agentic.ai-preferences-invalid.fix: Use the documented keys and values, e.g. "Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no".

agentic.ai-preferences-conflict.title: AI preferences contradict robots.txt rules
agentic.ai-preferences-conflict.why: Saying search=yes or ai-input=yes while blocking the bots that do that work sends opposite instructions; the block wins, and the stated preference is meaningless.
agentic.ai-preferences-conflict.fix: Make the two agree: allow the search and user bots, or change the preference to match your rules.

agentic.ai-txt-only.title: AI restrictions only in ai.txt
agentic.ai-txt-only.why: ai.txt (a Spawning proposal) is read by few AI crawlers. If it carries restrictions that robots.txt does not, the major crawlers will not see them.
agentic.ai-txt-only.fix: Put the rules that matter in robots.txt (per-bot groups) and, for use preferences, a Content-Signal line.

agentic.ai-plugin-legacy.title: Legacy ChatGPT plugin manifest still published
agentic.ai-plugin-legacy.why: ChatGPT plugins were retired in 2024. The ai-plugin.json manifest is no longer read by ChatGPT; it may point at an API that has also gone stale.
agentic.ai-plugin-legacy.fix: Remove /.well-known/ai-plugin.json, or replace it with an OpenAPI file in an api-catalog and, if relevant, an MCP server.

agentic.feed-missing.title: Articles but no RSS or Atom feed
agentic.feed-missing.why: Feeds are the oldest agent interface on the web: aggregators, readers and many AI tools use them to learn what is new without recrawling the site.
agentic.feed-missing.fix: Publish an RSS or Atom feed of your articles and link it with <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml"> in the page head.

agentic.feed-invalid.title: Feed has no items
agentic.feed-invalid.why: An advertised feed that is empty tells readers and agents nothing has been published.
agentic.feed-invalid.fix: Make the feed list recent articles (title, link, date, summary).

agentic.wellknown-wrong-type.title: Discovery documents served with the wrong content type
agentic.wellknown-wrong-type.why: Clients may refuse JSON metadata served as text/html or text/plain, and some frameworks check the media type strictly.
agentic.wellknown-wrong-type.fix: Serve these files as application/json (api-catalog as application/linkset+json).

agentic.wellknown-no-cors.title: Discovery documents not readable from browsers
agentic.wellknown-no-cors.why: Browser-based agents and MCP clients fetch metadata from other origins. Without Access-Control-Allow-Origin the browser blocks the response.
agentic.wellknown-no-cors.fix: Send "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *" on public discovery documents (they contain no secrets).

agentic.wellknown-redirect-offsite.title: Discovery documents redirect to another host
agentic.wellknown-redirect-offsite.why: Some clients do not follow redirects for /.well-known resources, and OAuth metadata fetched from another host fails the issuer check.
agentic.wellknown-redirect-offsite.fix: Serve the document directly from this origin.

agentic.discovery-blocked-by-robots.title: robots.txt blocks AI bots from llms.txt or /.well-known
agentic.discovery-blocked-by-robots.why: Publishing discovery files and then disallowing them for AI bots means compliant agents will not read them.
agentic.discovery-blocked-by-robots.fix: Allow /llms.txt and /.well-known/ for AI bots (add "Allow: /.well-known/" and "Allow: /llms.txt").

agentic-commerce.product-no-identifier.title: Product without a stable identifier
agentic-commerce.product-no-identifier.why: Shopping agents match products across sites by GTIN, MPN or SKU. Without one they cannot be sure your product is the one the user wants, and fall back to retailers that provide it.
agentic-commerce.product-no-identifier.fix: Add gtin (or gtin13/gtin12), mpn and sku to the Product JSON-LD.

agentic-commerce.offer-incomplete.title: Product offer missing price, currency or availability
agentic-commerce.offer-incomplete.why: An agent cannot quote or buy what it cannot price. price, priceCurrency and availability are the minimum for any shopping answer.
agentic-commerce.offer-incomplete.fix: Give each Offer price, priceCurrency (ISO 4217), availability (schema.org/InStock…) and url.

agentic-commerce.no-policies.title: Offers without shipping or returns information
agentic-commerce.no-policies.why: Shopping assistants compare total cost and return terms. Shipping details and a return policy in the markup let them answer “does it ship to me, can I return it” from your data.
agentic-commerce.no-policies.fix: Add shippingDetails and hasMerchantReturnPolicy to offers, or a MerchantReturnPolicy on the Organization.

agentic-commerce.unstable-product-url.title: Product reachable only through a parameterised URL
agentic-commerce.unstable-product-url.why: Agents store and revisit product URLs. Session IDs, tracking parameters or variant-only query strings without a clean canonical break those links.
agentic-commerce.unstable-product-url.fix: Give each product a clean canonical URL and use it as the Offer url and Product url.

agentic-commerce.no-checkout-protocol.title: Shop with no agent checkout protocol
agentic-commerce.no-checkout-protocol.why: Agent checkout protocols are new: the Agentic Commerce Protocol (OpenAI and Stripe), the Universal Commerce Protocol (Google and partners) and x402 payments. Early adopters can be bought from inside an assistant; most shops have none yet, and platform integrations (Shopify, Stripe, Google Merchant Center) are the usual route in.
agentic-commerce.no-checkout-protocol.fix: Check whether your commerce platform or payment provider offers ACP or UCP support, and keep product data (identifiers, prices, availability) complete so you are ready when it does.

agentic-commerce.ucp-invalid.title: UCP business profile is invalid
agentic-commerce.ucp-invalid.why: Agents read /.well-known/ucp to learn which commerce capabilities you support. An invalid profile stops them at the first step.
agentic-commerce.ucp-invalid.fix: Fix the listed errors against the current UCP specification.

agentic-commerce.x402-invalid.title: x402 payment endpoint is misconfigured
agentic-commerce.x402-invalid.why: x402 lets an agent pay for a resource after an HTTP 402 response describing the payment. If the advertised resource does not answer 402, or the payment requirements are malformed, agents cannot pay.
agentic-commerce.x402-invalid.fix: Return 402 with a JSON body containing x402Version and an accepts list (scheme, network, amount, payTo, asset) for unpaid requests.

agentic-commerce.products-without-schema.title: Shop pages without Product markup
agentic-commerce.products-without-schema.why: Shopping agents and AI answers read prices and availability from Product schema. Product pages without it must be scraped, which is error-prone.
agentic-commerce.products-without-schema.fix: Add Product JSON-LD with name, image, identifiers and offers to every product page (most shop platforms and SEO plugins can).

agentic.link-header-missing.title: Discovery documents not advertised in a Link header
agentic.link-header-missing.why: RFC 8288 Link headers let an agent learn where your API catalog, service docs or agent card live from a single request to the home page, without guessing well-known paths. RFC 9727 recommends rel="api-catalog" for exactly this.
agentic.link-header-missing.fix: Add a Link header to the home page response for each discovery document, e.g. Link: </.well-known/api-catalog>; rel="api-catalog", </docs/api>; rel="service-doc".

agentic.dns-aid-missing.title: Agent endpoints not published in DNS (DNS-AID)
agentic.dns-aid-missing.why: DNS for AI Discovery is an IETF draft that lets agents find a domain's MCP or A2A endpoints through SVCB records (for example _mcp._agents.example.com), before any HTTP request. Early, but cheap to add once you publish an agent.
agentic.dns-aid-missing.fix: Add a ServiceMode SVCB (or HTTPS) record at _mcp._agents.<your domain> and/or _a2a._agents.<your domain> pointing at the endpoint host, with alpn and port parameters. Sign the zone with DNSSEC.

agentic.auth-md-missing.title: No auth.md telling agents how to sign up
agentic.auth-md-missing.why: auth.md is a proposed plain-language file at the site root that tells AI agents how to register and authenticate with your API. It complements OAuth metadata, which says where the endpoints are but not the steps or policies. A proposal, not a standard.
agentic.auth-md-missing.fix: Serve /auth.md (text/markdown) describing how an agent gets credentials: the registration URL, supported grant types, scopes and any human approval step. Link it from your protected resource metadata.

agentic.agent-skills-invalid.title: Agent skills index is invalid
agentic.agent-skills-invalid.why: An agent skills index (/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json, a Cloudflare-led proposal) lists skills agents can download and use with your service. Entries without a name, description, URL or digest are skipped or cannot be verified.
agentic.agent-skills-invalid.fix: Give each entry a name, description, url and sha256 digest of the skill file, and a $schema field for the index version.

agentic-commerce.acp-invalid.title: ACP discovery file is invalid
agentic-commerce.acp-invalid.why: Agents that support the Agentic Commerce Protocol read /.well-known/acp.json to learn the protocol version and where your checkout API lives. Missing fields stop them before checkout.
agentic-commerce.acp-invalid.fix: Include protocol.name "acp", protocol.version, an https api_base_url and capabilities.services, following the current ACP specification.

fix.title: Let AI search and assistant crawlers read the site
steps: The rules below keep your training opt-out but allow AI search and assistant crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot…), which decide whether answers can cite you.
Replace robots.txt with the content below (existing rules are kept; only AI crawler groups change).
Create `robots.txt` with the content below.
Put it in the folder your web server or framework serves at the root (often `public/` or `static/`).
Deploy.
Open http://127.0.0.1:38107/robots.txt in a browser and confirm it returns the file with status 200.

## Rules
- Find the real files in this project first; the paths above are the usual locations for this stack and may differ.
- Change only what this fix needs. Keep existing behaviour, rules and content unless a step says otherwise.
- Do not invent facts (addresses, prices, clients, dates). Leave a clear TODO where a fact is missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] robots.txt allows OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User and PerplexityBot on public pages

fix.title: Stop the firewall or CDN blocking AI crawlers
steps: robots.txt is not the problem here: the AI crawler got a challenge or error page while a browser got the real page.
Cloudflare: Security → Bots: keep "Allow verified bots" on (Super Bot Fight Mode → Verified bots: Allow).
Cloudflare: AI Crawl Control → set the AI search and assistant crawlers you want to Allow (blocking there overrides robots.txt).
Cloudflare: Security → WAF → Custom rules → create a rule with the expression below and action **Skip** (skip Super Bot Fight Mode, managed rules and rate limiting), placed first.
Vercel: Project → Firewall → turn off Attack Challenge Mode when you are not under attack (it challenges crawlers too).
Vercel: Firewall → Bot Management: keep verified bots allowed; if you added a custom rule that challenges or denies by user agent, add an exception for verified AI bots above it.
Akamai: Bot Manager → Bot Categories → set the AI crawler / AI search categories to Allow or Monitor, not Deny or Tarpit; keep the "verified" (Akamai-categorised) bots allowed.
Other WAFs (Sucuri, Wordfence, Imperva, DataDome, server rules): allow the AI crawlers by verified IP range, not by user agent alone — user agents are easy to fake.

IP ranges are published by OpenAI (https://openai.com/gptbot.json, https://openai.com/searchbot.json, https://openai.com/chatgpt-user.json) and Perplexity (https://www.perplexity.ai/perplexitybot.json); Anthropic and Google publish verification guidance in their crawler docs.
Re-test with `avc audit --only ai-crawlers.user-fetchers-blocked` — it fetches the home page as each AI crawler.
