snippet.code:
# Harbourline

> Independent dental practice with clinics in Bristol, Bath and Leeds. Check-ups, hygiene, implants, aligners and same-day emergency appointments.

## Pages

- [Careers in Dentistry at Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/careers): Work at Harbourline: current vacancies for dental nurses, receptionists and hygienists, plus training, pay and what it is like to work here.
- [Paying for Dental Treatment and Finance](http://127.0.0.1:38107/finance): Ways to pay at Harbourline: card payments, deposits for laboratory work, interest-free finance over twelve months and itemised receipts for insurers.
- [About Harbourline Dental Studio: Our Story](http://127.0.0.1:38107/about): How Harbourline Dental Studio started in 2012, how we work, and what patients can expect from our dentists and staff.
- [Referrals for Dentists: Implants and Aligners](http://127.0.0.1:38107/referrals): Information for referring dentists: how to refer patients for implants, clear aligners or gum treatment, what we send back and typical waiting times.
- [Developer Information and Booking API](http://127.0.0.1:38107/developers): How software and AI agents can find Harbourline Dental Studio’s booking API, its machine-readable catalogue and the agent discovery files we publish.
- [Frequently Asked Questions – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/faq): Answers to common questions about new patient appointments, fees, emergency care, children’s check-ups, parking and paying for treatment.
- [Dental Treatment Prices and Fees – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/pricing): Current fees for check-ups, hygiene, fillings, crowns, implants, whitening and aligners at Harbourline Dental Studio clinics.
- [Book a Dental Appointment Online](http://127.0.0.1:38107/book): Request a check-up, hygiene visit or consultation at our Bristol, Bath or Leeds clinic. We confirm every request by phone or email.
- [Contact Harbourline Dental Studio – Phone and Email](http://127.0.0.1:38107/contact): Telephone numbers, email and addresses for Harbourline clinics in Bristol, Bath and Leeds, plus an enquiry form for non-urgent questions.
- [Information for New Patients – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/new-patients): Joining Harbourline: what your first appointment involves, what it costs, what to bring and how to register online before you arrive.
- [A Patient Guide to Clear Aligner Treatment](http://127.0.0.1:38107/invisalign-guide): Our patient guide to clear aligners: suitability, wearing time, attachments, cost in pounds and retainers after treatment.
- [Patient Stories – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/patient-stories): Real treatment journeys from Harbourline patients, in their own words: implants, aligners, nervous patients and children’s care.
- [Summer Whitening Offer – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/whitening-offer): Our summer whitening offer has moved to the teeth whitening page.

## Blog

- [Dental Advice and Practice News – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog): Practical advice on looking after your teeth and gums from the Harbourline team, plus news from our Bristol, Bath and Leeds clinics.
- [Oral health Articles – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/category/oral-health): Harbourline articles on brushing, cleaning between teeth, diet and the common problems our dentists and hygienists see at check-ups.
- [Practice news Articles – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/category/news): News from Harbourline Dental Studio clinics in Bristol, Bath and Leeds: new services, opening hours, events and building improvements.
- [Cosmetic dentistry Articles – Harbourline Dental Studio](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/category/cosmetic): Harbourline articles on teeth whitening, clear aligners, veneers and planning cosmetic dental treatment, with realistic costs and results.
- [Wisdom Teeth: When Do They Need Removing?](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/wisdom-teeth): Most wisdom teeth never need removing. The signs that one is causing problems, how removal works and how long recovery takes.
- [How to Choose a Toothpaste That Works](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/choosing-a-toothpaste): What to look for on a toothpaste label: fluoride strength, sensitivity ingredients, whitening claims and what you can ignore.
- [How Often Should You Have a Dental Check-Up?](http://127.0.0.1:38107/blog/dental-checkups-how-often): Six months is not the rule for everyone. How dentists decide your recall interval, from three months to two years.

Choosing a toothpaste

By Tom Ellis, Dental therapist · Published 4 May 2026 · Updated 18 May 2026

Key points from this article

  • Fluoride first: The single most important ingredient is fluoride.
  • For sensitive teeth: Toothpastes containing potassium nitrate, stannous fluoride or arginine reduce sensitivity when used twice a day for a few weeks.
  • Whitening and tartar control: Whitening pastes remove surface stain with mild abrasives or enzymes; they do not change the natural shade of the teeth.
  • What you can ignore: Flavour, colour and stripes make no difference to how well a toothpaste works.
  • A simple rule: If it contains the right amount of fluoride and you are happy to use it twice a day, it is a good toothpaste.

Fluoride first

The single most important ingredient is fluoride. Look for 1,350 to 1,500 parts per million on the label for adults and children over seven. Fluoride-free toothpastes do not protect against decay and are not recommended by UK dental guidance.

Children under three need at least 1,000 ppm, used as a smear on the brush.

For sensitive teeth

Toothpastes containing potassium nitrate, stannous fluoride or arginine reduce sensitivity when used twice a day for a few weeks. Keep using them after the sensitivity settles, or it tends to return.

Whitening and tartar control

Whitening pastes remove surface stain with mild abrasives or enzymes; they do not change the natural shade of the teeth. Tartar control pastes slow the build-up of new tartar but cannot remove what is already there.

What you can ignore

Flavour, colour and stripes make no difference to how well a toothpaste works. Natural or herbal labels do not mean safer, and many such products lack fluoride. Price is no guide to effectiveness: supermarket own-brand fluoride pastes work as well as premium ones.

A simple rule

If it contains the right amount of fluoride and you are happy to use it twice a day, it is a good toothpaste. If you have particular problems, such as sensitivity or a high decay rate, ask your dentist or hygienist for a recommendation at your next visit.

If you have questions about anything in this article, our team can help at your next appointment. Read about general dentistry at Harbourline or book a visit online.

About the author. Tom Ellis is a dental therapist at Harbourline Dental Studio. Tom qualified as a dental hygienist and therapist from the University of Portsmouth in 2019 and joined Harbourline in 2022.
